files.content:
# Todo List Application - Functional Requirements

## Executive Summary

This document defines the complete functional requirements for the TodoList application, a minimal yet comprehensive task management system designed for individual and collaborative use. The application enables users to create, manage, and track personal Todo items with secure authentication and role-based access control. The system prioritizes simplicity and ease of use while maintaining enterprise-grade security and performance standards.

## Document Information

- **Document Type**: Functional Requirements Specification
- **Service Prefix**: todoApp
- **Target Implementation**: TypeScript + NestJS + Prisma Backend
- **User Language**: English (US)
- **Documentation Focus**: Business Requirements and User Operations
- **Implementation Priority**: Minimal core functionality with extensible architecture

## 1. Core Todo Operations

### 1.1 Todo Item Creation

**WHEN a user clicks "Create Todo" or accesses the Todo creation interface, THE system SHALL enable the user to add a new Todo item with title and optional description through an intuitive form interface.**

**WHEN a user submits a new Todo item, THE system SHALL validate and store the following data with immediate feedback:**
- Todo title (required, 1-255 characters, trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace)
- Todo description (optional, 0-1000 characters)
- Created timestamp (auto-generated with timezone awareness)
- User association (linked to authenticated user via secure session)
- Status indicator (default: "active")
- Unique Todo identifier for tracking and reference

**WHEN a user attempts to create a Todo without a title, THE system SHALL display clear error message "Todo title is required" in red text below the title field and prevent form submission until corrected.**

**IF a user's Todo count exceeds 1,000 items, THE system SHALL display warning message "Todo limit reached (1,000 items maximum)" and provide options to archive or delete completed items before allowing new creation.**

**WHERE users have administrative privileges, THE system SHALL enable them to create Todo items on behalf of other users through a dropdown selection interface that displays all active user accounts with their email addresses and usernames.**

**WHEN creating a Todo item, THE system SHALL provide real-time character counters for title (255 max) and description (1000 max) fields to help users stay within limits.**

**IF a user attempts to create a duplicate Todo title within their active items, THE system SHALL display warning "You already have a Todo item with this title. Consider making it more specific or check if this is a duplicate."**

### 1.2 Todo Item Retrieval

**THE user SHALL be able to view all their Todo items in a clean, organized list format, with active items displayed above completed items, both sorted by creation date (newest first).**

**WHEN a user requests to view Todo items, THE system SHALL display with responsive layout:**
- Todo title (prominent, bold text)
- Todo description (if provided, in smaller text below title)
- Creation date and time (formatted as "Created on [Date] at [Time]")
- Status indicator (color-coded: blue for active, green for completed)
- Optional completion date (only shown for completed items)
- Edit and delete action buttons (visible on hover or click)
- Visual progress indicator showing completion percentage

**THE user SHALL be able to filter their Todo items using a status filter dropdown with options: "All Todo Items", "Active Only", "Completed Only" with immediate list updates upon selection.**

**THE user SHALL be able to search their Todo items using a search bar that filters results in real-time by title or description text, with search term highlighted in matching results.**

**WHERE users have administrative privileges, THE system SHALL enable them to view Todo items from all users through a comprehensive dashboard with user filter dropdown and combined status filtering options.**

**WHEN displaying Todo lists, THE system SHALL implement pagination for users with more than 50 items, showing 10 items per page with navigation controls.**

**IF a user has no Todo items, THE system SHALL display encouraging message "You don't have any Todo items yet. Click 'Create Todo' to get started!" with a prominent call-to-action button.**

### 1.3 Todo Item Editing

**WHEN a user clicks "Edit" on a Todo item, THE system SHALL display an inline editing interface or modal dialog allowing modification of title and description with the original content pre-populated.**

**IF a user modifies a Todo item, THE system SHALL update the modified timestamp and save changes immediately upon user clicking "Save" or pressing Enter, providing visual confirmation of successful save.**

**THE user SHALL be able to edit their own Todo items at any time, including completed items, with the system maintaining all edit history for audit purposes.**

**WHERE users have administrative privileges, THE system SHALL enable them to edit any user's Todo items through an administrative interface that clearly shows which user's item is being modified.**

**IF a completed Todo item is being edited, THE system SHALL provide option to change status back to active with clear explanation that this will remove the completion date.**

**WHEN editing a Todo item, THE system SHALL validate changes against the same rules as creation, preventing empty titles or overly long content, and displaying validation errors inline.**

### 1.4 Todo Item Completion

**WHEN a user clicks "Mark Complete" on an active Todo item, THE system SHALL change the status to "completed", record completion timestamp with timezone, and visually update the item with strikethrough formatting and completion indicator.**

**WHEN a user clicks "Mark Incomplete" on a completed Todo item, THE system SHALL change the status to "active", remove completion timestamp, and restore normal formatting without completion indicators.**

**THE completed Todo items SHALL remain visible in the user's list with distinct visual styling (gray text, strikethrough, checkmark icon) but appear below all active items in chronological order.**

**THE user SHALL be able to toggle Todo item status between complete and incomplete as needed, with each status change being logged with timestamp and user action for audit purposes.**

**WHERE users have administrative privileges, THE system SHALL enable them to change completion status of any user's Todo items through the administrative interface with full audit logging.**

**WHEN marking a Todo complete, THE system SHALL provide immediate visual feedback and optional brief celebration animation or message like "Great job! Todo marked as completed."**

### 1.5 Todo Item Deletion

**WHEN a user clicks "Delete" on a Todo item, THE system SHALL display confirmation dialog with the Todo title and message "Are you sure you want to delete this Todo item? This action cannot be undone."**

**IF user confirms deletion, THE system SHALL permanently remove the Todo item from the database, provide visual confirmation "Todo item deleted successfully", and update the displayed list immediately.**

**IF user cancels deletion, THE system SHALL keep the Todo item unchanged, close the confirmation dialog, and return the user to the normal list view.**

**THE user SHALL be able to delete their own Todo items at any time, with completed items remaining available for deletion as long as the user's account is active.**

**WHERE users have administrative privileges, THE system SHALL enable them to delete any user's Todo items through the administrative interface with proper authorization checks and audit logging.**

**IF a Todo item has been completed for more than 30 days, THE system SHALL display additional warning message "This Todo item was completed over 30 days ago. Are you sure you want to delete it? Consider archiving instead."**

**WHEN deleting a Todo item, THE system SHALL provide option to "Archive" instead of "Delete" for completed items, moving them to an archived section accessible via navigation menu.**

## 2. User Management Functions

### 2.1 User Registration

**WHEN a new user accesses the application for the first time, THE system SHALL provide a clean registration form with email, password, and confirm password fields along with clear instructions and validation feedback.**

**WHEN user submits registration form, THE system SHALL validate the following requirements with specific error messages:**
- Email format is valid (user@domain.com format) and not already registered
- Password meets security requirements (minimum 8 characters, contains uppercase, lowercase, and numbers)
- Password and confirm password match exactly with real-time validation
- All required fields are completed

**IF validation fails, THE system SHALL display specific error messages next to each problematic field, prevent form submission, and provide clear guidance on how to fix each issue.**

**IF validation succeeds, THE system SHALL create new user account with email verification requirement and redirect to confirmation page explaining next steps.**

**THE system SHALL send verification email to user within 5 minutes with subject "Verify Your TodoList Account" containing confirmation link that expires after 24 hours.**

**IF user doesn't verify email within 7 days, THE system SHALL automatically delete unverified account and display appropriate cleanup messaging to prevent confusion.**

**WHEN user successfully verifies email, THE system SHALL automatically log them in and redirect to Todo list dashboard with welcome message and brief onboarding tips.**

### 2.2 User Authentication

**WHEN user accesses application without valid session, THE system SHALL display login form with email and password fields, "Remember me" checkbox, and "Forgot password" link for account recovery.**

**IF user provides valid credentials, THE system SHALL create authenticated session with secure token management and redirect to Todo list dashboard within 3 seconds.**

**IF user provides invalid credentials, THE system SHALL display error message "Invalid email or password" after 2-second delay and maintain login form without revealing which field was incorrect for security.**

**THE system SHALL implement session timeout after 30 days of inactivity with warning message displayed 5 minutes before timeout.**

**IF session expires, THE system SHALL redirect user to login form and display message "Your session has expired. Please log in again to continue."**

**WHEN user logs in successfully, THE system SHALL display "Welcome back, [username]!" message and redirect to their Todo dashboard showing their existing items.**

**THE system SHALL implement secure password reset functionality that sends reset links to registered email addresses with 1-hour expiration and clear instructions for completion.**

### 2.3 User Profile Management

**WHEN user is authenticated, THE system SHALL display user profile section accessible via navigation menu, showing current email, account creation date, and Todo statistics (total, active, completed counts).**

**WHEN user accesses profile settings, THE system SHALL enable password change functionality with current password verification and new password requirements clearly displayed.**

**IF user changes password, THE system SHALL require current password verification, validate new password meets security requirements, and automatically log out all active sessions for security.**

**THE system SHALL validate new password meets the same security requirements as registration with real-time feedback on password strength and requirements checklist.**

**WHEN user updates profile information, THE system SHALL save changes immediately, display success message "Profile updated successfully", and refresh any displayed user information.**

**THE system SHALL provide option for users to deactivate their account with confirmation dialog explaining consequences and data retention policies.**

### 2.4 User Session Management

**THE system SHALL maintain user session using secure JWT tokens with 15-minute expiration and automatic refresh capabilities for active usage.**

**WHEN user performs actions (create, edit, delete Todo items), THE system SHALL refresh JWT token to extend session and update session activity timestamp.**

**IF user remains inactive for 15 minutes, THE system SHALL require re-authentication for security, displaying countdown timer and option to extend session.**

**WHEN user logs out, THE system SHALL immediately terminate session, clear all stored session data, and redirect to login page with message "You have been logged out successfully."**

**THE system SHALL allow users to have active sessions on multiple devices simultaneously while providing device management capabilities in profile settings.**

**WHEN suspicious activity is detected (rapid failed login attempts, unusual access patterns), THE system SHALL temporarily lock user account and send security notification email.**

## 3. Data Validation Rules

### 3.1 Todo Item Validation

**WHEN creating or editing Todo items, THE system SHALL enforce the following validation rules with immediate feedback:**
- Title: Required, 1-255 characters, no leading/trailing whitespace, must be unique within user's active items
- Description: Optional, 0-1000 characters, supports plain text formatting
- Creation data integrity: Must be associated with valid user session

**IF validation fails, THE system SHALL display specific error message identifying the exact validation issue with helpful guidance for resolution.**

**THE system SHALL prevent creation of duplicate Todo titles within a user's active items by checking against existing titles (case-insensitive comparison).**

**IF user attempts to submit empty title after trimming whitespace, THE system SHALL display error "Todo title cannot be empty. Please enter a descriptive title for your task."**

**IF user attempts to submit title longer than 255 characters, THE system SHALL display error "Todo title must be 255 characters or less. Current length: [X] characters."**

**WHEN validating Todo content, THE system SHALL strip any HTML tags or scripts to prevent XSS attacks and ensure content safety.**

### 3.2 User Account Validation

**WHEN registering or updating user accounts, THE system SHALL enforce comprehensive email validation:**
- Email must be valid format (user@domain.com with proper domain validation)
- Email must be unique across all registered users with real-time availability checking
- Email cannot be changed more than once per 24-hour period
- Email changes require verification via confirmation email

**WHEN setting passwords, THE system SHALL enforce robust password security with strength indicators:**
- Minimum 8 characters length
- Must contain at least one uppercase letter (A-Z)
- Must contain at least one lowercase letter (a-z)
- Must contain at least one number (0-9)
- Cannot contain spaces or common special characters for security
- Password strength meter with visual feedback

**IF password validation fails, THE system SHALL display detailed requirements checklist and prevent account creation/update until all criteria are met.**

**THE system SHALL implement rate limiting for registration attempts (maximum 5 attempts per IP address per hour) to prevent spam and abuse.**

### 3.3 Data Integrity Validation

**THE system SHALL prevent unauthorized access to Todo items by validating user ownership before allowing operations through secure session checks and user ID verification.**

**WHEN administrative users perform actions on other users' Todo items, THE system SHALL log all administrative actions with comprehensive details: user ID, timestamp, action type, target user, and outcome for audit purposes.**

**IF system detects data inconsistency (orphaned Todo items, invalid user references), THE system SHALL automatically attempt data repair with fallback reporting to administrators for manual intervention.**

**THE system SHALL maintain referential integrity between users and their Todo items at all times through database constraints and transaction management.**

**WHEN performing bulk operations, THE system SHALL implement transaction-based processing to ensure data consistency and provide rollback capabilities for failed operations.**

## 4. Business Logic

### 4.1 Todo Status Management Logic

**WHEN a Todo item is marked complete, THE system SHALL automatically execute the following workflow:**
- Set completion timestamp to current date/time with timezone awareness
- Change status from "active" to "completed" in database
- Update item visually to indicate completion (strikethrough text, green checkmark)
- Preserve all original Todo content (title, description, creation date)
- Log status change for audit trail
- Provide optional motivational message or celebration animation

**WHEN a completed Todo item is marked incomplete, THE system SHALL automatically execute the following workflow:**
- Remove completion timestamp from database
- Change status from "completed" to "active"
- Update item visually to indicate active status (normal formatting)
- Restore full edit capabilities and status toggle options
- Log status change for audit trail

**THE system SHALL maintain complete history of status changes for audit purposes, including who made the change, when, and from what status to what status.**

**WHEN Todo items transition between statuses, THE system SHALL provide immediate visual feedback and update all related statistics (completed count, completion percentage).**

### 4.2 User Permission Enforcement Logic

**THE system SHALL enforce comprehensive permission rules with clear separation between regular users and administrative users:**

**For Regular Users:**
- Can only view, create, edit, and delete their own Todo items through secure session validation
- Cannot access other users' Todo items or account information
- Cannot perform administrative functions or access user management features
- Limited to 1,000 Todo items maximum per account
- Can only view their own account statistics and profile information

**For Administrative Users:**
- Can view all Todo items from all users with comprehensive filtering options
- Can create, edit, and delete Todo items for any user through administrative interface
- Can access user account management and system settings
- Can perform bulk operations on multiple users' Todo items
- Can view system-wide statistics and usage reports
- Can manage system configuration and security settings

**THE system SHALL reject all unauthorized access attempts with appropriate error messages, security logging, and optional account lockout for repeated violations.**

**WHEN users attempt unauthorized actions, THE system SHALL display clear error message "You don't have permission to perform this action" without revealing sensitive system information.**

### 4.3 Data Retention and Cleanup Logic

**THE system SHALL implement automated data lifecycle management:**
- Automatically delete Todo items marked complete for more than 365 days unless user opts to keep them
- Maintain active Todo items indefinitely unless manually deleted by user
- If user account is deleted, automatically delete all associated Todo items with proper cleanup verification
- Create weekly automated backups of all Todo data and user account information
- Purge unverified user accounts that remain unactivated after 7 days from registration

**WHEN data cleanup processes run, THE system SHALL send optional email notification to users about items being archived or deleted (configurable in user settings).**

**THE system SHALL provide users with option to manually archive completed Todo items older than 30 days to keep their active list manageable.**

### 4.4 Search and Filter Logic

**WHEN user performs Todo search, THE system SHALL search within user's own Todo items only (unless administrative privileges are active) using optimized search algorithms.**

**THE search SHALL match text in both Todo titles and descriptions using case-insensitive partial matching with highlighting of matching terms.**

**IF search returns no results, THE system SHALL display helpful message "No Todo items found matching '[search term]'. Try different keywords or check your spelling."**

**WHEN user applies status filter, THE system SHALL immediately update Todo list display to show only items matching selected status with smooth transitions.**

**THE system SHALL allow combination of search text and status filters simultaneously, with real-time results updating as user types or changes filters.**

**WHEN performing searches, THE system SHALL implement pagination for results exceeding 50 items to maintain performance and usability.**

## 5. Feature Specifications

### 5.1 Minimal Core Features

**THE system SHALL implement the following essential features with intuitive user experience:**

**Todo Management:**
- Create new Todo items with title and optional description through clean, responsive form interface
- View personal Todo list with all active and completed items organized by status and date
- Edit existing Todo items (title and description) with inline editing or modal interface
- Mark Todo items as complete or incomplete with visual feedback and status confirmation
- Delete Todo items with confirmation dialog to prevent accidental deletions
- Search Todo items by text content with real-time filtering and result highlighting
- Filter Todo items by status (all, active, completed) with immediate list updates
- Sort Todo items by creation date, completion date, or title (alphabetical)

**User Authentication:**
- User registration with email and secure password with verification workflow
- User login with email and password with session management
- User logout with complete session termination and security cleanup
- Password change functionality with current password verification
- Session management with automatic timeout and security measures
- Account verification via email with clear instructions and support

**User Interface Features:**
- Responsive design that works seamlessly on desktop, tablet, and mobile devices
- Clean, intuitive interface optimized for easy Todo management
- Visual distinction between active (blue indicators) and completed (green checkmarks) Todo items
- Confirmation dialogs for destructive actions (deletions) with clear consequences
- Real-time updates for all user actions with immediate visual feedback
- Loading indicators for all operations to inform users of system status
- Error messages that are helpful and non-technical for end users

### 5.2 Administrative Features

**WHERE users have administrative privileges, THE system SHALL provide comprehensive management capabilities:**

**User Management:**
- View comprehensive list of all registered users with search and filtering capabilities
- Access any user's Todo items with full edit capabilities and audit logging
- Delete user accounts and all associated Todo items with proper confirmation and cleanup
- Reset user passwords when necessary with secure notification process
- View detailed user activity logs and session information for security monitoring
- Export user data and Todo information in various formats (CSV, JSON) for reporting

**System Administration:**
- Access system-wide Todo statistics and usage metrics with real-time dashboards
- Perform bulk operations on multiple users' Todo items with progress tracking
- Export comprehensive Todo data for reporting and analysis purposes
- Monitor system performance and error logs with alerting capabilities
- Manage system settings and configuration options through administrative interface
- Set user limits, system parameters, and security policies

**Reporting and Analytics:**
- Generate usage reports showing user activity, Todo completion rates, and system metrics
- Monitor performance indicators and system health with automated alerts
- Track security events and potential threats with incident reporting
- Analyze user behavior patterns to improve system functionality

### 5.3 Error Handling and User Experience

**THE system SHALL implement comprehensive error handling with user-friendly communication:**

**For User Errors:**
- Clear, specific error messages that help users understand and resolve issues without technical jargon
- Form validation that prevents submission of invalid data with immediate feedback
- Graceful handling of network connectivity issues with automatic retry mechanisms
- User guidance for common issues with troubleshooting suggestions
- Recovery options for failed operations with clear next steps

**For System Errors:**
- Automatic logging of all errors with timestamp, user context, and error details for debugging
- User-friendly error messages that don't expose system internals or security vulnerabilities
- Fallback mechanisms for critical system failures with graceful degradation
- Notification to administrators for critical system issues with escalation procedures
- Automatic recovery attempts for temporary failures with exponential backoff

**THE system SHALL provide comprehensive user guidance and support:**
- Contextual help text for form fields and actions with examples and explanations
- Onboarding instructions for new users with step-by-step guidance
- Tooltips explaining Todo status, available actions, and system features
- Confirmation messages for successful operations with next-step suggestions
- FAQ section addressing common questions and troubleshooting

### 5.4 Performance and Scalability Requirements

**THE system SHALL meet stringent performance requirements with monitoring and optimization:**

**Response Time Expectations:**
- Todo list loading: Under 2 seconds for up to 500 items, with pagination for larger lists
- Todo creation, editing, and deletion: Under 1 second response time with immediate visual feedback
- User authentication (login/logout): Under 3 seconds including session establishment
- Search operations: Under 1 second for typical query volumes with real-time results
- Page transitions and navigation: Under 500 milliseconds for smooth user experience

**System Capacity:**
- Support up to 10,000 registered users simultaneously with load balancing
- Handle up to 1,000 Todo items per user with efficient database indexing
- Process up to 1,000 Todo operations per minute during peak usage periods
- Maintain performance under normal load conditions with monitoring and alerting
- Handle concurrent user sessions with proper session management and cleanup

**Data Management:**
- Automatic indexing for fast Todo search and filtering across all user data
- Efficient database queries optimized for scalability and minimal resource usage
- Real-time synchronization of Todo changes across user sessions without conflicts
- Optimized data structures for minimal database load and maximum query performance
- Automated database maintenance and performance optimization routines

## 6. Integration and External Requirements

### 6.1 Email Integration

**THE system SHALL integrate with reliable email service for critical user communications:**
- User registration verification emails with clear instructions and support links
- Password reset emails with secure temporary links and usage guidelines
- Administrative notifications for critical system events and security alerts
- Optional notifications for Todo reminders and system updates

**Email templates SHALL be professional and user-friendly with:**
- Consistent branding and application identity throughout all communications
- Clear, actionable instructions with examples and support contact information
- Professional formatting optimized for readability across different email clients
- Simple language that doesn't require technical knowledge to understand
- Proper sender identification and contact information for user support

**Email delivery SHALL implement:**
- Retry mechanisms for temporary delivery failures with exponential backoff
- Delivery confirmation and bounce handling for invalid email addresses
- Spam prevention measures including proper authentication and content validation
- Unsubscribe mechanisms for non-essential notifications while maintaining critical communications

### 6.2 Security Integration

**THE system SHALL implement comprehensive security best practices:**
- HTTPS enforcement for all user interactions with automatic redirect from HTTP
- Password hashing using industry-standard algorithms (bcrypt with appropriate salt rounds)
- Input sanitization to prevent injection attacks and XSS vulnerabilities
- Rate limiting to prevent abuse and spam with configurable thresholds
- Secure session management with proper token handling and expiration

**The system SHALL implement security monitoring and logging:**
- Failed login attempt tracking with account lockout after multiple failures
- Password change activity logging with timestamp and IP address tracking
- Administrative user actions logging with comprehensive details for audit
- Data access monitoring for unauthorized access attempts with immediate alerting
- Security event correlation and threat detection with automated response

**Security incident response SHALL include:**
- Automated security alerting for suspicious activities and potential breaches
- Account lockdown procedures for compromised accounts with user notification
- Data breach notification protocols with proper authorities and affected users
- Security audit trails with comprehensive logging for forensic analysis
- Regular security assessments and vulnerability scanning with remediation tracking

## 7. Quality Assurance Requirements

### 7.1 Testing Requirements

**THE system SHALL pass comprehensive testing across all functional areas:**
- Unit testing for all Todo and user management functions with minimum 90% code coverage
- Integration testing for authentication and authorization flows with real-world scenarios
- Performance testing to validate response time requirements under various load conditions
- Security testing to verify protection against common web application vulnerabilities
- User acceptance testing to ensure business requirements are met with real user feedback
- Cross-browser compatibility testing for major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
- Mobile responsiveness testing across different device sizes and orientations

**Testing documentation SHALL include:**
- Test case specifications with expected outcomes and test data
- Automated test suite with continuous integration and deployment
- Manual testing procedures for user experience validation
- Performance benchmark results and scalability validation reports
- Security assessment reports with vulnerability remediation documentation

### 7.2 Monitoring and Maintenance

**THE system SHALL implement comprehensive monitoring capabilities:**
- Real-time performance monitoring with alerting for response time degradation
- Error tracking and automated reporting with trend analysis and root cause identification
- User activity analytics and usage reporting with engagement metrics
- Database performance monitoring with query optimization alerts
- System resource monitoring with capacity planning and scaling recommendations

**Maintenance capabilities SHALL include:**
- Automated backup and recovery procedures with tested restoration processes
- Database maintenance and optimization routines with performance tuning
- Log rotation and archival systems with appropriate retention policies
- System health checks and status reporting with proactive issue detection
- Update and patch management with rollback capabilities and testing procedures

**Documentation and support SHALL provide:**
- Comprehensive system documentation for administrators and developers
- User manuals and help documentation with troubleshooting guides
- API documentation for any external integrations or third-party services
- Training materials for administrative users and system operators
- Incident response procedures with escalation paths and communication protocols

## 8. Success Criteria

**THE application SHALL be considered successful when all following criteria are met:**
- All core Todo operations function correctly (create, read, update, delete, complete/incomplete) with user-friendly interfaces and appropriate feedback
- User authentication and authorization work reliably for both regular and administrative user roles with proper security measures
- Data validation prevents invalid inputs and provides helpful, actionable error messages that guide users to resolution
- Performance requirements are consistently met under normal usage conditions with monitoring and optimization
- System security protects against common web application vulnerabilities with proper implementation and testing
- User interface is intuitive and requires no programming knowledge to operate effectively
- Administrative functions provide comprehensive system management and oversight capabilities
- System maintains data integrity and consistency across all operations and user interactions
- Email integration functions reliably for user communications and system notifications
- Documentation and support materials enable successful system deployment and operation

**Performance benchmarks SHALL be validated through:**
- Load testing with 1,000 concurrent users performing typical Todo operations
- Stress testing with peak usage scenarios and resource exhaustion testing
- Security testing with penetration testing and vulnerability assessments
- Usability testing with real users who have no technical background
- Compatibility testing across different browsers, devices, and operating systems

## 9. Future Considerations

**While implementing the minimal required functionality, the system SHALL be designed with extensibility in mind to support future enhancements such as:**

**Enhanced Todo Management:**
- Todo item categories and tagging with color-coding and organization
- Due date tracking with reminders and deadline notifications
- Priority levels (high, medium, low) with visual indicators and sorting options
- Todo item attachments and file uploads with secure storage
- Subtasks and task dependencies with completion tracking

**Collaboration Features:**
- Collaborative Todo items shared between users with permission controls
- Team workspaces with shared Todo lists and group management
- Comments and discussion on Todo items with activity feeds
- Real-time collaborative editing with conflict resolution
- Task assignments and delegation between team members

**Advanced Features:**
- Mobile application development for iOS and Android platforms
- Advanced reporting and analytics with custom dashboards
- Integration with external calendar systems and productivity tools
- Automated task creation from email or other communication channels
- Voice commands and natural language task creation

**Enterprise Features:**
- Single sign-on (SSO) integration with enterprise identity providers
- Advanced audit trails and compliance reporting
- Custom user roles and permissions beyond basic user/admin
- API access for third-party integrations and automation
- White-label deployment options for organizational branding

This comprehensive functional requirements specification ensures that the TodoList application provides essential task management capabilities while maintaining security, performance, and usability standards suitable for both individual users and organizational deployment. The specifications prioritize simplicity and ease of use while providing a robust foundation for future enhancement and scaling.

# Todo List Application - Requirements Analysis Report

## Executive Summary

This requirements analysis report defines the comprehensive business and technical specifications for a minimal yet robust Todo list application designed for individual productivity and task management. The application provides essential Todo management functionality through secure user authentication, Todo CRUD operations, and administrative oversight capabilities.

The Todo application serves both individual users who need personal task management and administrators who require system oversight and user management capabilities. The system emphasizes simplicity, security, and reliable functionality while maintaining enterprise-grade data protection and user privacy standards.

## Service Overview and Business Case

### Problem Statement and Solution

Modern professionals struggle with effective task organization, leading to decreased productivity and increased stress. The Todo list application addresses this fundamental need by providing a straightforward, reliable tool for managing personal and professional tasks through an intuitive interface that promotes productivity without overwhelming complexity.

### Target Users and Value Proposition

**Primary Users: Individual Professionals**
- Knowledge workers, freelancers, students, and busy professionals
- Users seeking quick task entry and completion tracking
- Individuals preferring simple, distraction-free interfaces
- Target audience requiring reliable task management without steep learning curves

**Secondary Users: Administrative Managers**
- Team leaders and project managers requiring oversight capabilities
- Administrative staff needing system management features
- Users responsible for user account management and system oversight

### Core Value Proposition

**For Individual Users:**
- **Mental Clarity**: Clean interface reduces decision fatigue and helps users focus on task completion
- **Quick Task Management**: Rapid task addition, editing, and completion without complex navigation
- **Progress Tracking**: Visual feedback on task completion provides motivation and satisfaction
- **Reliable Access**: Consistent availability ensures users never lose track of important tasks

**For Administrative Users:**
- **System Oversight**: Comprehensive view of user activity and system health
- **User Management**: Simple tools for managing user accounts and permissions
- **Data Integrity**: Reliable backup and management capabilities ensure no user data loss

## User Actors and Authentication Requirements

### User Actor Definitions

#### Regular User (user)
**Business Role**: Individual task management service user who creates and manages personal Todo lists for productivity and organization.

**Responsibilities and Capabilities:**
- Create, edit, delete, and mark complete personal Todo items
- Organize Todos through categorization and priority assignment
- Manage personal account settings and preferences
- View and search through their own Todo history and statistics
- Export or backup their personal Todo data
- Manage personal session and security settings

**Data Scope and Ownership:**
- Complete ownership and control over their own Todo items
- Can only access and modify their personal data
- User data remains private and isolated from all other users
- Can choose to share specific Todos with others through explicit sharing mechanisms

#### Administrative User (admin)
**Business Role**: Platform administrator responsible for system operations, user management, and platform maintenance while respecting user privacy.

**Responsibilities and Capabilities:**
- Monitor overall system health and user activity patterns
- Manage user accounts and handle account issues
- Access any user's Todo data when necessary for support purposes
- Generate platform-wide statistics and reports
- Manage system configuration and settings
- Handle data integrity and backup operations

**Data Scope and Boundaries:**
- Can access any user's data for legitimate operational purposes
- Administrative access is logged and auditable for compliance
- Limited to operational needs and support requirements
- User data privacy maintained even during administrative access

### Complete Authentication Flow Requirements

#### User Registration Process

**WHEN** a new user accesses the registration page, **THE** system SHALL collect:
- Email address (primary account identifier)
- Strong password meeting security requirements
- Password confirmation
- Optional full name for personalization

**WHEN** user submits registration information, **THE** system SHALL validate:
- Email format valid and not already registered
- Password meets complexity requirements (8+ characters, mixed case, numbers, special characters)
- Password and confirmation match exactly
- All fields completed before processing

**WHEN** registration validation succeeds, **THE** system SHALL:
- Create user account in pending verification status
- Send verification email to user's email address
- Provide clear instructions for email verification process
- Prevent login until email verification completed

#### Email Verification Process

**WHEN** user receives verification email, **THE** system SHALL:
- Provide unique verification link with limited time validity (24 hours)
- Include clear instructions for verification process
- Set verification link expiration to 24 hours from generation

**WHEN** user clicks verification link, **THE** system SHALL:
- Validate link authenticity and expiration status
- Activate user account upon successful verification
- Redirect user to login page with success confirmation
- Log verification activity for security auditing

#### User Login Process

**WHEN** user accesses login page, **THE** system SHALL:
- Present email and password input fields
- Provide "Forgot Password" link for password recovery
- Display "Remember Me" option for session persistence

**WHEN** user submits login credentials, **THE** system SHALL:
- Validate email format and password presence
- Authenticate credentials against stored user data
- Check account status (must be verified and active)
- Generate JWT tokens upon successful authentication

**WHEN** authentication succeeds, **THE** system SHALL:
- Create user session with appropriate JWT access and refresh tokens
- Set secure session cookies with proper attributes
- Redirect user to their personal dashboard
- Log successful login for security monitoring

#### Password Recovery Process

**WHEN** user requests password recovery, **THE** system SHALL:
- Verify email address exists in the system
- Generate secure password reset token
- Send password reset email with time-limited reset link
- Log password recovery request for security auditing

**WHEN** user accesses password reset link, **THE** system SHALL:
- Validate reset token authenticity and expiration
- Present secure password reset form
- Require new password meeting complexity requirements
- Confirm password strength and match before processing

### Authorization and Permission Matrix

| Action | Regular User | Administrative User |
|--------|--------------|-------------------|
| Create personal Todo item | ✅ Allowed | ✅ Allowed (any user's data) |
| Read own Todo items | ✅ Allowed | ✅ Allowed (any user's data) |
| Edit own Todo items | ✅ Allowed | ✅ Allowed (any user's data) |
| Delete own Todo items | ✅ Allowed | ✅ Allowed (any user's data) |
| Mark Todo as complete/incomplete | ✅ Allowed | ✅ Allowed (any user's data) |
| View list of all users | ❌ Denied | ✅ Allowed |
| Edit user account details | ❌ Denied | ✅ Allowed |
| Reset user passwords | ❌ Denied | ✅ Allowed |
| View system logs | ❌ Denied | ✅ Allowed |

### JWT Token Security and Management

**Access Token Payload:**
- `userId`: Unique identifier for authenticated user
- `actorType`: User actor type ("user" or "admin")
- `permissions`: Array of permitted actions for this actor
- `sessionId`: Unique identifier for this login session
- `issuedAt`: Token generation timestamp
- `expiresAt`: Token expiration timestamp (15 minutes from generation)

**Refresh Token Payload:**
- `userId`: Unique identifier for authenticated user
- `sessionId`: Reference to associated session
- `issuedAt`: Token generation timestamp
- `expiresAt`: Token expiration timestamp (7 days from generation)
- `tokenType`: Identifier for refresh token type

**Session Management Requirements:**
- Maintain JWT access token with 15-minute expiration
- Provide refresh token mechanism for extended sessions
- Validate token integrity on each protected resource request
- Log session activity for security monitoring
- Support multiple concurrent sessions per user

## Comprehensive Functional Requirements

### Core Todo Operations

#### Todo Item Creation

**WHEN** a user clicks "Create Todo", **THE** system SHALL enable the user to add a new Todo item with title and description.

**WHEN** a user submits a new Todo item, **THE** system SHALL validate and store:
- Todo title (required, 1-255 characters)
- Todo description (optional, 0-1000 characters)
- Created timestamp (auto-generated)
- User association (linked to authenticated user)
- Status indicator (default: "active")

**Validation Rules:**
- Todo title MUST be required and contain between 1 and 200 characters of meaningful text
- Todo description MUST be optional and limited to 1,000 characters
- Todo title CANNOT be identical to existing active Todo titles for the same user
- Empty titles SHALL display error "Todo title cannot be empty"
- Titles exceeding 255 characters SHALL display error "Todo title must be 255 characters or less"

**IF** a user's Todo count exceeds 1,000 items, **THE** system SHALL display warning "Todo limit reached (1,000 items)" and prevent new item creation.

**WHERE** users have administrative privileges, **THE** system SHALL enable them to create Todo items on behalf of other users by selecting target user account.

#### Todo Item Retrieval

**THE** user SHALL be able to view all their Todo items in a list format, sorted by creation date (newest first).

**WHEN** a user requests to view Todo items, **THE** system SHALL display:
- Todo title and description
- Creation date and time
- Status (active/completed)
- Optional completion date
- Edit and delete action buttons

**Filtering and Search Capabilities:**
- THE user SHALL be able to filter their Todo items by status (all, active, completed)
- THE user SHALL be able to search their Todo items by title or description text
- **WHERE** users have administrative privileges, **THE** system SHALL enable them to view Todo items from all users, with filters for specific users and status

**Search Logic:**
- **WHEN** user performs Todo search, **THE** system SHALL search within user's own Todo items only (unless administrative privileges)
- The search SHALL match text in both Todo titles and descriptions using case-insensitive partial matching
- **IF** search returns no results, **THE** system SHALL display message "No Todo items found matching your search criteria"

#### Todo Item Editing

**WHEN** a user clicks "Edit" on a Todo item, **THE** system SHALL display a form allowing modification of title and description.

**IF** a user modifies a Todo item, **THE** system SHALL update the modified timestamp and save changes immediately.

**Edit Authorization Rules:**
- THE user SHALL be able to edit their own Todo items at any time
- **WHERE** users have administrative privileges, **THE** system SHALL enable them to edit any user's Todo items
- **IF** a completed Todo item is being edited, **THE** system SHALL allow editing of most fields but maintain completion timestamp

**Edit Restrictions:**
- THE editing user SHALL be the original creator of the Todo item
- THE system SHALL verify user ownership before allowing any modifications
- ADMIN users SHALL be permitted to edit ANY user's Todo items
- Users SHALL NOT be able to modify:
  - The Todo item ID
  - The creation timestamp
  - The original creator's user ID
  - The completion status (editing completion status requires separate completion action)

#### Todo Item Completion

**WHEN** a user clicks "Mark Complete" on an active Todo item, **THE** system SHALL change the status to "completed" and record completion timestamp.

**WHEN** a user clicks "Mark Incomplete" on a completed Todo item, **THE** system SHALL change the status to "active" and remove completion timestamp.

**Completion Logic:**
- THE completed Todo items SHALL remain visible in the user's list but appear visually distinct from active items
- THE user SHALL be able to toggle Todo item status between complete and incomplete as needed
- **WHERE** users have administrative privileges, **THE** system SHALL enable them to change completion status of any user's Todo items

**Status Change Behavior:**
- **WHEN** a Todo item is marked complete, **THE** system SHALL automatically:
  - Set completion timestamp to current date/time
  - Change status from "active" to "completed"
  - Update item visually to indicate completion (strikethrough text)
  - Preserve all original Todo content (title, description, creation date)

- **WHEN** a completed Todo item is marked incomplete, **THE** system SHALL automatically:
  - Remove completion timestamp
  - Change status from "completed" to "active"
  - Update item visually to indicate active status
  - Restore full edit capabilities

#### Todo Item Deletion

**WHEN** a user clicks "Delete" on a Todo item, **THE** system SHALL display confirmation dialog "Are you sure you want to delete this Todo item?"

**IF** user confirms deletion, **THE** system SHALL permanently remove the Todo item from the database.

**IF** user cancels deletion, **THE** system SHALL keep the Todo item unchanged.

**Deletion Authorization:**
- THE user SHALL be able to delete their own Todo items at any time
- **WHERE** users have administrative privileges, **THE** system SHALL enable them to delete any user's Todo items
- **IF** a Todo item has been completed for more than 30 days, **THE** system SHALL display additional warning "This Todo item was completed over 30 days ago. Are you sure you want to delete it?"

**Deletion Constraints:**
- THE Todo creator MAY delete their own Todo items
- ADMIN users MAY delete ANY user's Todo items
- NON-OWNER users SHALL NOT be able to delete Todo items belonging to other users
- DELETED Todo items SHALL be permanently removed from the system
- **ADMIN deletions of other users' Todo items SHALL require explicit confirmation**

### User Management Functions

#### User Registration

**WHEN** a new user accesses the application, **THE** system SHALL provide registration form with email, password, and confirm password fields.

**Validation Requirements:**
- Email format MUST be valid and unique
- Password MUST meet security requirements (minimum 8 characters, contains uppercase, lowercase, and numbers)
- Password and confirm password MUST match exactly

**IF** validation fails, **THE** system SHALL display specific error messages for each validation issue and prevent account creation.

**IF** validation succeeds, **THE** system SHALL create new user account with email verification requirement.

**Additional Requirements:**
- THE system SHALL send verification email to user with confirmation link to activate account
- **IF** user doesn't verify email within 7 days, **THE** system SHALL automatically delete unverified account

#### User Authentication

**WHEN** user accesses application without valid session, **THE** system SHALL display login form requiring email and password.

**IF** user provides valid credentials, **THE** system SHALL create authenticated session and redirect to Todo list dashboard.

**IF** user provides invalid credentials, **THE** system SHALL display error message "Invalid email or password" and maintain login form.

**Session Management:**
- THE system SHALL implement session timeout after 30 days of inactivity
- **IF** session expires, **THE** system SHALL redirect user to login form and display message "Session expired. Please log in again."
- Maintain user session using JWT tokens with 15-minute expiration
- **WHEN** user performs actions (create, edit, delete Todo items), **THE** system SHALL refresh JWT token to extend session
- **IF** user remains inactive for 15 minutes, **THE** system SHALL require re-authentication for security

#### User Profile Management

**WHEN** user is authenticated, **THE** system SHALL display user profile section with current email and account information.

**WHEN** user accesses profile settings, **THE** system SHALL enable password change functionality.

**IF** user changes password, **THE** system SHALL require current password verification before accepting new password.

**Password Change Requirements:**
- THE system SHALL validate new password meets same security requirements as registration
- **WHEN** user updates profile information, **THE** system SHALL save changes immediately and display confirmation "Profile updated successfully."

## Business Rules and Validation Logic

### Todo Creation Business Rules

#### Title Validation Requirements
- THE Todo title SHALL be a required field and CANNOT be empty or null
- THE Todo title SHALL contain between 1 and 200 characters
- THE Todo title SHALL allow alphanumeric characters, spaces, and common punctuation marks
- THE Todo title SHALL reject HTML tags and script injection attempts
- THE Todo title SHALL be trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace

#### Description Validation Rules
- THE Todo description SHALL be optional and CAN be empty
- THE Todo description SHALL be limited to 2,000 characters maximum
- THE Todo description SHALL accept plain text only (no rich formatting)
- THE Todo description SHALL be validated for XSS prevention

#### Completion Status Rules
- ALL newly created Todo items SHALL default to incomplete status
- THE system SHALL track completion status as boolean true/false
- THE completion status SHALL default to false (incomplete) upon creation
- USERS MAY mark Todo items as complete immediately after creation if desired

#### Creator Attribution Rules
- THE Todo item SHALL automatically record the user ID of the creator
- THE system SHALL automatically record the creation timestamp
- THE creator information SHALL be immutable and CANNOT be modified
- THE creation timestamp SHALL use the user's local timezone

### Data Integrity Rules

#### Referencial Integrity Rules
- EVERY Todo item SHALL reference a valid, existing user
- THE system SHALL prevent creation of Todo items with invalid user references
- USER deletion SHALL cascade to their Todo items according to business policy
- FOREIGN KEY constraints SHALL be enforced at the database level

#### Security Validation Rules
- ALL user input SHALL be sanitized before database storage
- SQL injection attempts SHALL be detected and blocked
- XSS attempts SHALL be prevented through input sanitization
- Authentication tokens SHALL be validated for each request

#### Business Logic Validation Rules
- TODO item creation SHALL validate user permissions
- TODO item editing SHALL verify ownership or admin status
- TODO item deletion SHALL require appropriate authorization
- ALL timestamp fields SHALL be validated for reasonable values

### Permission Enforcement Logic

#### Authentication-Based Access Control
**WHEN** a user attempts to access Todo system resources, **THE** system SHALL:

1. **Verify Authentication Status**: Check if user is logged in
2. **Validate Session Token**: Verify JWT token validity and expiration
3. **Determine User Role**: Identify whether user is standard or admin
4. **Check Resource Permissions**: Verify user has access to requested resource
5. **Enforce Permission Rules**: Allow or deny access based on business rules

#### Resource-Specific Permission Rules

**FOR Todo creation operations:**
- ALL authenticated users MAY create Todo items
- No special permissions required for Todo creation

**FOR Todo viewing operations:**
- Users MAY view their own Todo items
- Admins MAY view all users' Todo items
- Non-owners CANNOT view other users' Todo items

**FOR Todo modification operations:**
- Todo creators MAY edit their own Todo items
- Admins MAY edit any user's Todo items
- Non-owners CANNOT edit others' Todo items

**FOR Todo deletion operations:**
- Todo creators MAY delete their own Todo items
- Admins MAY delete any user's Todo items
- Non-owners CANNOT delete others' Todo items

### Business Logic Flow

#### Todo Creation Flow
**WHEN** a user creates a new Todo item, **THE** following business logic flow SHALL execute:

```
1. Authentication Verification
   └── Verify user login status and session validity
   
2. Input Data Collection
   └── Collect title, description, and user authentication details
   
3. Data Validation Process
   └── Validate title length, format, and content
   └── Validate description length, format, and content (if provided)
   └── Verify user authentication and permissions
   
4. Database Operation
   └── Create Todo record with proper attribution
   └── Set default completion status to false
   └── Record creation timestamp
   
5. Response Generation
   └── Return created Todo item with all details
   └── Confirm successful creation to user
```

#### Todo Editing Flow
**WHEN** a user edits an existing Todo item, **THE** following business logic flow SHALL execute:

```
1. Authentication and Authorization Verification
   └── Verify user authentication status
   └── Verify user owns Todo item OR has admin privileges
   
2. Load Existing Todo Data
   └── Retrieve current Todo item from database
   └── Verify Todo item exists and is accessible
   
3. Input Data Validation
   └── Validate edited title and description
   └── Check for malicious content or injection attempts
   
4. Update Operation
   └── Update Todo item with new values
   └── Preserve immutable fields (ID, creator, creation date)
   └── Record modification timestamp
   
5. Response Generation
   └── Return updated Todo item details
   └── Confirm successful modification
```

#### Todo Deletion Flow
**WHEN** a user deletes a Todo item, **THE** following business logic flow SHALL execute:

```
1. Authentication and Authorization Verification
   └── Verify user authentication status
   └── Verify user owns Todo item OR has admin privileges
   
2. Final Permission Check
   └── Confirm user has deletion permissions
   └── Verify deletion action is intentional
   
3. Database Deletion
   └── Remove Todo item from database permanently
   └── Record deletion in audit log
   
4. Response Generation
   └── Confirm successful deletion
   └── Return minimal success response
```

## User Scenarios and Workflows

### New User Registration Flow

**Primary Registration Scenario:**
**WHEN** a visitor wants to create a new account, **THE** system SHALL guide them through a complete registration process with email verification.

#### Step-by-Step Registration Process

1. **Registration Initiation**
   - User accesses registration page/endpoint
   - System displays registration form with required fields
   - **WHEN** user submits incomplete or invalid information, **THE** system SHALL display specific validation errors

2. **Information Input**
   - User provides email address, password, and confirmation
   - System validates email format and password strength requirements
   - **WHEN** invalid email format is provided, **THE** system SHALL show email format error
   - **WHEN** weak password is provided, **THE** system SHALL display password requirements

3. **Account Creation**
   - System creates user account with pending status
   - Email verification email is sent to user's email address
   - Account remains inactive until email verification is completed
   - User receives confirmation message about verification email

4. **Email Verification**
   - User clicks verification link in email
   - System activates account and sets user as verified
   - User is automatically logged in after successful verification
   - Welcome message and initial Todo list setup are presented

#### Registration Error Scenarios

**Invalid Email Domain**
**IF** user attempts to register with email from restricted domains, **THEN** the system SHALL reject registration and display appropriate error message.

**Email Already Exists**
**IF** user attempts to register with email that already exists in system, **THEN** the system SHALL inform user about existing account and provide password recovery option.

**Registration Rate Limiting**
**IF** user attempts multiple registrations within short time period, **THEN** the system SHALL implement rate limiting and inform user about temporary restrictions.

**Network Connectivity Issues**
**IF** registration form submission fails due to network issues, **THEN** the system SHALL allow user to retry and preserve entered information.

### User Authentication Process

**Primary Login Scenario:**
**WHEN** an authenticated user wants to access their Todo list, **THE** system SHALL provide secure login with session management.

#### Step-by-Step Login Process

1. **Login Initiation**
   - User accesses login page/endpoint
   - System displays login form with email and password fields
   - User enters their registered email and password

2. **Credential Validation**
   - System validates email format and password presence
   - **WHEN** invalid email format is detected, **THE** system SHALL display format error
   - **WHEN** password is missing, **THE** system SHALL show required field error

3. **Authentication Verification**
   - System verifies credentials against user database
   - **WHEN** credentials are invalid, **THE** system SHALL display authentication error
   - **WHEN** account is not verified, **THE** system SHALL show verification required message

4. **Session Creation**
   - System creates secure session with JWT token
   - User is redirected to their Todo dashboard/list
   - Session begins tracking user activity for security

#### Password Recovery Process

1. **Recovery Request**
   - User selects "Forgot Password" option
   - System requests email address for password reset
   - **WHEN** invalid email is provided, **THE** system SHALL show appropriate error

2. **Reset Email Delivery**
   - System sends password reset email if email exists
   - User receives email with secure reset link
   - Reset link expires after specified time period

3. **Password Reset**
   - User clicks reset link and provides new password
   - System validates new password meets requirements
   - Password is updated and user is prompted to log in

### Todo Creation Journey

**Primary Todo Creation Scenario:**
**WHEN** an authenticated user wants to add a new task to their list, **THE** system SHALL provide guided Todo creation with validation.

#### Step-by-Step Creation Process

1. **Creation Initiation**
   - User selects "Add Todo" or "Create Task" option
   - System displays Todo creation form
   - Required fields and optional fields are clearly marked

2. **Information Entry**
   - User enters Todo title/description
   - User may add optional details like due date, priority, or category
   - System performs real-time validation as user types

3. **Validation and Submission**
   - System validates all entered information
   - **WHEN** validation fails, **THE** system SHALL display specific error messages
   - User can correct errors and resubmit

4. **Todo Creation**
   - System creates new Todo item in user's account
   - Todo is assigned unique identifier and creation timestamp
   - New Todo appears in user's Todo list with default status

#### Todo Creation Requirements

**Title Validation**
THE Todo title SHALL be required and must contain between 1 and 200 characters of meaningful text.

**Due Date Handling**
**IF** user provides due date, **THEN** the date SHALL be validated to ensure it's a valid future date unless otherwise specified.

**Priority Assignment**
**WHEN** creating Todo without explicit priority, **THE** system SHALL assign default priority level.

#### Creation Error Scenarios

**Database Connection Issues**
**IF** system cannot save Todo due to database issues, **THEN** the system SHALL inform user of temporary error and allow retry.

**Duplicate Todo Detection**
**IF** user attempts to create identical Todo, **THEN** the system SHALL warn user about potential duplication and confirm before proceeding.

**Storage Limitations**
**IF** user has reached maximum Todo limit, **THEN** the system SHALL inform user and provide upgrade or cleanup options.

### Todo Management Workflows

#### Viewing Personal Todo List
**WHEN** authenticated user wants to see their Todo items, **THE** system SHALL display organized list with sorting and filtering options.

#### List Display Process

1. **List Generation**
   - System retrieves all Todo items for authenticated user
   - Todos are sorted by creation date, priority, or completion status
   - System displays Todos in user-friendly format

2. **List Organization**
   - Active (incomplete) Todos are displayed prominently
   - Completed Todos may be shown separately or filtered out
   - Due dates and priorities are clearly indicated

3. **Navigation and Filtering**
   - User can filter Todos by status, priority, or date range
   - User can sort list by different criteria
   - System remembers user's preferred view settings

#### Editing Existing Todos
**WHEN** user wants to modify an existing Todo, **THE** system SHALL provide editing capability with validation.

#### Edit Process Steps

1. **Edit Initiation**
   - User clicks edit button on selected Todo
   - System displays Todo editing form with current information
   - All fields are populated with existing data

2. **Information Modification**
   - User can modify title, description, due date, or priority
   - System performs validation as changes are made
   - User can save changes or cancel editing

3. **Update Validation**
   - System validates modified information
   - **WHEN** validation fails, **THE** system SHALL preserve user changes and show specific errors
   - Successful updates are saved immediately

#### Edit Restrictions

**Ownership Verification**
THE system SHALL allow users to edit only their own Todo items, preventing unauthorized modifications.

**Completion Status Handling**
**IF** Todo is marked as completed, **THE** system SHALL allow editing of most fields but maintain completion timestamp.

### Administrative User Scenarios

#### Admin Access and Management
**WHEN** administrator wants to manage system-wide operations, **THE** system SHALL provide elevated access with appropriate controls.

#### Admin Login Process

1. **Administrative Authentication**
   - Admin logs in using elevated credentials
   - System identifies administrative role and grants additional permissions
   - Admin dashboard displays system-wide management options

2. **Permission Verification**
   - System verifies admin permissions for each requested action
   - Admin actions are logged for audit purposes
   - Unauthorized access attempts are rejected with appropriate messages

#### System-Wide Todo Management
**WHEN** administrator needs to view or manage user's Todo items, **THE** system SHALL provide controlled access to all user data.

#### User Data Access Process

1. **User Search and Selection**
   - Admin can search for users by email, name, or other identifiers
   - System displays list of matching users with basic information
   - Admin selects target user for Todo management

2. **Todo List Access**
   - System displays selected user's Todo items to admin
   - Admin can view, edit, or delete any Todo in user's list
   - All admin actions are logged with timestamp and admin identifier

## Security and Data Protection Requirements

### Authentication Security Measures

**THE** authentication system SHALL implement the following security controls:
- Password complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters with mixed case, numbers, and special characters
- Account lockout after 5 consecutive failed login attempts for 15 minutes
- Rate limiting on authentication endpoints to prevent brute force attacks
- Secure password hashing using industry-standard algorithms (bcrypt with appropriate salt rounds)
- Session timeout after 30 minutes of inactivity requiring re-authentication

### Data Protection and Privacy Requirements

**THE** user data protection measures SHALL include:
- All user passwords must be hashed with strong cryptographic algorithms
- User email addresses must be encrypted at rest in the database
- Personal Todo data must be encrypted during transmission (HTTPS mandatory)
- Session tokens must be transmitted over secure channels only
- User data access logs must be maintained for compliance and security

**THE** privacy protection requirements SHALL:
- User data must not be shared with third parties without explicit consent
- Administrative access to user data must be logged and auditable
- Users must be able to request data export or deletion
- Data retention policies must be clearly defined and communicated
- Users must control their data sharing and visibility settings

### Session Security Controls

**THE** session security implementation SHALL:
- Use secure, HTTP-only cookies for session token storage
- Implement proper cookie attributes (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite)
- Validate session integrity on every protected resource request
- Terminate sessions upon suspicious activity detection
- Provide session management interface for users to monitor active sessions

### Security Monitoring and Compliance

**THE** system SHALL implement comprehensive security monitoring:
- Log all authentication attempts (successful and failed)
- Monitor and alert on unusual login patterns or locations
- Track administrative access to user data for audit purposes
- Implement security event correlation and alerting
- Maintain security incident response procedures

**THE** compliance requirements SHALL include:
- User data protection measures aligned with applicable privacy regulations
- Secure data transmission and storage practices
- Audit trail maintenance for administrative actions
- User consent management for data processing activities
- Data breach notification procedures and response plans

## Performance and Scalability Requirements

### System Capacity and Performance

**THE** system SHALL meet the following performance requirements:

**Response Time Expectations:**
- Todo list loading: Under 2 seconds for up to 500 items
- Todo creation, editing, and deletion: Under 1 second response time
- User authentication (login/logout): Under 3 seconds
- Search operations: Under 1 second for typical query volumes

**System Capacity:**
- Support up to 10,000 registered users simultaneously
- Handle up to 1,000 Todo items per user
- Process up to 1,000 Todo operations per minute during peak usage
- Maintain performance under normal load conditions

**Data Management:**
- Automatic indexing for fast Todo search and filtering
- Efficient database queries that scale with user base
- Real-time synchronization of Todo changes across user sessions
- Optimized data structures for minimal database load

### Scalability Considerations

**THE** system SHALL be designed to handle:
- UP TO 1,000 active concurrent users
- UNLIMITED Todo items per user
- MINIMAL performance degradation with increased user load
- HORIZONTAL scaling capability for future growth

### Data Retention and Cleanup Logic

**THE** system SHALL automatically delete Todo items that have been marked complete for more than 365 days.

**THE** system SHALL maintain active Todo items indefinitely unless manually deleted by user.

**IF** user account is deleted, **THE** system SHALL automatically delete all associated Todo items.

**THE** system SHALL create weekly backups of all Todo data and user account information.

**THE** system SHALL purge unverified user accounts that remain unactivated after 7 days from registration.

## Error Handling and Recovery Procedures

### Comprehensive Error Handling

**THE** system SHALL implement comprehensive error handling:

**For User Errors:**
- Clear, specific error messages that help users understand and resolve issues
- Form validation that prevents submission of invalid data
- Graceful handling of network connectivity issues
- Automatic retry mechanisms for temporary failures

**For System Errors:**
- Automatic logging of all errors with timestamp and user context
- User-friendly error messages that don't expose system internals
- Fallback mechanisms for critical system failures
- Notification to administrators for critical system issues

### User Recovery Processes

**THE** system SHALL provide helpful user guidance:
- Contextual help text for form fields and actions
- Onboarding instructions for new users
- Tooltips explaining Todo status and available actions
- Confirmation messages for successful operations

**Emergency Contact and Support:**
**IF** user encounters critical errors that prevent system use, **THEN** the system SHALL provide emergency contact information and escalation procedures.

**WHEN** user data appears corrupted or lost, **THE** system SHALL initiate data recovery procedures and provide regular status updates.

### Network Connectivity Issues

**WHEN** user experiences network connectivity problems, **THE** system SHALL provide appropriate error handling and recovery options.

#### Network Error Scenarios

**Connection Timeout**
**IF** user request times out due to network issues, **THEN** the system SHALL inform user about connectivity problems and suggest retry.

**Offline Operation**
**IF** user loses internet connection during Todo creation or editing, **THEN** the system SHALL preserve unsaved changes and restore when connection is restored.

**Connection Restoration**
**WHEN** network connection is restored, **THE** system SHALL automatically retry pending operations and sync any locally cached changes.

## Integration and External Requirements

### Email Integration

**THE** system SHALL integrate with email service for:
- User registration verification emails
- Password reset emails
- Administrative notifications for critical system events

**Email templates SHALL be professional and include:**
- Clear branding and application identity
- Simple, actionable instructions for users
- Contact information for support when needed
- Professional formatting and readable content

### Security Integration

**THE** system SHALL implement security best practices:
- HTTPS enforcement for all user interactions
- Password hashing using industry-standard algorithms
- Input sanitization to prevent injection attacks
- Rate limiting to prevent abuse and spam
- Secure session management with proper token handling

**THE** system SHALL log security-relevant events:**
- Failed login attempts
- Password change activities
- Administrative user actions
- Data access from unauthorized users

## Quality Assurance and Testing Requirements

### Testing Requirements

**THE** system SHALL pass comprehensive testing including:**
- Unit testing for all Todo and user management functions
- Integration testing for authentication and authorization flows
- Performance testing to validate response time requirements
- Security testing to verify protection against common vulnerabilities
- User acceptance testing to ensure business requirements are met

### Monitoring and Maintenance

**THE** system SHALL implement monitoring capabilities:**
- Real-time performance monitoring and alerting
- Error tracking and automated reporting
- User activity analytics and usage reporting
- Database performance monitoring and optimization alerts

**THE** system SHALL provide maintenance capabilities:**
- Automated backup and recovery procedures
- Database maintenance and optimization routines
- Log rotation and archival systems
- System health checks and status reporting

## Success Criteria and Implementation Readiness

### Application Success Criteria

**THE** application SHALL be considered successful when:**
- All core Todo operations function correctly (create, read, update, delete, complete/incomplete)
- User authentication and authorization work reliably for both user and admin roles
- Data validation prevents invalid inputs and provides helpful error messages
- Performance requirements are met under normal usage conditions
- System is secure against common web application vulnerabilities
- User interface is intuitive and requires no programming knowledge to operate
- Administrative functions allow proper system management and oversight

### Implementation Readiness

**THE** system SHALL provide implementation readiness through:
- Complete functional requirements specification
- Detailed user actor definitions and authentication flows
- Comprehensive business rules and validation logic
- Clear security and performance requirements
- Comprehensive error handling and recovery procedures
- Complete user scenario documentation

This requirements analysis report serves as the complete foundation for Todo list application development, providing all necessary business and technical specifications to build a production-ready system that meets user needs while maintaining security, performance, and reliability standards.
