# Business Rules for Todo Management System

## Executive Summary

This document defines the comprehensive business rules, validation logic, and operational constraints for the Todo management system. These rules ensure data integrity, user permission enforcement, and consistent application behavior across all Todo operations.

The Todo application provides essential task management functionality through minimum viable features: user authentication, Todo item creation, editing, deletion, and completion tracking. Business rules govern every aspect of Todo lifecycle management while maintaining security and data consistency.

## 1. Business Rules Foundation

### Core Business Principles
THE Todo management system SHALL operate under the following fundamental business principles:

1. **User Ownership Principle**: Every Todo item MUST be owned by the user who created it
2. **Data Integrity Principle**: All Todo data MUST be validated and consistent at all times
3. **Permission Isolation Principle**: Users CANNOT access or modify Todo items belonging to other users
4. **Audit Trail Principle**: All Todo modifications MUST be tracked with proper timestamps and user attribution

### System Boundaries and Scope
THE Todo application SHALL handle only the following business entities:
- User accounts and authentication data
- Todo items with basic task information
- Todo completion status and timestamps

THE Todo application SHALL NOT handle:
- Advanced task categorization or tagging
- Complex project management features
- File attachments or multimedia content
- Social sharing or collaboration features

## 2. Todo Creation Rules

### Todo Item Validation Requirements

WHEN a user attempts to create a new Todo item, THE system SHALL validate the following requirements:

#### Title Validation Rules
- THE Todo title SHALL be a required field and CANNOT be empty or null
- THE Todo title SHALL contain between 1 and 200 characters
- THE Todo title SHALL allow alphanumeric characters, spaces, and common punctuation marks
- THE Todo title SHALL reject HTML tags and script injection attempts
- THE Todo title SHALL be trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace

#### Description Validation Rules
- THE Todo description SHALL be optional and CAN be empty
- THE Todo description SHALL be limited to 2,000 characters maximum
- THE Todo description SHALL accept plain text only (no rich formatting)
- THE Todo description SHALL be validated for XSS prevention

#### Completion Status Rules
- ALL newly created Todo items SHALL default to incomplete status
- THE system SHALL track completion status as boolean true/false
- THE completion status SHALL default to false (incomplete) upon creation
- USERS MAY mark Todo items as complete immediately after creation if desired

#### Creator Attribution Rules
- THE Todo item SHALL automatically record the user ID of the creator
- THE system SHALL automatically record the creation timestamp
- THE creator information SHALL be immutable and CANNOT be modified
- THE creation timestamp SHALL use the user's local timezone

### Todo Creation Workflow Rules

WHEN a user submits a new Todo item for creation, THE system SHALL execute the following sequence:

1. **Authentication Verification**: Verify the user is logged in and authenticated
2. **Input Validation**: Validate all provided Todo data against business rules
3. **Data Sanitization**: Clean and sanitize all user input data
4. **Database Creation**: Create the Todo item with proper ownership attribution
5. **Response Generation**: Return success confirmation with the new Todo item details

IF any validation fails during Todo creation, THE system SHALL:
- Return specific error messages indicating which validation rule was violated
- NOT create the Todo item in the database
- Preserve any valid partial data entered by the user
- Log the validation failure for security monitoring

## 3. Edit and Delete Constraints

### Todo Modification Authorization Rules

WHEN a user attempts to edit an existing Todo item, THE system SHALL enforce the following authorization constraints:

#### Ownership Verification Rules
- THE editing user SHALL be the original creator of the Todo item
- THE system SHALL verify user ownership before allowing any modifications
- ADMIN users SHALL be permitted to edit ANY user's Todo items
- NON-OWNER users SHALL be denied access and receive appropriate error messages

#### Editable Field Constraints
- USERS MAY edit the Todo title and description fields
- USERS SHALL NOT be able to modify:
  - The Todo item ID
  - The creation timestamp
  - The original creator's user ID
  - The completion status (editing completion status requires separate completion action)

### Todo Deletion Authorization Rules

WHEN a user attempts to delete a Todo item, THE system SHALL enforce the following deletion constraints:

#### Deletion Permission Rules
- THE Todo creator MAY delete their own Todo items
- ADMIN users MAY delete ANY user's Todo items
- NON-OWNER users SHALL NOT be able to delete Todo items belonging to other users
- DELETED Todo items SHALL be permanently removed from the system

#### Deletion Confirmation Requirements
- USERS shall NOT be required to provide confirmation when deleting their own Todo items
- ADMIN deletions of other users' Todo items SHALL require explicit confirmation
- THE system SHALL implement soft deletion for audit purposes if required by business policy
- COMPLETED Todo items MAY be deleted using the same rules as incomplete items

### Edit and Delete Audit Requirements

WHEN any Todo item is edited or deleted, THE system SHALL:
- Record the user ID of the person performing the action
- Record the timestamp of the modification
- Store the previous values if editing (for audit trail)
- Log the action for security and compliance purposes

## 4. Data Validation Logic

### Comprehensive Input Validation Rules

#### Title Field Validation Logic
THE Todo title field SHALL comply with the following validation logic:

- **Required Field Check**: Title MUST be present and non-empty
- **Length Validation**: Title MUST be between 1 and 200 characters inclusive
- **Character Set Validation**: Title SHALL contain only allowed characters:
  - English letters (A-Z, a-z)
  - Numbers (0-9)
  - Common punctuation marks (!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:,.<>?)
  - Whitespace characters (space, tab, newline)
- **Security Validation**: Title SHALL NOT contain:
  - HTML tags (< > /)
  - JavaScript code
  - SQL injection attempts
  - XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) payloads
- **Format Validation**: Title SHALL be properly encoded in UTF-8

#### Description Field Validation Logic
THE Todo description field SHALL comply with the following validation logic:

- **Optional Field Check**: Description MAY be null or empty
- **Length Validation**: When provided, description MUST be between 1 and 2,000 characters
- **Character Set Validation**: Same character restrictions as title field
- **Security Validation**: Same security checks as title field
- **Format Validation**: Text MUST be properly encoded and sanitized

#### User Data Validation Logic
FOR user-related data validation, THE system SHALL enforce:

- **User Authentication**: Every Todo operation SHALL verify user authentication status
- **User ID Validation**: User IDs SHALL be validated as existing, active user accounts
- **Session Validation**: User sessions SHALL be verified as valid and non-expired

### Data Integrity Rules

THE Todo system SHALL maintain data integrity through the following validation mechanisms:

#### Referential Integrity Rules
- EVERY Todo item SHALL reference a valid, existing user
- THE system SHALL prevent creation of Todo items with invalid user references
- USER deletion SHALL cascade to their Todo items according to business policy
- FOREIGN KEY constraints SHALL be enforced at the database level

#### Business Logic Validation Rules
- TODO item creation SHALL validate user permissions
- TODO item editing SHALL verify ownership or admin status
- TODO item deletion SHALL require appropriate authorization
- ALL timestamp fields SHALL be validated for reasonable values

#### Security Validation Rules
- ALL user input SHALL be sanitized before database storage
- SQL injection attempts SHALL be detected and blocked
- XSS attempts SHALL be prevented through input sanitization
- Authentication tokens SHALL be validated for each request

## 5. User Permission Rules

### User Role Definitions and Permissions

#### Standard User Permissions
STANDARD users (user role) SHALL have the following permissions:

- **Todo Creation Permissions**: Users MAY create unlimited Todo items
- **Todo Viewing Permissions**: Users MAY view their own Todo items
- **Todo Editing Permissions**: Users MAY edit Todo items they created
- **Todo Deletion Permissions**: Users MAY delete Todo items they created
- **Profile Management Permissions**: Users MAY view and edit their own profile information
- **Session Management Permissions**: Users MAY log in, log out, and manage their sessions

#### Administrator User Permissions
ADMIN users (admin role) SHALL have the following elevated permissions:

- **Global Todo Management**: Admins MAY view, edit, and delete ANY user's Todo items
- **User Management**: Admins MAY manage all user accounts in the system
- **System Administration**: Admins MAY access system settings and configuration
- **Audit Access**: Admins MAY view system logs and audit trails
- **Override Permissions**: Admins MAY override user restrictions when necessary

### Permission Enforcement Logic

#### Authentication-Based Access Control
WHEN a user attempts to access Todo system resources, THE system SHALL:

1. **Verify Authentication Status**: Check if user is logged in
2. **Validate Session Token**: Verify JWT token validity and expiration
3. **Determine User Role**: Identify whether user is standard or admin
4. **Check Resource Permissions**: Verify user has access to requested resource
5. **Enforce Permission Rules**: Allow or deny access based on business rules

#### Resource-Specific Permission Rules

FOR Todo creation operations:
- ALL authenticated users MAY create Todo items
- No special permissions required for Todo creation

FOR Todo viewing operations:
- Users MAY view their own Todo items
- Admins MAY view all users' Todo items
- Non-owners CANNOT view other users' Todo items

FOR Todo modification operations:
- Todo creators MAY edit their own Todo items
- Admins MAY edit any user's Todo items
- Non-owners CANNOT edit others' Todo items

FOR Todo deletion operations:
- Todo creators MAY delete their own Todo items
- Admins MAY delete any user's Todo items
- Non-owners CANNOT delete others' Todo items

### Permission Error Handling

WHEN insufficient permissions prevent an operation, THE system SHALL:
- Return HTTP 403 Forbidden status
- Provide specific error message explaining permission denial
- Log the unauthorized access attempt for security monitoring
- NOT reveal sensitive information about resource ownership to unauthorized users

## 6. Business Logic Flow

### Complete Todo Lifecycle Process

#### Todo Creation Flow
WHEN a user creates a new Todo item, THE following business logic flow SHALL execute:

```
1. Authentication Verification
   └── Verify user login status and session validity
   
2. Input Data Collection
   └── Collect title, description, and user authentication details
   
3. Data Validation Process
   └── Validate title length, format, and content
   └── Validate description length, format, and content (if provided)
   └── Verify user authentication and permissions
   
4. Database Operation
   └── Create Todo record with proper attribution
   └── Set default completion status to false
   └── Record creation timestamp
   
5. Response Generation
   └── Return created Todo item with all details
   └── Confirm successful creation to user
```

#### Todo Editing Flow
WHEN a user edits an existing Todo item, THE following business logic flow SHALL execute:

```
1. Authentication and Authorization Verification
   └── Verify user authentication status
   └── Verify user owns Todo item OR has admin privileges
   
2. Load Existing Todo Data
   └── Retrieve current Todo item from database
   └── Verify Todo item exists and is accessible
   
3. Input Data Validation
   └── Validate edited title and description
   └── Check for malicious content or injection attempts
   
4. Update Operation
   └── Update Todo item with new values
   └── Preserve immutable fields (ID, creator, creation date)
   └── Record modification timestamp
   
5. Response Generation
   └── Return updated Todo item details
   └── Confirm successful modification
```

#### Todo Deletion Flow
WHEN a user deletes a Todo item, THE following business logic flow SHALL execute:

```
1. Authentication and Authorization Verification
   └── Verify user authentication status
   └── Verify user owns Todo item OR has admin privileges
   
2. Final Permission Check
   └── Confirm user has deletion permissions
   └── Verify deletion action is intentional
   
3. Database Deletion
   └── Remove Todo item from database permanently
   └── Record deletion in audit log
   
4. Response Generation
   └── Confirm successful deletion
   └── Return minimal success response
```

### Todo Completion Toggle Logic

WHEN a user marks a Todo item as complete or incomplete, THE following business logic SHALL apply:

#### Completion Status Rules
- THE completion status SHALL be toggleable by Todo owner or admin
- THE system SHALL automatically record completion timestamp when marked complete
- THE system SHALL NOT modify completion timestamp when marked incomplete
- THE completion timestamp SHALL reflect the most recent status change

#### Status Change Validation
- USERS MAY only change completion status of Todo items they own
- ADMINS MAY change completion status of any user's Todo items
- THE completion status SHALL be validated as boolean true/false
- THE system SHALL maintain completion history if required

## 7. Edge Cases and Error Handling

### Uncommon Scenarios and Recovery Procedures

#### Orphaned Todo Items
WHEN a user account is deleted while Todo items exist, THE system SHALL:

- DELETE all Todo items belonging to the deleted user account
- LOG the deletion for audit purposes
- RETURN appropriate error messages to any attempted access to deleted items
- MAINTAIN referential integrity throughout the deletion process

#### Concurrent Modification Scenarios
WHEN multiple users attempt to modify the same Todo item simultaneously, THE system SHALL:

- IMPLEMENT optimistic locking to detect conflicts
- REJECT modifications made to stale Todo item versions
- PROVIDE conflict resolution guidance to users
- LOG concurrent modification attempts for monitoring

#### Invalid or Corrupted Data
WHEN the system detects invalid or corrupted Todo data, THE system SHALL:

- QUARANTINE corrupted Todo items from public access
- LOG corruption detection for technical investigation
- ATTEMPT automatic data recovery if possible
- ESCALATE to system administrators for manual intervention

#### Authentication and Session Issues
WHEN authentication failures occur during Todo operations, THE system SHALL:

- TERMINATE any ongoing Todo modifications
- REQUIRE user re-authentication before proceeding
- PROVIDE clear error messages about authentication requirements
- LOG authentication failures for security monitoring

### System Error Recovery Procedures

#### Database Connectivity Issues
WHEN database connectivity problems occur, THE system SHALL:

- RETURN appropriate HTTP 500 status for Todo operations
- PROVIDE user-friendly error messages
- LOG database connectivity issues for technical investigation
- ATTEMPT connection retry if appropriate

#### Validation Failure Scenarios
WHEN Todo data validation fails, THE system SHALL:

- RETURN specific HTTP 400 status with validation error details
- HIGHLIGHT the specific fields that failed validation
- PROVIDE helpful error messages explaining validation requirements
- PRESERVE any valid input data entered by the user

## 8. Data Integrity Requirements

### Consistency and Reliability Rules

#### Transaction Integrity
ALL Todo creation, editing, and deletion operations SHALL execute within database transactions to ensure:

- ATOMICITY: Operations complete fully or not at all
- CONSISTENCY: Database remains in valid state after operations
- ISOLATION: Concurrent operations don't interfere with each other
- DURABILITY: Successfully completed operations persist permanently

#### Data Synchronization Rules
THE Todo system SHALL maintain data synchronization through:

- CONSISTENT database updates across all related records
- PROPER handling of concurrent access scenarios
- RELIABLE timestamp management across all operations
- CONSISTENT permission enforcement across all data access

#### Audit and Logging Requirements
THE system SHALL maintain comprehensive audit trails for:

- ALL Todo creation, modification, and deletion events
- USER authentication and session management events
- PERMISSION denied events for security monitoring
- SYSTEM errors and exception handling events

### Performance and Scalability Considerations

#### Response Time Requirements
THE Todo system SHALL meet the following performance requirements:

- TODO item creation SHALL complete within 2 seconds
- TODO item retrieval SHALL complete within 1 second
- TODO item editing SHALL complete within 2 seconds
- TODO item deletion SHALL complete within 2 seconds

#### Scalability Constraints
THE system SHALL be designed to handle:

- UP TO 1,000 active concurrent users
- UNLIMITED Todo items per user
- MINIMAL performance degradation with increased user load
- HORIZONTAL scaling capability for future growth

## Summary

These business rules define the complete operational framework for the Todo management system. All rules are designed to ensure data integrity, security, and user experience while maintaining the minimum functionality approach requested for the application. The rules provide clear guidance for developers implementing the system while ensuring consistent behavior across all Todo operations.

The business logic emphasizes user ownership, data validation, and proper authorization while providing comprehensive error handling and recovery procedures. These rules serve as the foundation for implementing a secure, reliable, and user-friendly Todo management system.

# TodoApp Requirements Analysis Report

## 1. Service Overview

### 1.1 Purpose and Vision

The TodoApp Todo List Application provides a streamlined, secure task management solution designed for individual productivity and personal organization. The application focuses on essential Todo management capabilities through a clean, intuitive interface that requires no programming knowledge to operate.

### 1.2 Target Users

The application serves two primary user segments:

**Individual Users**: Personal task management for daily productivity, project tracking, and personal organization. Users who need a reliable, simple way to create, manage, and track their personal tasks and goals.

**System Administrators**: Administrative users who require system oversight capabilities to manage user accounts, monitor platform usage, and provide technical support when needed.

### 1.3 Core Value Proposition

**Simple Task Management**: Enable users to quickly create, organize, and track their personal tasks without complexity or unnecessary features.

**Secure Personal Data**: Provide robust security and privacy protection for user's personal Todo data through proper authentication and authorization.

**Reliable Performance**: Ensure consistent, fast response times for all Todo operations to support daily productivity workflows.

**Administrative Oversight**: Provide system administrators with appropriate tools to manage the platform and support users when needed.

### 1.4 Business Model

The TodoApp operates as a software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform with freemium capabilities:

**Free Tier**: Basic Todo management functionality for individual users including unlimited Todo creation, editing, deletion, and basic completion tracking.

**Administrative Features**: Elevated access for platform administrators to manage users, monitor system health, and provide customer support.

**Data Ownership**: Users maintain complete ownership and control over their personal Todo data with secure authentication and privacy protection.

### 1.5 Success Metrics

The application achieves success when:
- Users can reliably create, edit, and manage their Todo items without errors
- Authentication system provides secure access with appropriate session management
- Performance meets specified response time requirements under normal usage
- Administrative features enable proper system oversight and user support
- User data remains private and secure while allowing appropriate administrative access for support

## 2. User Actors and Authentication Requirements

### 2.1 User Actor Definitions

#### Regular User Actor
**Business Role**: Individual task management service user who creates and manages personal Todo lists for productivity and organization purposes.

**Responsibilities and Capabilities**:
- Create, edit, delete, and mark complete personal Todo items
- Organize Todos through basic categorization and priority assignment
- Manage personal account settings and preferences
- View and search through their own Todo history and statistics
- Export or backup their personal Todo data
- Manage personal session and security settings

**Data Scope and Ownership**:
- Users have complete ownership and control over their own Todo items
- Users can only access and modify their personal data
- User data remains private and isolated from all other users
- Users can choose to share specific Todos with others through explicit sharing mechanisms

**Usage Patterns**:
- Daily task creation and completion activities
- Periodic review and organization of Todo lists
- Account maintenance and preference updates
- Periodic data export or backup activities

#### Administrative User Actor
**Business Role**: Platform administrator responsible for system operations, user management, and platform maintenance while respecting user privacy and data protection requirements.

**Responsibilities and Capabilities**:
- Monitor overall system health and user activity patterns
- Manage user accounts (view user lists, handle account issues, deactivate problematic accounts)
- Access any user's Todo data when necessary for support purposes
- Generate platform-wide statistics and reports
- Manage system configuration and settings
- Handle data integrity and backup operations
- Respond to user support requests requiring account access

**Data Scope and Boundaries**:
- Administrators can access any user's data for legitimate operational purposes
- Administrative access is logged and auditable for compliance
- Administrative actions are limited to operational needs and support requirements
- User data privacy is maintained even during administrative access

**Usage Patterns**:
- Regular system monitoring and maintenance activities
- User support and account issue resolution
- Periodic review of system metrics and user statistics
- Emergency response and data recovery operations

### 2.2 Authentication Flow Requirements

#### User Registration Process

**WHEN** a new user accesses the registration page, **THE** system SHALL collect the following information:
- Email address (used as primary account identifier)
- Strong password meeting security requirements
- Password confirmation
- Optional full name for personalization

**WHEN** a user submits registration information, **THE** system SHALL perform the following validations:
- Email address must be valid format and not already registered
- Password must meet minimum complexity requirements (8+ characters, mixed case, numbers, special characters)
- Password and confirmation must match exactly
- All fields must be completed before processing

**WHEN** registration validation succeeds, **THE** system SHALL:
- Create user account in pending verification status
- Send verification email to user's email address
- Provide clear instructions for email verification process
- Prevent login until email verification is completed

**WHEN** registration validation fails, **THE** system SHALL:
- Display specific error messages for each validation failure
- Preserve user input (except password fields)
- Guide user to correct validation errors
- Maintain registration session for user convenience

#### Email Verification Process

**WHEN** user receives verification email, **THE** system SHALL:
- Provide unique verification link with limited time validity
- Include clear instructions for verification process
- Set verification link expiration to 24 hours from generation

**WHEN** user clicks verification link, **THE** system SHALL:
- Validate link authenticity and expiration status
- Activate user account upon successful verification
- Redirect user to login page with success confirmation
- Log verification activity for security auditing

**WHEN** verification link expires or is invalid, **THE** system SHALL:
- Display appropriate error message explaining expiration
- Provide option to request new verification email
- Maintain user account in pending status until successful verification

#### User Login Process

**WHEN** user accesses login page, **THE** system SHALL:
- Present email and password input fields
- Provide "Forgot Password" link for password recovery
- Display "Remember Me" option for session persistence

**WHEN** user submits login credentials, **THE** system SHALL:
- Validate email format and password presence
- Authenticate credentials against stored user data
- Check account status (must be verified and active)
- Generate JWT tokens upon successful authentication

**WHEN** authentication succeeds, **THE** system SHALL:
- Create user session with appropriate JWT access and refresh tokens
- Set secure session cookies with proper attributes
- Redirect user to their personal dashboard
- Log successful login for security monitoring

**WHEN** authentication fails, **THE** system SHALL:
- Display generic authentication error message (no specific failure details)
- Log failed login attempt for security monitoring
- Implement rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks
- Allow user to attempt login again after brief cooldown

#### Password Recovery Process

**WHEN** user requests password recovery, **THE** system SHALL:
- Verify email address exists in the system
- Generate secure password reset token
- Send password reset email with time-limited reset link
- Log password recovery request for security auditing

**WHEN** user accesses password reset link, **THE** system SHALL:
- Validate reset token authenticity and expiration
- Present secure password reset form
- Require new password meeting complexity requirements
- Confirm password strength and match before processing

**WHEN** password reset completes successfully, **THE** system SHALL:
- Update user password with new secure hash
- Invalidate all existing sessions and refresh tokens
- Send confirmation email about password change
- Redirect user to login page with success message

#### Session Management Requirements

**WHILE** user has active session, **THE** system SHALL:
- Maintain JWT access token with 15-minute expiration
- Provide refresh token mechanism for extended sessions
- Validate token integrity on each protected resource request
- Log session activity for security monitoring

**WHEN** access token expires, **THE** system SHALL:
- Validate refresh token and generate new access token
- Maintain user session without requiring re-authentication
- Refresh token validity maintains session continuity

**WHEN** refresh token expires or becomes invalid, **THE** system SHALL:
- Terminate user session and require re-authentication
- Clear all session data and cookies

### 2.4 JWT Token Security and Management

#### Token Generation and Structure

**WHEN** user authentication succeeds, **THE** system SHALL generate JWT tokens with the following payload structure:

**Access Token Payload**:
- `userId`: Unique identifier for authenticated user
- `actorType`: User actor type ("user" or "admin")
- `permissions`: Array of permitted actions for this actor
- `sessionId`: Unique identifier for this login session
- `issuedAt`: Token generation timestamp
- `expiresAt`: Token expiration timestamp (15 minutes from generation)

**Refresh Token Payload**:
- `userId`: Unique identifier for authenticated user
- `sessionId`: Reference to associated session
- `issuedAt`: Token generation timestamp
- `expiresAt`: Token expiration timestamp (7 days from generation)
- `tokenType`: Identifier for refresh token type

#### Token Security Requirements

**THE** JWT token implementation SHALL implement the following security measures:
- Tokens must be signed with secure algorithm (HS256 minimum)
- Token secrets must be stored securely and rotated periodically
- All tokens must include expiration times to limit exposure
- Token payload must not contain sensitive user information
- Refresh tokens must be single-use or revocable

**THE** token validation process SHALL:
- Verify token signature integrity on every request
- Check token expiration status before processing requests
- Validate session ID consistency across token types
- Log all token validation failures for security monitoring

- **USERS** MAY mark Todo items as complete immediately after creation if desired

**Creator Attribution Rules**
- **THE** Todo item SHALL automatically record the user ID of the creator

**External Service Dependencies:**
- When third-party services fail (email, file storage, etc.), provide graceful degradation
- Display message: "Some features are temporarily unavailable while we resolve technical issues. Core functionality remains accessible."

## 7. Performance and Quality Requirements

### 7.1 Performance Expectations

**Response Time Requirements:**
- Todo list loading: Under 2 seconds for up to 500 items
- Todo creation, editing, and deletion: Under 1 second response time
- User authentication (login/logout): Under 3 seconds
- Search operations: Under 1 second for typical query volumes

**System Capacity:**
- Support up to 10,000 registered users simultaneously
- Handle up to 1,000 Todo items per user
- Process up to 1,000 Todo operations per minute during peak usage
- Maintain performance under normal load conditions

**Data Management:**
- Automatic indexing for fast Todo search and filtering
- Efficient database queries that scale with user base
- Real-time synchronization of Todo changes across user sessions
- Optimized data structures for minimal database load

### 7.2 Quality Assurance Requirements

**Testing Requirements:**
- Unit testing for all Todo and user management functions
- Integration testing for authentication and authorization flows
- Performance testing to validate response time requirements
- Security testing to verify protection against common vulnerabilities
- User acceptance testing to ensure business requirements are met

**Monitoring and Maintenance:**
- Real-time performance monitoring and alerting
- Error tracking and automated reporting
- User activity analytics and usage reporting
- Database performance monitoring and optimization alerts

## 8. Success Criteria

The application SHALL be considered successful when:

- All core Todo operations function correctly (create, read, update, delete, complete/incomplete)
- User authentication and authorization work reliably for both user and admin roles
- Data validation prevents invalid inputs and provides helpful error messages
- Performance requirements are met under normal usage conditions
- System is secure against common web application vulnerabilities
- User interface is intuitive and requires no programming knowledge to operate
- Administrative functions allow proper system management and oversight
- Error handling provides clear, actionable guidance to users for recovery
- User data remains private and secure while enabling necessary administrative access

## 9. Future Considerations

While implementing the minimal required functionality, the system SHALL be designed with extensibility in mind to support future enhancements such as:

- Todo item categories and tagging
- Due date tracking and reminders
- Collaborative Todo items shared between users
- Mobile application development
- Advanced reporting and analytics
- Integration with external calendar systems
- Team-based Todo management
- Priority-based filtering and sorting
- Todo item dependencies and subtasks

This comprehensive requirements analysis ensures that the TodoApp Todo List Application provides essential task management capabilities while maintaining security, performance, and usability standards suitable for both individual users and administrative oversight. The specification serves as the authoritative foundation for backend development, ensuring all user interactions are properly supported with appropriate validation, security, and error handling.

# TodoApp Requirements Analysis Report

## 1. Executive Summary

TodoApp is a streamlined task management application designed to provide essential Todo list functionality with minimal complexity. The application focuses on core task management capabilities while ensuring optimal user experience and system reliability. This requirements analysis defines the minimum viable features required for an effective Todo list application that can be implemented by backend developers without unnecessary complexity.

## 2. User Actors and Authentication

### 2.1 Primary User Actor

**Registered User**: Individuals who create accounts to manage their personal Todo lists.

**Actor Description**: End users who need to organize, track, and manage their daily tasks and responsibilities. These users value simplicity and reliability over advanced features.

**Core Capabilities**:
- Create, edit, and delete Todo items
- Mark Todo items as complete or incomplete
- View their personal Todo list
- Manage their user account and authentication

### 2.2 Authentication Requirements

**WHEN a user visits TodoApp for the first time, THE system SHALL provide options to register a new account or log in to an existing account.**

**WHEN a user registers a new account, THE system SHALL require a valid email address and secure password, then create their account and automatically log them in.**

**WHEN a user logs in with valid credentials, THE system SHALL authenticate them and redirect them to their personal Todo dashboard within 2 seconds.**

**WHEN a user enters invalid login credentials, THE system SHALL display an error message within 1 second and allow them to retry without locking their account.**

**WHEN a user logs out, THE system SHALL terminate their session and redirect them to the login page.**

### 2.3 Session Management

**WHEN a user is authenticated, THE system SHALL maintain their session and automatically refresh authentication tokens as needed.**

**IF a user's session expires, THE system SHALL redirect them to the login page and clear any cached data.**

**WHEN a user closes their browser or navigates away, THE system SHALL preserve their session state and automatically log them back in when they return (if session is still valid).**

## 3. Core Todo Operations

### 3.1 Todo Item Creation

**WHEN a user wants to add a new task, THE system SHALL provide a simple input field where they can enter the task description.**

**WHEN a user submits a new Todo item, THE system SHALL save it to their personal Todo list and immediately display it in their active tasks view.**

**WHEN a user creates a Todo item with an empty description, THE system SHALL display an error message and prevent saving until valid content is provided.**

**WHEN a user creates a Todo item, THE system SHALL automatically assign a unique identifier and timestamp for tracking purposes.**

### 3.2 Todo Item Management

**WHEN a user wants to edit an existing Todo item, THE system SHALL allow them to click on the item and modify the description while maintaining the original creation timestamp.**

**WHEN a user marks a Todo item as complete, THE system SHALL visually indicate the completion status and move the item to a completed section or strike-through the text.**

**WHEN a user marks a completed Todo item as incomplete, THE system SHALL restore it to the active tasks view and remove completion indicators.**

**WHEN a user wants to delete a Todo item, THE system SHALL provide a delete option and remove the item permanently from their list upon confirmation.**

### 3.3 Todo List Display

**WHEN a user accesses their Todo dashboard, THE system SHALL display their active (incomplete) Todo items in a clear, organized list format.**

**THE system SHALL show completed Todo items in a separate section or with distinct visual styling to distinguish them from active tasks.**

**WHEN a user has many Todo items (more than 20), THE system SHALL provide a clean, scrollable interface that maintains performance and readability.**

## 4. User Scenarios and Workflows

### 4.1 New User Registration and First Use

**Scenario: First-Time User Registration**

1. User visits TodoApp homepage
2. User clicks "Sign Up" button
3. User enters email address and creates secure password
4. System validates email format and password strength
5. System creates account and logs user in automatically
6. System displays welcome message and empty Todo dashboard
7. User is ready to start adding their first Todo items

### 4.2 Daily Todo Management Workflow

**Scenario: Managing Daily Tasks**

1. User logs into TodoApp
2. User sees their existing Todo list from previous sessions
3. User adds new tasks for the day using the input field
4. User reviews their list and marks completed items as done
5. User edits descriptions of tasks that need clarification
6. User deletes tasks that are no longer relevant
7. User logs out, knowing their progress is saved

### 4.3 Todo Completion and Progress Tracking

**Scenario: Completing Tasks Throughout the Day**

1. User reviews their active Todo list
2. User works on a specific task
3. User marks the task as complete when finished
4. User sees visual feedback confirming completion
5. User can still see completed tasks for reference
6. User can unmark completed tasks if needed
7. Progress is automatically saved and synchronized

## 5. Business Rules and Data Validation

### 5.1 Todo Item Validation Rules

**WHEN a user creates a Todo item, THE system SHALL enforce the following rules:**
- Description must be between 1 and 200 characters
- Description cannot be purely whitespace
- Only printable characters are allowed
- Unique system-generated ID is automatically assigned

**WHEN a user edits a Todo item, THE system SHALL validate that:**
- Updated description meets all creation validation rules
- Original creation timestamp is preserved
- User ownership is verified before allowing edits

### 5.2 User Account Validation Rules

**WHEN a user registers, THE system SHALL validate that:**
- Email address is in valid format (user@domain.com)
- Password meets minimum security requirements (8+ characters)
- Email address is not already registered in the system

**WHEN a user logs in, THE system SHALL verify that:**
- Email address exists in the system
- Password matches the stored encrypted password
- Account status is active (not suspended or deleted)

### 5.3 Data Integrity Rules

**THE system SHALL enforce the following data integrity requirements:**
- Each user can only access and modify their own Todo items
- Todo items are permanently deleted when explicitly removed by the user
- Completed status changes are timestamped for audit purposes
- User session data is encrypted and secure

## 6. Error Handling and Recovery

### 6.1 Authentication Error Handling

**WHEN login fails due to invalid credentials, THE system SHALL display a clear error message and allow retry without account lockout.**

**WHEN registration fails due to duplicate email, THE system SHALL inform the user that the email is already registered and suggest logging in instead.**

**WHEN session expires during Todo operations, THE system SHALL save any pending changes and redirect to login with a friendly message.**

### 6.2 Todo Operation Error Handling

**WHEN saving a Todo item fails due to system error, THE system SHALL display an error message and preserve the user's input for retry.**

**WHEN deleting a Todo item fails, THE system SHALL show an error message and maintain the item in its current state.**

**WHEN network connectivity is lost, THE system SHALL queue user actions and retry when connection is restored, showing appropriate status indicators.**

### 6.3 System Error Recovery

**WHEN database connections fail, THE system SHALL attempt reconnection and provide users with status updates while maintaining data integrity.**

**WHEN unexpected system errors occur, THE system SHALL log the error details and present users with a friendly error message and suggested actions.**

## 7. Security Requirements

### 7.1 Authentication Security

**THE system SHALL store user passwords using industry-standard hashing algorithms and never store passwords in plain text.**

**THE system SHALL use secure session management with encrypted tokens and automatic expiration.**

**THE system SHALL validate user permissions before allowing access to Todo data and enforce data isolation between users.**

### 7.2 Data Protection

**THE system SHALL encrypt all user data in transit using HTTPS/TLS protocols.**

**THE system SHALL implement proper access controls ensuring users can only access their own Todo items.**

**THE system SHALL follow secure coding practices to prevent common vulnerabilities like SQL injection and cross-site scripting.**

## 8. Performance Requirements

### 8.1 Response Time Standards

**WHEN a user logs in, THE system SHALL complete authentication and display the dashboard within 2 seconds.**

**WHEN a user creates a new Todo item, THE system SHALL save it and update the display within 1 second.**

**WHEN a user marks a Todo item as complete, THE system SHALL update the status and visual indicators within 800 milliseconds.**

**WHEN a user loads their Todo list, THE system SHALL display the initial view within 2 seconds for lists up to 100 items.**

### 8.2 Scalability Requirements

**THE system SHALL support at least 100 concurrent users performing Todo operations simultaneously.**

**THE system SHALL handle Todo lists containing up to 1,000 items per user while maintaining acceptable performance.**

**WHEN the system experiences high load, THE system SHALL prioritize critical Todo operations and provide appropriate user feedback.**

## 9. Data Management Requirements

### 9.1 Data Storage

**THE system SHALL store the following Todo item data:**
- Unique identifier (system-generated)
- User ID (foreign key to user account)
- Description text
- Creation timestamp
- Completion status (boolean)
- Completion timestamp (if completed)
- Last modification timestamp

**THE system SHALL store the following user account data:**
- User ID (unique primary key)
- Email address (unique)
- Encrypted password hash
- Account creation timestamp
- Last login timestamp
- Account status (active/inactive)

### 9.2 Data Retention and Backup

**THE system SHALL implement automatic data backup procedures to prevent data loss.**

**WHEN users delete their Todo items, THE system SHALL permanently remove them from the active database.**

**THE system SHALL maintain data integrity through proper transaction management and error recovery procedures.**

## 10. User Interface Requirements

### 10.1 Core Interface Elements

**THE system SHALL provide a clean, intuitive interface with the following essential elements:**
- Login/Registration form for new and returning users
- Todo input field for adding new tasks
- Todo list display showing active and completed items
- Checkbox or button to mark items complete/incomplete
- Edit option for modifying Todo descriptions
- Delete option for removing Todo items
- Logout functionality

### 10.2 User Experience Standards

**THE system SHALL provide immediate visual feedback for all user actions within 100 milliseconds.**

**THE system SHALL use clear, consistent visual styling that works well on both desktop and mobile devices.**

**THE system SHALL maintain responsive design principles to ensure usability across different screen sizes.**

## 11. Technical Implementation Guidelines

### 11.1 System Architecture

**THE system SHALL use a modern, scalable backend architecture with proper separation of concerns.**

**THE system SHALL implement RESTful API design for Todo operations and user authentication.**

**THE system SHALL use a reliable database system with proper indexing for efficient Todo data retrieval.**

### 11.2 Technology Stack Recommendations

**Backend Technology**: TypeScript with NestJS framework for robust server-side development

**Database**: PostgreSQL or MySQL for reliable data storage and ACID compliance

**Authentication**: JWT tokens with secure refresh token implementation

**API Design**: RESTful endpoints with proper HTTP status codes and error handling

**Security**: HTTPS/TLS encryption, password hashing, input validation, and SQL injection prevention

## 12. Testing and Quality Assurance

### 12.1 Functional Testing Requirements

**THE system SHALL undergo comprehensive testing of all Todo CRUD operations to ensure reliability.**

**THE system SHALL test user registration and authentication flows under various scenarios including edge cases.**

**THE system SHALL validate data integrity and user isolation through security testing.**

### 12.2 Performance Testing Requirements

**THE system SHALL be tested under simulated load conditions to verify response time requirements.**

**THE system SHALL undergo stress testing to ensure stability under high user loads.**

**THE system SHALL be tested across different browsers and devices to ensure cross-platform compatibility.**

## 13. Success Criteria

**TodoApp SHALL be considered successful when it meets the following criteria:**

1. Users can easily register, log in, and manage their personal Todo lists
2. All Todo operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete) work reliably within specified response times
3. The system maintains data security and user privacy through proper authentication and access controls
4. Users experience a clean, intuitive interface that makes task management simple and efficient
5. The system performs well under normal usage patterns and maintains reliability during peak loads
6. Users can access their Todo data consistently across different devices and sessions
7. The application handles errors gracefully and provides clear feedback to users

## 14. Implementation Priorities

### Phase 1: Core Functionality (Essential)
- User registration and authentication
- Basic Todo item creation, editing, and deletion
- Marking Todo items as complete/incomplete
- User session management
- Basic error handling

### Phase 2: Enhancement (Recommended)
- Improved user interface with better visual feedback
- Data validation and input sanitization
- Performance optimization
- Comprehensive error handling
- Security hardening

### Phase 3: Advanced Features (Optional)
- Search and filtering capabilities
- Todo categories or tags
- Due dates and reminders
- Bulk operations
- Data export/import

## Conclusion

This requirements analysis provides a comprehensive foundation for building a TodoApp with minimum but essential functionality. The specifications focus on core task management capabilities while ensuring user security, system reliability, and optimal performance. By following these requirements, backend developers can create a production-ready Todo list application that serves users' basic task management needs effectively and efficiently.

The emphasis on simplicity, reliability, and performance ensures that the application meets the needs of users who want straightforward task management without unnecessary complexity, while maintaining the technical standards required for production deployment.

# Todo List Application - Requirements Analysis Report

## Executive Summary

This document provides comprehensive requirements analysis for a Todo List Application designed to provide users with essential task management capabilities. The application focuses on minimum functionality while ensuring robust security, scalability, and user experience. The system enables users to create, manage, and track their tasks through a web-based interface with secure user authentication and data protection.

The Todo List Application serves individual users who need a simple yet effective way to organize their daily tasks and improve personal productivity. The system prioritizes ease of use while maintaining enterprise-grade security standards and reliable performance.

## 1. Service Overview

### 1.1 Service Purpose and Vision

The Todo List Application provides users with a secure, reliable platform for managing personal tasks and improving productivity. The service focuses on essential task management functionality without unnecessary complexity, making it accessible to users of all technical backgrounds.

**Core Value Proposition:**
- Simplified task management with intuitive user interface
- Secure personal data storage and user authentication
- Reliable task tracking and status management
- Cross-platform accessibility through web browser
- Fast, responsive user experience

### 1.2 Target Users

The application serves individual users who need personal task management solutions:

**Primary User Profile:**
- Individual professionals managing daily work tasks
- Students organizing assignments and study materials
- Personal users tracking household and personal responsibilities
- Users seeking simple, reliable task management without complex project management features

**User Characteristics:**
- Varying technical expertise levels
- Prefer simple, straightforward interfaces
- Need reliable task tracking capabilities
- Value security and privacy of personal task data
- Use multiple devices and expect data synchronization

### 1.3 Core Value Proposition

**Essential Task Management:**
- Create, edit, and delete tasks with minimal friction
- Mark tasks as complete/incomplete with simple interactions
- Organize tasks in logical, easy-to-navigate structure
- Real-time updates and synchronization across devices

**Security and Privacy:**
- Secure user authentication with industry-standard practices
- Personal task data protected with encryption and access controls
- User privacy respected with minimal data collection
- Compliant with data protection regulations

**User Experience:**
- Intuitive interface requiring no training or documentation
- Fast response times for all user interactions
- Reliable system availability and data persistence
- Responsive design working on all device sizes

### 1.4 Success Metrics

**User Engagement Metrics:**
- Daily active users maintaining consistent task management habits
- User retention rates showing long-term adoption
- Task completion rates indicating effective productivity improvement
- User satisfaction scores reflecting positive experience

**Technical Performance Metrics:**
- Application response times under 2 seconds for all operations
- 99.9% system uptime ensuring reliable access
- Zero data loss incidents with robust backup systems
- Secure authentication with no security breach incidents

## 2. User Actors and Authentication

### 2.1 User Actor Definitions

The system implements a role-based user model supporting individual users with administrative oversight capabilities:

**Standard User Actor:**
- Individual users managing personal tasks
- Create, read, update, and delete their own tasks
- Manage personal account settings and preferences
- View personal task history and completion statistics
- Access task management features through web interface

**Administrator Actor:**
- System administrators managing application functionality
- Access user management capabilities and system monitoring
- View system-wide statistics and usage analytics
- Manage user accounts and resolve technical issues
- Access security logs and audit trails for compliance

### 2.2 Authentication Flow Requirements

**User Registration Process:**
- WHEN users create new accounts, THE system SHALL collect email address and secure password
- THE system SHALL validate email format and password strength requirements
- THE system SHALL create user records with unique identifiers and timestamps
- WHEN registration is successful, THE system SHALL automatically log users into their new accounts
- THE system SHALL send email verification requests requiring user confirmation

**User Login Process:**
- WHEN users enter credentials, THE system SHALL validate email format and password strength
- THE system SHALL verify credentials against secure user database
- WHEN authentication succeeds, THE system SHALL issue secure JWT tokens
- WHEN authentication fails, THE system SHALL provide clear error messages without revealing sensitive information
- THE system SHALL implement rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks

**Session Management:**
- WHEN users authenticate successfully, THE system SHALL create secure sessions with appropriate expiration
- THE system SHALL automatically renew sessions for active users
- WHEN users log out, THE system SHALL immediately invalidate all session tokens
- THE system SHALL implement automatic logout after periods of inactivity

### 2.3 Permission Matrix

**Standard User Permissions:**
- Create new tasks with title, description, and status
- Read and view all personal tasks with filtering and sorting options
- Update existing tasks including status changes and content modifications
- Delete personal tasks with confirmation requirements
- Manage personal account settings and preferences
- View personal task statistics and completion history

**Administrator Permissions:**
- All standard user permissions for system testing
- Access user management interface for administrative functions
- View system-wide statistics and performance metrics
- Access security logs and audit trails for compliance monitoring
- Manage user accounts including password resets and account status changes

**Permission Enforcement:**
- THE system SHALL validate user permissions for every data operation
- THE system SHALL prevent unauthorized access to other users' tasks
- THE system SHALL implement role-based access control with least privilege principle
- WHEN permission violations occur, THE system SHALL log security events and return appropriate error responses

### 2.4 JWT Token Management

**Token Structure and Security:**
- JWT tokens SHALL contain user identification, role information, and expiration timestamps
- Token payloads SHALL include userId (UUID), role (user/admin), and issuedAt/expiration timestamps
- THE system SHALL use secure token signing with industry-standard algorithms
- Refresh tokens SHALL have longer expiration periods than access tokens

**Token Lifecycle:**
- Access tokens SHALL expire after 15 minutes for security
- Refresh tokens SHALL expire after 7 days to maintain user sessions
- THE system SHALL automatically refresh tokens before expiration
- THE system SHALL invalidate all tokens immediately upon user logout

**Token Storage and Transmission:**
- THE system SHALL transmit tokens via secure HTTP headers
- THE system SHALL store refresh tokens in secure, httpOnly cookies
- THE system SHALL require HTTPS for all token transmission
- THE system SHALL implement token rotation for enhanced security

## 3. Functional Requirements

### 3.1 Core Todo Operations

**Task Creation Requirements:**
- WHEN users create tasks, THE system SHALL require minimum task title with optional description
- THE system SHALL automatically assign unique identifiers and timestamps to new tasks
- THE system SHALL set initial task status as 'pending' by default
- WHEN task creation succeeds, THE system SHALL immediately display the new task to users
- THE system SHALL validate task data for appropriate length and content constraints

**Task Reading and Display:**
- WHEN users view tasks, THE system SHALL display all personal tasks with current status
- THE system SHALL provide filtering options for task status (pending, completed)
- THE system SHALL support sorting tasks by creation date, due date, or priority
- THE system SHALL implement pagination for users with large numbers of tasks
- WHEN tasks are displayed, THE system SHALL show task status, creation date, and last modification

**Task Update Operations:**
- WHEN users modify tasks, THE system SHALL allow updates to title, description, and status
- THE system SHALL maintain task history including creation and modification timestamps
- THE system SHALL validate update requests ensuring users can only modify their own tasks
- WHEN task updates succeed, THE system SHALL immediately reflect changes in user interface
- THE system SHALL implement optimistic locking to prevent concurrent modification conflicts

**Task Deletion Operations:**
- WHEN users delete tasks, THE system SHALL require confirmation to prevent accidental deletions
- THE system SHALL permanently remove deleted tasks from the database
- THE system SHALL update task statistics and completion metrics after deletions
- WHEN deletions occur, THE system SHALL log audit events for administrative oversight
- THE system SHALL provide task recovery options within defined time periods

### 3.2 User Management Functions

**Account Management:**
- WHEN users access account settings, THE system SHALL allow password changes with current password verification
- THE system SHALL permit email address updates requiring email verification
- THE system SHALL provide account deletion options with data removal confirmations
- THE system SHALL maintain user preferences including task display preferences
- WHEN account changes occur, THE system SHALL send appropriate email notifications

**Personal Data Management:**
- THE system SHALL provide data export functionality for users to download their task data
- THE system SHALL implement data deletion procedures compliant with privacy regulations
- THE system SHALL maintain user privacy through minimal data collection practices
- WHEN users request data deletion, THE system SHALL remove all personal information within defined timeframes

### 3.3 Data Validation Rules

**Task Data Validation:**
- Task titles SHALL be required and limited to 200 characters maximum
- Task descriptions SHALL be optional and limited to 1000 characters maximum
- THE system SHALL validate task status values to ensure only valid status options
- THE system SHALL reject tasks with inappropriate content using content filtering
- WHEN validation fails, THE system SHALL provide specific error messages indicating validation issues

**User Input Sanitization:**
- THE system SHALL sanitize all user inputs to prevent security vulnerabilities
- THE system SHALL validate email formats using standard email validation rules
- THE system SHALL enforce password complexity requirements for security
- THE system SHALL implement input length limits to prevent buffer overflow attacks
- WHEN input validation fails, THE system SHALL reject requests with appropriate error responses

### 3.4 Business Logic Requirements

**Task Status Management:**
- Tasks SHALL have distinct statuses: 'pending', 'in_progress', 'completed', 'cancelled'
- THE system SHALL allow status transitions following defined business rules
- THE system SHALL maintain task completion history and timestamps
- WHEN tasks are marked complete, THE system SHALL calculate completion statistics
- THE system SHALL support bulk status updates for task management efficiency

**Data Integrity Requirements:**
- THE system SHALL maintain referential integrity between users and their tasks
- THE system SHALL implement data backup and recovery procedures
- THE system SHALL prevent data corruption through transaction management
- WHEN data integrity issues occur, THE system SHALL implement error recovery procedures

## 4. User Scenarios

### 4.1 New User Registration Flow

**Scenario 1: First-Time User Registration**

WHEN a new user accesses the Todo List Application for the first time,
THE user SHALL be presented with a registration form requiring email address and password,
THE system SHALL validate email format and password strength requirements,
WHEN the user submits valid registration information,
THE system SHALL create a new user account and automatically log the user in,
THE system SHALL display a welcome screen with instructions for creating the first task,
THE user SHALL then be able to immediately start creating and managing tasks.

**User Experience Flow:**
1. User navigates to application URL
2. User clicks "Sign Up" button on login screen
3. User enters email address and creates secure password
4. System validates input and creates user account
5. System automatically logs user in and redirects to main task interface
6. User sees empty task list with prompt to create first task
7. User creates initial task and sees immediate confirmation

### 4.2 User Login Process

**Scenario 2: Returning User Login**

WHEN a returning user accesses the Todo List Application,
THE user SHALL be presented with login form requiring email and password,
WHEN the user enters correct credentials,
THE system SHALL validate credentials and issue secure authentication tokens,
THE system SHALL redirect the user to their personal task dashboard,
THE user SHALL see all their existing tasks with current status information.

**User Experience Flow:**
1. User navigates to application URL
2. User enters email address and password
3. System validates credentials and authenticates user
4. System creates secure session and issues JWT tokens
5. User is redirected to main task management interface
6. User sees personalized dashboard with their tasks

### 4.3 Todo Creation Journey

**Scenario 3: Creating a New Task**

WHEN a logged-in user wants to create a new task,
THE user SHALL click "Add Task" button or use keyboard shortcut,
THE system SHALL display task creation form with title and description fields,
WHEN the user enters task information and clicks "Create",
THE system SHALL validate task data and create the task with unique identifier,
THE system SHALL immediately display the new task in the user's task list,
THE user SHALL see confirmation of successful task creation.

**User Experience Flow:**
1. User clicks "Add New Task" button in main interface
2. System displays task creation form with input fields
3. User enters task title and optional description
4. User clicks "Create Task" button
5. System validates input and creates task record
6. System updates task list display with new task
7. User sees confirmation message and new task in list

### 4.4 Todo Management Workflows

**Scenario 4: Managing Task Status**

WHEN a user wants to mark a task as complete,
THE user SHALL click the checkbox or status button next to the task,
THE system SHALL update task status and record completion timestamp,
THE system SHALL immediately reflect status change in user interface,
THE system SHALL update task completion statistics and progress indicators.

**User Experience Flow:**
1. User sees task list with various task statuses
2. User clicks checkbox to mark task as complete
3. System updates task status in database
4. System updates visual display to show completed status
5. User sees updated statistics and progress indicators
6. Task moves to completed section or gets filtered appropriately

**Scenario 5: Editing Existing Tasks**

WHEN a user wants to modify task information,
THE user SHALL click edit button or double-click task title,
THE system SHALL display task editing interface with current task data,
WHEN the user modifies task information and saves changes,
THE system SHALL validate updated data and save modifications,
THE system SHALL immediately reflect changes in the task list display.

**User Experience Flow:**
1. User clicks edit button on existing task
2. System displays editing form with current task data
3. User modifies task title, description, or status
4. User clicks "Save Changes" button
5. System validates and saves updated task information
6. System updates task list display with modified task
7. User sees confirmation of successful update

### 4.5 Error Recovery Scenarios

**Scenario 6: Handling Network Connectivity Issues**

WHEN a user experiences network connectivity problems,
THE system SHALL detect connection failures and display appropriate error messages,
THE system SHALL implement automatic retry mechanisms for failed operations,
WHEN network connectivity is restored,
THE system SHALL synchronize pending changes and update user interface,
THE user SHALL be informed of successful synchronization or any conflicts requiring attention.

**User Experience Flow:**
1. User attempts to create or modify task while offline
2. System detects connection failure and prevents operation
3. System displays connectivity error message to user
4. User may continue working with local data cache
5. When connection is restored, system synchronizes changes
6. User receives confirmation of successful synchronization

**Scenario 7: Handling Authentication Token Expiration**

WHEN user authentication tokens expire during active use,
THE system SHALL detect token expiration and automatically refresh tokens,
THE system SHALL continue user session without requiring re-authentication,
WHEN token refresh fails, THE system SHALL prompt user to re-authenticate,
THE user SHALL be able to continue task management after re-authentication.

**User Experience Flow:**
1. User is actively using application when token expires
2. System detects expiration and automatically refreshes tokens
3. User continues working without interruption
4. If refresh fails, system displays authentication prompt
5. User re-enters credentials and regains access
6. User returns to previous task management interface

## 5. Business Rules

### 5.1 Todo Creation Rules

**Task Creation Constraints:**
- THE system SHALL require non-empty task titles with maximum 200 characters
- THE system SHALL allow optional task descriptions with maximum 1000 characters
- THE system SHALL automatically assign unique identifiers to all new tasks
- THE system SHALL set default status to 'pending' for all new tasks
- THE system SHALL record creation timestamps for audit and sorting purposes

**Task Content Validation:**
- THE system SHALL reject tasks containing prohibited content or spam
- THE system SHALL validate character encoding and prevent injection attacks
- THE system SHALL implement content length limits to prevent database issues
- THE system SHALL sanitize input to remove potentially harmful content
- WHEN validation fails, THE system SHALL provide specific error messages

**User Ownership Rules:**
- THE system SHALL assign all tasks to authenticated user who creates them
- THE system SHALL prevent users from creating tasks for other users
- THE system SHALL enforce data isolation ensuring users only see their own tasks
- THE system SHALL implement user-specific task access controls

### 5.2 Edit and Delete Constraints

**Task Modification Rules:**
- THE system SHALL allow users to modify only their own tasks
- THE system SHALL maintain task modification history and timestamps
- THE system SHALL prevent modification of tasks after deletion
- THE system SHALL implement optimistic locking to prevent concurrent modifications
