# TodoApp Data Management Requirements

## Document Overview

This document defines comprehensive data management requirements for the TodoApp system, establishing the business rules, lifecycle policies, and integrity requirements for managing user and Todo data throughout the system.

The TodoApp system is designed to provide users with a personal task management solution while ensuring secure, reliable, and organized data handling. These requirements establish the foundation for building a production-ready Todo application that prioritizes user privacy, data integrity, and seamless user experience.

## Business Context and Data Needs

The TodoApp system manages two primary data domains: user account data and Todo item data. Each user maintains their own private Todo list with full control over their data, while administrators have system-wide oversight capabilities. The data management approach prioritizes user privacy, data integrity, and efficient organization to support a streamlined Todo management experience.

### Core Business Value Proposition

WHEN users choose to manage their tasks through TodoApp, THE system SHALL provide them with:
- Secure and private task management with complete data ownership
- Reliable data persistence ensuring no task loss due to system failures
- Efficient organization capabilities allowing users to structure their tasks according to their workflow
- Comprehensive backup and recovery solutions providing peace of mind
- Cross-session data continuity ensuring access from any device

### Data Privacy and Security Requirements

WHEN users store their personal task information in TodoApp, THE system SHALL:
- Maintain complete isolation between different users' data
- Encrypt all stored user information to prevent unauthorized access
- Provide users with full control over their data including export and deletion capabilities
- Implement secure authentication mechanisms preventing unauthorized account access
- Log all data access and modification events for security audit purposes

## 1. Data Models and Relationships

### Core Data Entities

#### User Data Requirements

WHEN a user registers for an account, THE system SHALL store the following user account information:
- User identification information including unique user ID, email address, and username
- Authentication credentials including encrypted password and password reset tokens
- User profile information including display name, account creation date, and last login timestamp
- Account status information including active status, suspension flags, and email verification status
- User preferences and settings including timezone selection and notification preferences

WHEN users update their account information, THE system SHALL:
- Validate all profile updates against business rules and format requirements
- Update modification timestamps to track account change history
- Require proper authentication for sensitive changes such as email address or password modifications
- Send confirmation notifications to users when critical account information changes
- Maintain complete audit trails of all profile modifications for security purposes

#### Todo Item Data Requirements

WHEN users create new Todo items, THE system SHALL store the following Todo item information:
- Todo identification including unique Todo ID and automatic user association
- Todo content information including title, description, and detailed notes
- Todo status and state information including completed flag, completion date, and priority level
- Todo organization data including category assignment, tags, and optional due date
- Todo lifecycle timestamps including creation date, last modification date, and last accessed date
- Todo metadata including created by user information and last modified by user tracking

WHEN users modify existing Todo items, THE system SHALL:
- Preserve original creation timestamps while updating modification timestamps
- Allow comprehensive modifications including title, description, status, category, tags, and due date
- Validate all changes against established business rules and system constraints
- Require ownership verification before allowing any modifications to Todo items
- Log all Todo item changes with complete before/after state information for audit purposes

#### Authentication and Session Data Requirements

WHEN users authenticate with the system, THE system SHALL store the following authentication-related data:
- User login session information including session tokens and expiration timestamps
- Security event logs including login attempts, password changes, and security breach tracking
- Password reset and account verification tokens with proper expiration date management
- Account lockout tracking including failed attempt counts and security flags

### Data Relationship Structure

#### User-Todo Relationship Requirements

WHEN users interact with their Todo items, THE system SHALL establish and maintain:
- A one-to-many relationship where each user owns multiple Todo items and each Todo item belongs to exactly one user
- Complete data isolation ensuring users can only access and modify their own Todo items
- Automatic association of all Todo items with the authenticated user's account
- Administrative override capabilities allowing authorized administrators to access any user's Todo items

#### Authentication-User Relationship Requirements

WHEN users maintain active sessions, THE system SHALL:
- Establish session-based authentication where each session references a valid user account
- Allow multiple simultaneous sessions for a single user across different devices or browsers
- Implement automatic session expiration based on security policies and user inactivity
- Verify user authentication status for all Todo operations and account management functions

### Data Organization Requirements

#### User Data Isolation Requirements

WHEN users access the system, THE system SHALL ensure:
- Complete data isolation between different users preventing cross-user data access
- Private user authentication data that is not accessible to other users or unauthorized parties
- Controlled cross-user data access requiring explicit administrative authorization
- User-specific search and filtering returning only data belonging to the requesting user

#### Administrative Data Access Requirements

WHEN administrative users access the system for moderation and management, THE system SHALL provide:
- Read-only access to all user account information for administrative review
- Full access to all Todo items across all users for content moderation purposes
- Limited administrative functions including user suspension and account management capabilities
- Detailed audit trails documenting all administrative actions performed on user data

## 2. Data Lifecycle Management

### Data Creation Requirements

#### User Account Creation Process

WHEN a new user successfully registers for an account, THE system SHALL:
- Generate a unique user identifier immediately upon successful registration completion
- Store encrypted password securely and require email verification before account activation
- Create initial user profile with default preferences and system settings
- Initialize user-specific data structures and storage allocation for Todo items
- Log complete account creation event with timestamp, source information, and user details

#### Todo Item Creation Process

WHEN a user creates a new Todo item through the system interface, THE system SHALL:
- Generate a unique Todo identifier automatically linked to the user's account
- Require Todo title with minimum character requirements to ensure meaningful task description
- Optionally accept Todo description, category, tags, and due date information
- Set initial status to incomplete and record creation timestamp for tracking purposes
- Associate the new Todo item with the authenticated user's account automatically
- Validate all input data against established business rules before permanent storage

### Data Modification Requirements

#### User Profile Updates

WHEN a user updates their profile information through account settings, THE system SHALL:
- Validate all modified fields against established business rules and format requirements
- Update the modification timestamp to reflect the most recent profile change
- Require proper authentication for sensitive changes such as email address or password
- Send user notifications confirming successful profile updates and changes made
- Maintain comprehensive audit trails of all profile changes with before/after states

#### Todo Item Updates

WHEN a user modifies an existing Todo item, THE system SHALL:
- Preserve the original creation timestamp while updating modification timestamp
- Allow comprehensive modifications to title, description, status, category, tags, and due date
- Validate all changes against business rules and system constraints before storage
- Require ownership verification to ensure users can only modify their own Todo items
- Log all Todo item changes with complete before/after state information for audit purposes

### Data Deletion Requirements

#### User-Initiated Deletion

WHEN a user initiates deletion of their account or Todo items, THE system SHALL:
- Require explicit user confirmation before executing permanent deletion of data
- Provide soft-delete option with configurable grace period for data recovery purposes
- Remove all associated Todo items automatically when user account deletion occurs
- Generate final data export option for users before permanent deletion execution
- Log all deletion events with user identification, deletion reason, and timestamp

#### Administrative Deletion

WHEN an administrative user initiates deletion of user data, THE system SHALL:
- Require elevated authentication levels and comprehensive audit trail documentation
- Provide appropriate notification to affected users when deletion is legally required
- Maintain detailed deletion logs for compliance purposes and potential data recovery
- Execute deletion process through secure administrative interface with proper authorization

## 3. Data Retention Policies

### User Account Data Retention

#### Active User Data Retention

THE system SHALL maintain user account data while accounts remain active according to the following rules:
- User account information SHALL be retained indefinitely while the account remains active and in good standing
- Authentication data SHALL be maintained with secure encryption protection throughout active use
- User profile and preference data SHALL be preserved to maintain full account functionality
- Session data SHALL be automatically cleaned up when sessions expire to maintain system performance

#### Inactive Account Data Retention

WHEN user accounts become inactive, THE system SHALL:
- Retain account data for a minimum of twelve months after the user's last login activity
- Provide grace period notifications for account reactivation before executing data purging
- Send reactivation reminder emails and notifications before permanent data deletion
- Archive inactive account data with reduced system resource usage for cost efficiency

### Todo Item Data Retention

#### Active User Todo Retention

THE system SHALL preserve Todo items while users have active accounts following these policies:
- Completed Todo items SHALL be retained indefinitely unless explicitly deleted by the user
- Incomplete Todo items SHALL be maintained until user deletion or completion action occurs
- Todo metadata and timestamps SHALL be preserved for historical tracking and user reference
- Bulk operations on Todo data SHALL remain under complete user control without automatic deletion

#### Deleted Todo Recovery

THE system SHALL provide temporary recovery capability for accidentally deleted items:
- Deleted Todo items SHALL be recoverable for thirty days after deletion date
- System SHALL provide user interface for managing recoverable items with clear recovery options
- Data purging after recovery period SHALL be permanent and complete with no recovery possible
- Recovery process SHALL restore original Todo status, metadata, and all associated information

### Session and Authentication Data Retention

#### Session Data Management

THE system SHALL manage session data with the following retention policies:
- Active session tokens SHALL expire according to established security policy time limits
- Expired session data SHALL be automatically purged from system to maintain performance
- Failed login attempts SHALL be logged and automatically cleaned up after appropriate retention period
- Password reset tokens SHALL expire within twenty-four hours of generation for security

#### Security Event Retention

THE system SHALL maintain security event data for compliance and audit purposes:
- Authentication attempts SHALL be logged with complete timestamps and source information
- Security events SHALL be retained for minimum ninety days for compliance requirements
- Administrative actions SHALL be logged permanently for audit and regulatory purposes
- System security logs SHALL be maintained and accessible for authorized security reviews

## 4. Backup and Recovery Requirements

### User Data Backup Strategy

#### Automated Backup Requirements

THE system SHALL implement comprehensive data backup procedures with the following specifications:
- User account data SHALL be backed up daily with incremental updates to minimize system impact
- Todo item data SHALL be synchronized with user account backups to maintain data consistency
- Authentication and session data SHALL be included in daily backup processes for complete recovery
- Backup processes SHALL run automatically without user intervention or manual oversight

#### Backup Data Protection

THE system SHALL ensure backup data security and integrity through these measures:
- Backup files SHALL be encrypted using industry-standard encryption protocols
- Backup storage SHALL be geographically separate from production data for disaster protection
- Access to backup data SHALL be restricted to authorized personnel only with proper authentication
- Backup integrity SHALL be verified regularly through automated checks and validation processes

### Disaster Recovery Requirements

#### System Recovery Objectives

THE system SHALL establish clear and measurable recovery objectives:
- Recovery Time Objective (RTO) SHALL be maximum four hours for complete system restoration
- Recovery Point Objective (RPO) SHALL be maximum twenty-four hours of potential data loss
- User data recovery SHALL preserve all user Todo items and account information completely
- System functionality SHALL be fully restored following documented recovery procedures

#### User Data Recovery Process

WHEN system recovery is required due to disaster or failure, THE system SHALL:
- Restore user account data from the most recent available backup with verification
- Recreate all user Todo items with original timestamps, status, and metadata intact
- Validate complete data integrity after recovery completion and before system restoration
- Notify users of any data restoration limitations or gaps in the recovery process

### Data Export and Portability

#### User Data Export Requirements

THE system SHALL provide users with comprehensive data portability options:
- Users SHALL be able to export their complete Todo list in machine-readable standard format
- Export SHALL include all Todo metadata, timestamps, completion status, and organizational information
- Account information export SHALL be available upon user request with appropriate privacy protections
- Export process SHALL maintain user privacy and data security throughout transfer

#### Bulk Data Operations

THE system SHALL support administrative bulk data operations for legitimate purposes:
- Administrators SHALL be able to export anonymized user data for system analysis and improvement
- Bulk operations SHALL include comprehensive logging and audit trails for compliance
- Large-scale data exports SHALL be processed securely and efficiently with progress tracking
- Users SHALL be notified of any administrative data access or export activity as required

## 5. Data Integrity Rules

### User Data Validation Requirements

#### Account Information Validation

THE system SHALL validate all user account data at entry and during updates according to these rules:
- Email addresses SHALL conform to valid email format requirements and domain validation
- Password requirements SHALL meet minimum security standards and complexity requirements
- Username SHALL be unique within the system and meet established format requirements
- Required profile fields SHALL be completed before account activation and system access

#### Todo Item Data Validation

THE system SHALL validate all Todo item data according to business rules and constraints:
- Todo title SHALL be required and meet minimum character requirements for meaningful description
- Todo description SHALL be validated for appropriate content length and character limits
- Due dates SHALL be validated for logical date sequences and business rule compliance
- Category and tag assignments SHALL be validated against user-authorized and available options

### Data Consistency Requirements

#### User Data Consistency

THE system SHALL maintain data consistency across all user interactions and system components:
- User authentication status SHALL be consistent across all system components and interfaces
- User preferences and settings SHALL be applied consistently throughout the entire application
- Todo item status SHALL be synchronized across all user interfaces and access points
- User session data SHALL expire consistently across all system access points and devices

#### Cross-User Data Integrity

THE system SHALL prevent cross-user data contamination through these protective measures:
- User Todo lists SHALL be completely isolated from other users' data and operations
- User search results SHALL only return data belonging to the authenticated requesting user
- Administrative access SHALL not interfere with normal user data operations or privacy
- Data aggregation operations SHALL respect user privacy boundaries and data isolation

### Error Recovery and Data Correction

#### Data Error Detection

THE system SHALL implement robust error detection mechanisms for data integrity:
- Data validation SHALL occur at all data entry and modification points throughout the system
- System SHALL detect and flag inconsistent data states automatically during routine operations
- User data integrity SHALL be verified during routine system operations and maintenance
- Backup verification SHALL include comprehensive data integrity checks and validation

#### Data Correction Procedures

WHEN data integrity issues are detected during system operations, THE system SHALL:
- Automatically flag corrupted or inconsistent data for administrator review and resolution
- Provide user notification when personal data integrity issues affect their account
- Maintain comprehensive audit trails of all data correction actions performed on the system
- Restore data from verified backup when necessary for complete data recovery and integrity

### Data Access Control and Privacy

#### User Privacy Protection

THE system SHALL implement strict privacy controls and data protection measures:
- Users SHALL only access their own data unless explicitly authorized by system administrators
- Administrative access to user data SHALL be logged, monitored, and available for audit review
- Data sharing between users SHALL require explicit user consent and proper authorization
- Privacy settings SHALL be enforced consistently across all system components and interfaces

#### Secure Data Handling

THE system SHALL maintain secure data handling practices throughout all operations:
- All user data SHALL be encrypted in both storage and transmission to prevent unauthorized access
- Data access SHALL be logged for security audit purposes and compliance requirements
- Sensitive operations SHALL require appropriate authentication levels and authorization verification
- Data disposal SHALL follow secure deletion protocols meeting industry security standards

## Conclusion

These data management requirements establish a comprehensive framework for managing user and Todo data within the TodoApp system. The requirements prioritize user privacy, data integrity, and system reliability while providing clear guidelines for data lifecycle management, retention policies, and backup procedures.

Implementation of these requirements will ensure that user data is properly protected, managed, and available throughout the system's operational lifecycle. The document provides backend developers with clear specifications for implementing robust data management capabilities that meet both functional requirements and regulatory compliance needs.

The TodoApp system will deliver users a reliable, secure, and efficient task management experience with complete data ownership and privacy protection, establishing trust and confidence in the platform for long-term task management needs.

# Todo List Application Requirements Analysis Report

## Service Overview

### Service Purpose and Vision

The Todo List Application is a web-based task management system designed to help users organize, track, and complete their daily tasks efficiently. The service provides a simple yet comprehensive platform where users can create, manage, and monitor their personal todo items with secure authentication and data persistence.

**Core Value Proposition:**
- Streamlined task creation and management
- Secure user authentication and data protection
- Real-time task status updates
- Intuitive user interface for maximum productivity
- Reliable data persistence across sessions

**Target Users:**
- Individual users managing personal tasks
- Small teams requiring basic task coordination
- Users seeking simple but effective task management

**Business Model:**
The application operates on a freemium model with basic task management features available to all users and advanced features for premium users.

**Success Metrics:**
- User registration and retention rates
- Daily active users and session duration
- Task completion rates and user productivity metrics
- System uptime and response time performance

## User Actors and Authentication

### User Actor Definitions

**1. Regular User (Primary Actor)**
- **Purpose**: Core user who manages personal tasks
- **Capabilities**: Create, read, update, and delete personal todos
- **Permissions**: Full access to own todo items, limited system access
- **Authentication**: Email/password registration and login
- **Session Management**: JWT token-based authentication with 30-minute expiration

**2. Administrator (Secondary Actor)**
- **Purpose**: System administrator managing application-wide operations
- **Capabilities**: Monitor system performance, manage user accounts, view system analytics
- **Permissions**: Full administrative access, user management, system configuration
- **Authentication**: Enhanced security with multi-factor authentication
- **Session Management**: Extended session tokens with refresh mechanism

### Authentication Flow Requirements

**User Registration Process:**
- Email address validation required
- Password strength requirements (minimum 8 characters, mixed case, numbers)
- Automatic email verification before account activation
- Duplicate email prevention with clear error messages
- Registration timestamp tracking for audit purposes

**User Login Process:**
- Email/password credential verification
- Failed login attempt tracking (max 5 attempts before temporary lockout)
- JWT token generation upon successful authentication
- Session management with automatic token refresh
- "Remember me" functionality extending session duration

**Password Management:**
- Secure password hashing using bcrypt algorithm
- Password change functionality for authenticated users
- Password reset via secure email link with expiration
- Strong password validation and complexity requirements

**Security Requirements:**
- All passwords must be hashed using industry-standard algorithms
- JWT tokens must include user ID, email, and role information
- Session timeout after 30 minutes of inactivity
- Account lockout after 5 consecutive failed login attempts
- Secure password reset process with time-limited tokens

## Functional Requirements

### Core Todo Operations

**Todo Creation Requirements:**
- WHEN a user creates a new todo item, THE system SHALL require a title (1-200 characters)
- WHEN a user creates a todo item, THE system SHALL allow optional description field (0-1000 characters)
- WHEN a user creates a todo item, THE system SHALL automatically set completion status to false
- WHEN a user creates a todo item, THE system SHALL automatically set creation timestamp
- WHEN a user creates a todo item, THE system SHALL associate the item with the authenticated user's account

**Todo Read Operations:**
- WHEN a user requests todo list, THE system SHALL return only todos belonging to that authenticated user
- WHEN a user requests todo list, THE system SHALL return todos sorted by creation date (newest first)
- WHEN a user requests individual todo item, THE system SHALL verify ownership before returning data
- WHEN a user requests todo list, THE system SHALL include completion status and timestamps

**Todo Update Operations:**
- WHEN a user updates a todo item, THE system SHALL validate that the todo belongs to the authenticated user
- WHEN a user updates todo title, THE system SHALL enforce 1-200 character limit
- WHEN a user updates todo description, THE system SHALL enforce 0-1000 character limit
- WHEN a user marks todo as complete, THE system SHALL set completion timestamp
- WHEN a user marks todo as incomplete, THE system SHALL clear completion timestamp

**Todo Delete Operations:**
- WHEN a user deletes a todo item, THE system SHALL verify ownership before deletion
- WHEN a user deletes a todo item, THE system SHALL permanently remove the item from database
- WHEN a user deletes a todo item, THE system SHALL return success confirmation

### User Management Functions

**User Profile Management:**
- WHEN a user updates profile information, THE system SHALL validate email format and uniqueness
- WHEN a user changes password, THE system SHALL require current password verification
- WHEN a user updates profile, THE system SHALL update database and return confirmation
- WHEN a user requests profile data, THE system SHALL return non-sensitive user information

**Account Management:**
- WHEN a user requests account deletion, THE system SHALL require password confirmation
- WHEN a user deletes account, THE system SHALL remove all associated todo items
- WHEN a user deletes account, THE system SHALL permanently remove user data
- WHEN a user requests data export, THE system SHALL provide user data in JSON format

### Data Validation Rules

**Todo Item Validation:**
- Title field: Required, 1-200 characters, no HTML injection allowed
- Description field: Optional, 0-1000 characters, plain text only
- Completion status: Boolean, system-controlled
- User ownership: Automatically assigned based on authenticated user
- Creation timestamp: Automatically set by system, read-only
- Update timestamp: Automatically updated on modifications

**User Data Validation:**
- Email: Required, valid format, unique across system
- Password: Required, minimum 8 characters, mixed case, numbers, special characters
- User role: System-controlled, USER or ADMIN only
- Account status: Active, pending verification, or suspended

### Business Logic

**Todo Completion Logic:**
- WHEN a user marks todo as complete, THE system SHALL set completion timestamp to current time
- WHEN a user unmarks todo as complete, THE system SHALL clear completion timestamp
- WHEN a user edits completed todo, THE system SHALL preserve completion status unless explicitly changed
- WHEN a user creates duplicate todos, THE system SHALL allow duplicates (user decision)

**User Session Logic:**
- WHEN user logs in successfully, THE system SHALL generate JWT token with 30-minute expiration
- WHEN user makes authenticated request, THE system SHALL validate JWT token
- WHEN JWT token expires, THE system SHALL require user re-authentication
- WHEN user remains inactive for 30 minutes, THE system SHALL automatically log out user

**Permission Enforcement:**
- WHEN user accesses todos, THE system SHALL filter results by authenticated user ID
- WHEN user attempts to modify others' todos, THE system SHALL return authorization error
- WHEN admin user accesses system functions, THE system SHALL verify admin role
- WHEN unauthorized user accesses admin functions, THE system SHALL return forbidden response

## User Scenarios

### New User Registration Flow

**Scenario 1: First-Time User Registration**
- User navigates to registration page
- User enters valid email address and strong password
- User submits registration form
- System validates email uniqueness and password strength
- System creates new user account with pending verification status
- System sends verification email to user's email address
- User clicks verification link in email
- System activates user account and redirects to login page
- User logs in with verified credentials
- System generates JWT token and displays empty todo dashboard

**Scenario 2: Registration with Invalid Data**
- User enters email address already in use
- User submits registration form
- System detects duplicate email and returns error message
- User enters weak password (less than 8 characters)
- System validates password and returns strength requirement message
- User enters invalid email format
- System validates email format and returns error message
- User corrects all issues and successfully registers

### User Login Process

**Scenario 3: Successful User Login**
- User enters correct email and password
- User clicks login button
- System validates credentials against database
- System generates JWT token with user information
- System sets session cookie and redirects to dashboard
- User sees their todo list and personal information
- System logs successful login event

**Scenario 4: Failed Login Attempts**
- User enters incorrect password
- System validates and rejects credentials
- User attempts login again with wrong credentials
- System tracks failed attempts
- After 5 failed attempts, system temporarily locks account
- System sends security notification email to user
- User must wait 15 minutes or reset password to regain access

### Todo Creation Journey

**Scenario 5: Creating First Todo Item**
- User clicks "Add New Todo" button
- User enters todo title "Buy groceries"
- User optionally adds description "Milk, bread, eggs"
- User clicks save button
- System validates title and creates todo item
- System assigns unique ID and timestamps
- System displays new todo in user's list
- User sees confirmation message

**Scenario 6: Creating Multiple Todos**
- User creates todo "Complete project proposal"
- User creates todo "Schedule team meeting"
- User creates todo "Review quarterly reports"
- System creates all todos with sequential IDs
- System displays todos in chronological order
- User sees organized list of tasks

### Todo Management Workflows

**Scenario 7: Marking Todo as Complete**
- User reviews pending todo items
- User clicks checkbox next to completed task
- System updates completion status and timestamp
- System moves completed todo to bottom of list
- User sees visual confirmation of completion
- User can optionally uncheck to mark as incomplete

**Scenario 8: Editing Todo Items**
- User clicks edit button on existing todo
- User modifies title or description
- User saves changes
- System validates changes and updates database
- System updates modification timestamp
- User sees updated todo information

**Scenario 9: Deleting Todo Items**
- User clicks delete button on todo item
- System displays confirmation dialog
- User confirms deletion
- System permanently removes todo from database
- System updates user's todo list
- User sees confirmation message

### Error Recovery Scenarios

**Scenario 10: Handling Network Connectivity Issues**
- User creates todo while network is unstable
- System attempts to save todo to database
- System detects connection failure
- System displays error message to user
- System retries operation when connection restored
- User sees success message or failure notification

**Scenario 11: Session Timeout Handling**
- User remains inactive for 30 minutes
- System automatically logs out user
- User attempts to create new todo
- System redirects to login page
- User re-authenticates and returns to dashboard
- User's todos remain intact and accessible

**Scenario 12: Data Validation Error Recovery**
- User attempts to create todo with empty title
- System validates and rejects empty title
- System displays clear error message
- User enters valid title and resubmits
- System creates todo successfully
- User sees confirmation and new todo item

## Business Rules

### Todo Creation Rules

**Title Requirements:**
- Todo titles must be between 1 and 200 characters
- Titles cannot be empty or contain only whitespace
- Special characters are allowed but HTML/JavaScript injection is prohibited
- Duplicate titles are permitted (user choice)
- Title trimming is applied automatically (leading/trailing spaces removed)

**Description Requirements:**
- Todo descriptions are optional (0-1000 characters)
- If provided, descriptions must be plain text only
- HTML tags and scripts are stripped from descriptions
- Rich text formatting is not supported
- Character count includes spaces and punctuation

**Association Rules:**
- Each todo must be associated with exactly one authenticated user
- User ownership is determined by JWT token at creation time
- Todos cannot be shared between users or transferred
- Administrator users cannot create todos on behalf of regular users

**Timestamp Rules:**
- Creation timestamp is automatically set by system
- Creation timestamp uses UTC timezone
- Timestamps are immutable after creation
- Update timestamp is set on any modification
- Completion timestamp is set when todo is marked complete

### Edit and Delete Constraints

**Edit Permissions:**
- Only the todo owner can edit title, description, or completion status
- Administrators can view all todos but cannot edit regular users' todos
- Edit operations are logged for audit purposes
- Edit conflicts are resolved by last-update-wins mechanism
- Concurrent edits by same user are prevented by user interface design

**Delete Permissions:**
- Only the todo owner can delete their todos
- Delete operations are permanent and cannot be undone
- Bulk delete operations are not supported
- Delete operations require user confirmation for safety
- Administrators cannot delete regular users' todos

**Data Integrity:**
- Todo IDs must be globally unique across system
- Referenced user IDs must exist in users table
- Cascade delete is implemented for user account deletion
- Soft delete is not implemented (permanent removal)
- Data validation occurs at database and application levels

### User Permission Rules

**Regular User Permissions:**
- Create, read, update, delete own todos
- View own user profile and account information
- Change own password and email address
- Export own data in JSON format
- Delete own account (removes all associated todos)
- Cannot access administrative functions
- Cannot view other users' data

**Administrator Permissions:**
- All regular user permissions for own todos
- View system-wide analytics and performance metrics
- Monitor user registration and activity statistics
- Manage user accounts (view, suspend, activate)
- Access system health checks and logs
- Cannot modify regular users' personal todos
- Cannot access other users' private data

**Security Constraints:**
- JWT tokens expire after 30 minutes of inactivity
- Failed login attempts result in temporary account lockout
- Password reset tokens expire after 1 hour
- Admin functions require enhanced authentication
- All administrative actions are logged and auditable

### Business Logic Flow

**Todo Lifecycle Management:**
1. Creation: User creates todo → System validates → Todo stored in database
2. Active State: Todo appears in user's active list
3. Completion: User marks complete → System updates status and timestamp
4. Editing: User modifies todo → System validates changes → Updates stored record
5. Deletion: User deletes todo → System confirms → Permanently removes record

**User Session Management:**
1. Registration: User registers → Email verification required → Account activated
2. Login: User authenticates → JWT token generated → Session begins
3. Activity: User performs actions → Token validation → Session continues
4. Inactivity: 30 minutes pass → Token expires → User logged out
5. Logout: User explicitly logs out → Token invalidated → Session ended

**Data Validation Flow:**
1. User Input: Data submitted through interface
2. Client Validation: Basic format checking in browser
3. Server Validation: Comprehensive business rule validation
4. Database Validation: Data type and constraint checking
5. Response: Success/error response with clear messaging

## Error Handling

### Authentication Errors

**Registration Errors:**
- Email already exists: "An account with this email address already exists. Please use a different email or try logging in."
- Invalid email format: "Please enter a valid email address (e.g., user@example.com)."
- Weak password: "Password must be at least 8 characters long and contain uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters."
- Email delivery failure: "Registration email could not be sent. Please try again later or contact support."
- Database connection error: "Account creation failed. Please try again in a few moments."

**Login Errors:**
- Invalid credentials: "Invalid email or password. Please check your credentials and try again."
- Account not verified: "Please verify your email address before logging in. Check your inbox for the verification link."
- Account suspended: "Your account has been temporarily suspended. Please contact support for assistance."
- Too many failed attempts: "Too many failed login attempts. Please wait 15 minutes before trying again."
- JWT token expired: "Your session has expired. Please log in again to continue."
- Invalid JWT token: "Invalid session. Please log in again."

**Password Reset Errors:**
- Email not found: "If an account exists with this email address, a password reset link has been sent."
- Reset token expired: "Password reset link has expired. Please request a new password reset."
- Invalid reset token: "Invalid password reset link. Please request a new password reset."
- Reset token already used: "Password reset link has already been used. Please request a new password reset."

### Todo Operation Errors

**Todo Creation Errors:**
- Title too short: "Todo title must be at least 1 character long."
- Title too long: "Todo title cannot exceed 200 characters. Current length: {length}"
- Description too long: "Todo description cannot exceed 1000 characters. Current length: {length}"
- Invalid characters: "Todo title contains invalid characters. Please use only standard text characters."
- Database connection error: "Failed to save todo. Please try again in a few moments."
- User not authenticated: "Please log in to create todos."

**Todo Read Errors:**
- Todo not found: "The requested todo item could not be found."
- Access denied: "You do not have permission to view this todo item."
- Database query error: "Failed to retrieve todos. Please try again."
- Authentication required: "Please log in to view your todos."

**Todo Update Errors:**
- Todo not found: "The todo item you are trying to update could not be found."
- Access denied: "You do not have permission to modify this todo item."
- Validation failed: "Todo update failed validation. Please check your input and try again."
- Concurrent modification: "This todo was modified by another process. Please refresh and try again."
- Database update error: "Failed to update todo. Please try again."

**Todo Delete Errors:**
- Todo not found: "The todo item you are trying to delete could not be found."
- Access denied: "You do not have permission to delete this todo item."
- Database delete error: "Failed to delete todo. Please try again."
- Confirmation required: "Please confirm you want to permanently delete this todo item."

### Data Validation Errors

**Input Validation Errors:**
- Missing required field: "{fieldName} is required and cannot be empty."
- Invalid format: "{fieldName} must be in the correct format."
- Length violation: "{fieldName} must be between {min} and {max} characters."
- Character restriction: "{fieldName} contains characters that are not allowed."
- SQL injection attempt: "Invalid input detected. Please use standard text characters only."

**System Validation Errors:**
- Database constraint violation: "Data integrity error. Please check your input and try again."
- Foreign key violation: "Referenced data does not exist or is invalid."
- Unique constraint violation: "Duplicate data detected. Please use unique values."
- Null constraint violation: "Required data is missing."

### System Errors

**Infrastructure Errors:**
- Database connection failure: "Database temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a few moments."
- Server overload: "System is experiencing high load. Please try again in a few moments."
- Maintenance mode: "System is currently under maintenance. Please try again later."
- Network connectivity: "Network connection error. Please check your internet connection."
- File system error: "System storage error. Please try again or contact support."

**Security Errors:**
- Unauthorized access attempt: "Access denied. Please log in to continue."
- CSRF token invalid: "Security token expired. Please refresh the page and try again."
- Rate limit exceeded: "Too many requests. Please wait before trying again."
- Suspicious activity: "Unusual activity detected. Please contact support if this was not you."

### User Recovery Processes

**Automatic Recovery:**
- Network timeout: Automatic retry with exponential backoff
- Session expiration: Automatic redirect to login page
- Token refresh: Automatic JWT token renewal before expiration
- Database connection: Automatic reconnection attempts
- Cache invalidation: Automatic cache refresh on data changes

**Manual Recovery:**
- User password reset: Email-based secure reset process
- Account lockout: Time-based automatic unlock (15 minutes)
- Session recovery: Re-login to restore session
- Data sync: Manual page refresh to sync latest data
- Error reporting: Clear error messages with suggested actions

**Support Recovery:**
- Contact information: Clear support contact details in error messages
- Troubleshooting steps: Step-by-step recovery instructions
- System status: Public status page for system health
- Escalation process: Clear path for critical issues
- Data recovery: Account deletion and data export options

## Performance Requirements

### Response Time Expectations

**Page Load Performance:**
- Initial page load: 2 seconds maximum for authenticated users
- Dashboard rendering: 1.5 seconds maximum after authentication
- Todo list display: 1 second maximum for typical user lists (≤100 todos)
- Single todo view: 0.5 seconds maximum
- Page navigation: 0.8 seconds maximum between sections

**API Response Times:**
- User authentication (login/register): 1 second maximum
- Todo CRUD operations: 500 milliseconds maximum
- User profile operations: 300 milliseconds maximum
- Password reset operations: 2 seconds maximum (includes email delivery)
- Data export operations: 3 seconds maximum for typical datasets

**Database Query Performance:**
- Simple todo retrieval: 100 milliseconds maximum
- Complex queries with filtering: 250 milliseconds maximum
- User authentication queries: 150 milliseconds maximum
- Data aggregation queries: 500 milliseconds maximum
- Bulk operations: Linear scaling based on data size

### System Throughput Requirements

**Concurrent User Capacity:**
- Minimum concurrent users: 100 simultaneous active users
- Peak load capacity: 500 concurrent users without performance degradation
- User session management: Support 1000+ concurrent sessions
- Database connection pool: Maximum 50 concurrent database connections
- API request handling: 100 requests per second sustained rate

**Data Processing Capacity:**
- Todo creation rate: 50 todos per second peak capacity
- User registration rate: 10 registrations per second peak capacity
- Data export processing: Handle 1000+ todo export requests per hour
- Database writes: Support 200 write operations per second
- Database reads: Support 1000 read operations per second

**Storage and Memory Requirements:**
- User data storage: Efficient storage for user profiles and preferences
- Todo data storage: Optimized storage for todo items with indexing
- Session storage: In-memory session management with cleanup
- Cache storage: Redis-based caching for frequently accessed data
- Backup storage: Daily automated backups with 30-day retention

### User Experience Performance

**Interface Responsiveness:**
- Form submissions: Immediate visual feedback within 100 milliseconds
- Button interactions: Visual response within 50 milliseconds
- Page transitions: Smooth transitions under 200 milliseconds
- Error displays: Error messages appear within 200 milliseconds
- Loading indicators: Clear loading states for operations over 500 milliseconds

**Real-time Updates:**
- Todo status changes: Immediate visual updates without page refresh
- Authentication state: Real-time session management
- Data synchronization: Automatic refresh of stale data
- Notification delivery: Real-time system notifications
- Multi-tab synchronization: Consistent state across browser tabs

**Mobile Performance:**
- Mobile page load: 3 seconds maximum for mobile networks
- Touch interface: Responsive touch interactions under 100 milliseconds
- Mobile data usage: Optimized data transfer for limited bandwidth
- Offline capability: Basic offline functionality for viewing todos
- Progressive loading: Incremental content loading for large datasets

### Scalability Considerations

**Horizontal Scaling Support:**
- Stateless application design for load balancing
- Database read replicas for improved query performance
- Session storage in external cache (Redis) for multi-instance support
- API gateway for request routing and rate limiting
- Microservices architecture preparation for future expansion

**Database Scaling:**
- Indexed queries for efficient data retrieval
- Database connection pooling for connection management
- Query optimization for complex operations
- Partitioning strategy for large datasets
- Read replica configuration for read-heavy workloads

**Caching Strategy:**
- Application-level caching for frequently accessed data
- Database query result caching
- Static asset caching for improved page load times
- API response caching for immutable data
- Cache invalidation strategy for data consistency

### Performance Monitoring

**Key Performance Indicators:**
- Response time monitoring for all API endpoints
- Database query performance tracking
- User session duration and engagement metrics
- System resource utilization (CPU, memory, disk)
- Error rates and system availability

**Monitoring Tools:**
- Application performance monitoring (APM) integration
- Database performance monitoring
- Real-time alerting for performance degradation
- Automated performance testing in CI/CD pipeline
- Performance benchmarking and regression testing

**Optimization Strategies:**
- Regular performance audits and optimization
- Database query optimization and indexing
- Code optimization for critical paths
- Asset optimization (compression, minification)
- Content delivery network (CDN) for static assets

## Security Requirements

### Authentication Security

**Password Security Requirements:**
- WHEN users create passwords, THE system SHALL require minimum 8 characters
- WHEN users create passwords, THE system SHALL require uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters
- WHEN passwords are stored, THE system SHALL hash passwords using bcrypt algorithm with minimum 12 salt rounds
- WHEN users change passwords, THE system SHALL verify current password before allowing change
- WHEN password reset occurs, THE system SHALL generate secure, time-limited reset tokens

**JWT Token Security:**
- WHEN JWT tokens are generated, THE system SHALL include user ID, email, role, and expiration time
- WHEN JWT tokens are validated, THE system SHALL verify token signature and expiration
- WHEN JWT tokens expire, THE system SHALL require re-authentication for continued access
- WHEN users log out, THE system SHALL invalidate current JWT token
- WHEN suspicious activity detected, THE system SHALL invalidate all active tokens for affected user

**Account Protection:**
- WHEN 5 consecutive failed login attempts occur, THE system SHALL temporarily lock account for 15 minutes
- WHEN account lockout triggers, THE system SHALL send security notification email to user
- WHEN user attempts password reset, THE system SHALL verify email ownership before sending reset link
- WHEN password reset token expires, THE system SHALL require new token generation
- WHEN user account remains inactive, THE system SHALL log out user after 30 minutes of inactivity

### Data Protection Requirements

**Data Encryption:**
- WHEN sensitive data is stored, THE system SHALL encrypt data at rest using industry-standard encryption
- WHEN data is transmitted, THE system SHALL use HTTPS/TLS encryption for all communications
- WHEN passwords are processed, THE system SHALL never store or transmit passwords in plaintext
- WHEN JWT tokens are used, THE system SHALL sign tokens using secure cryptographic algorithms
- WHEN database backups are created, THE system SHALL encrypt backup files

**Input Sanitization:**
- WHEN user input is received, THE system SHALL sanitize all input to prevent XSS attacks
- WHEN database queries are executed, THE system SHALL use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection
- WHEN HTML content is displayed, THE system SHALL escape special characters to prevent script injection
- WHEN file uploads are processed, THE system SHALL validate file types and scan for malicious content
- WHEN user data is displayed, THE system SHALL validate data integrity before presentation

**Data Privacy:**
- WHEN user data is processed, THE system SHALL comply with applicable data protection regulations
- WHEN user accounts are deleted, THE system SHALL permanently remove all associated personal data
- WHEN user data is exported, THE system SHALL provide data in portable, readable format
- WHEN data is shared with third parties, THE system SHALL obtain explicit user consent
- WHEN data retention period expires, THE system SHALL automatically purge user data

### Access Control Security

**Authorization Requirements:**
- WHEN users access resources, THE system SHALL verify ownership before allowing access
- WHEN administrative functions are used, THE system SHALL verify admin role permissions
- WHEN API endpoints are accessed, THE system SHALL implement role-based access control
- WHEN cross-user access is attempted, THE system SHALL deny unauthorized access attempts
- WHEN privilege escalation is detected, THE system SHALL immediately terminate user session

**Session Management:**
- WHEN user sessions are created, THE system SHALL generate unique session identifiers
- WHEN sessions expire, THE system SHALL automatically log out users
- WHEN multiple sessions are detected, THE system SHALL notify users of concurrent logins
- WHEN suspicious session activity occurs, THE system SHALL require re-authentication
- WHEN session data is stored, THE system SHALL protect session information from unauthorized access

**API Security:**
- WHEN API requests are received, THE system SHALL validate JWT tokens for authentication
- WHEN API rate limits are exceeded, THE system SHALL return rate limit error responses
- WHEN CORS requests are processed, THE system SHALL enforce strict origin policies
- WHEN API keys are used, THE system SHALL implement secure key management practices
- WHEN API documentation is exposed, THE system SHALL protect sensitive endpoint information

### Data Privacy Requirements

**Personal Data Handling:**
- WHEN collecting user personal data, THE system SHALL provide clear privacy notices
- WHEN processing personal data, THE system SHALL obtain explicit user consent
- WHEN storing personal data, THE system SHALL implement data minimization principles
- WHEN sharing personal data, THE system SHALL inform users of data sharing practices
- WHEN users request data deletion, THE system SHALL provide complete data removal within 30 days

**Data Retention Policies:**
- WHEN user accounts are inactive, THE system SHALL retain data for minimum 2 years
- WHEN user accounts are deleted, THE system SHALL remove all personal data within 30 days
- WHEN system logs are created, THE system SHALL retain logs for minimum 90 days
- WHEN backup data is stored, THE system SHALL encrypt and limit retention to 30 days
- WHEN audit trails are maintained, THE system SHALL preserve records for compliance requirements

**User Rights Implementation:**
- WHEN users request data access, THE system SHALL provide complete data export within 7 days
- WHEN users request data correction, THE system SHALL update records within 3 days
- WHEN users request data portability, THE system SHALL provide machine-readable data format
- WHEN users withdraw consent, THE system SHALL cease processing within immediate effect
- WHEN users object to processing, THE system SHALL provide alternative processing methods

### Security Monitoring

**Security Event Logging:**
- WHEN security events occur, THE system SHALL log timestamp, user ID, IP address, and event type
- WHEN failed authentication attempts are detected, THE system SHALL log detailed failure information
- WHEN authorization failures occur, THE system SHALL log attempted resource and user information
- WHEN data access violations are detected, THE system SHALL log detailed audit information
- WHEN system configuration changes occur, THE system SHALL log administrative actions

**Threat Detection:**
- WHEN suspicious patterns are detected, THE system SHALL trigger security alerts
- WHEN brute force attacks are identified, THE system SHALL implement automatic countermeasures
- WHEN unusual user behavior is detected, THE system SHALL flag accounts for review
- WHEN system vulnerabilities are discovered, THE system SHALL implement immediate security patches
- WHEN security incidents occur, THE system SHALL provide incident response procedures

**Security Incident Response:**
- WHEN security breaches are detected, THE system SHALL contain the incident within 15 minutes
- WHEN user accounts are compromised, THE system SHALL notify affected users within 1 hour
- WHEN system security is compromised, THE system SHALL implement emergency access controls
- WHEN data breaches occur, THE system SHALL follow regulatory notification requirements
- WHEN security incidents are resolved, THE system SHALL conduct post-incident analysis

## Data Management

### Data Models and Relationships

**User Entity Model:**
- User ID: Globally unique identifier (UUID format)
- Email Address: User's primary email for authentication and notifications
- Password Hash: Securely hashed password using bcrypt algorithm
- User Role: Enumerated type (USER, ADMIN) determining permissions
- Account Status: Current account state (ACTIVE, PENDING_VERIFICATION, SUSPENDED)
- Email Verification Status: Boolean indicating email confirmation completion
- Registration Timestamp: UTC timestamp of account creation
- Last Login Timestamp: UTC timestamp of most recent successful authentication
- Account Lockout Until: UTC timestamp if account is temporarily locked
- Failed Login Attempts: Counter tracking consecutive failed login attempts

**Todo Entity Model:**
- Todo ID: Globally unique identifier (UUID format)
- Title: Task title (1-200 characters, required)
- Description: Optional task description (0-1000 characters)
- Completion Status: Boolean indicating whether task is completed
- Creation Timestamp: UTC timestamp when todo was created
- Update Timestamp: UTC timestamp of most recent modification
- Completion Timestamp: UTC timestamp when task was marked complete
- User ID: Foreign key reference to owning user
- Soft Delete Flag: Boolean indicating if todo is marked for deletion (future implementation)
- Order Index: Integer for custom ordering within user's todo list

**Relationship Model:**
- One-to-Many: User to Todo (each user owns multiple todos)
- Cascade Rules: User deletion cascades to remove all associated todos
- Indexing Strategy: Primary indexes on User ID and Todo ID for performance
- Foreign Key Constraints: Enforced at database level for referential integrity
- Unique Constraints: User ID + Todo ID combination for ownership verification

### Data Lifecycle Management

**Data Creation Process:**
- User Registration: Create user record with hashed password and verification status
- Todo Creation: Create todo record with automatic timestamps and user association
- Session Creation: Generate JWT token and establish user session
- Audit Logging: Record creation events for audit trail maintenance
- Data Validation: Validate all inputs before database insertion

**Data Modification Process:**
- Todo Updates: Modify todo fields with automatic update timestamp
- Profile Updates: Update user information with change tracking
- Authentication Changes: Update password with secure hashing process
- Status Changes: Track all status changes with audit trail
- Concurrency Handling: Implement optimistic locking for concurrent modifications

**Data Deletion Process:**
- Soft Delete Implementation: Mark records for deletion without immediate removal
- User Account Deletion: Remove user and cascade delete all associated todos
- Scheduled Cleanup: Permanently remove soft-deleted records after retention period
- Data Integrity Verification: Ensure no orphaned records remain after deletion
- Audit Trail Preservation: Maintain deletion logs for compliance requirements

### Data Retention Policies

**User Data Retention:**
- Active User Data: Retained indefinitely while account remains active
- Inactive User Data: Retained for 2 years after last login
- Deleted User Data: Permanently removed within 30 days of deletion request
- User Session Data: Retained for 30 minutes after last activity
- Authentication Logs: Retained for 90 days for security compliance

**Todo Data Retention:**
- Active Todo Data: Retained indefinitely while user account is active
- Completed Todo Data: Retained for 1 year after completion
- Deleted Todo Data: Permanently removed within 7 days of deletion
- Todo History: Maintain completion and modification timestamps
- Bulk Delete Operations: Preserve deletion audit logs for 1 year

**System Data Retention:**
- Application Logs: Retained for 90 days for debugging and monitoring
- Error Logs: Retained for 1 year for issue tracking and analysis
- Performance Metrics: Retained for 6 months for system optimization
- Security Logs: Retained for 1 year for compliance and security analysis
- Backup Data: Retained for 30 days with daily rotation schedule

### Backup and Recovery

**Backup Strategy:**
- Daily Automated Backups: Complete database backup performed daily at 2:00 AM UTC
- Incremental Backups: Hourly incremental backups for continuous data protection
- Cross-Regional Replication: Backup data replicated to multiple geographic regions
- Encrypted Backups: All backup files encrypted using AES-256 encryption
- Backup Verification: Automated verification of backup integrity and completeness

**Recovery Procedures:**
- Point-in-Time Recovery: Ability to restore data to any point within retention period
- Partial Recovery: Selective recovery of specific user accounts or todo items
- Disaster Recovery: Complete system restoration within 4-hour maximum downtime
- Recovery Testing: Monthly recovery drills to ensure backup and restore procedures
- Recovery Documentation: Detailed recovery procedures with step-by-step instructions

**Data Integrity Assurance:**
- Checksum Validation: All backup files validated using cryptographic checksums
- Consistency Checks: Database consistency verification during backup processes
- Replication Monitoring: Real-time monitoring of backup replication health
- Alert System: Immediate alerts for backup failures or integrity issues
- Recovery Time Objectives: Maximum 4-hour recovery time for complete system restoration

### Data Integrity Rules

**Referential Integrity:**
- Foreign Key Constraints: All relationships enforced at database level
- Cascade Delete Rules: User deletion automatically removes all associated todos
- Orphan Prevention: No orphaned records allowed in the system
- Constraint Validation: All data modifications validated against integrity constraints
- Unique Constraints: Enforced uniqueness for User ID, Email, and Todo ID

**Data Validation Rules:**
- Format Validation: Email addresses validated using RFC-compliant regex patterns
- Length Constraints: All text fields constrained by maximum length requirements
- Type Validation: All fields validated against expected data types
- Range Validation: Numeric fields constrained within acceptable ranges
- Null Constraint Validation: Required fields validated for non-null values

**Business Rule Enforcement:**
- User Ownership: Todos can only be accessed by their owning users
- Timestamp Ordering: Creation timestamps cannot be modified after creation
- Status Transitions: Todo completion status changes tracked with timestamps
- Session Validation: User sessions must be authenticated before data access
- Permission Checking: All operations validated against user's role and permissions

**Data Consistency Mechanisms:**
- ACID Transactions: All database operations wrapped in ACID-compliant transactions
- Optimistic Locking: Concurrent modification conflicts detected and resolved
- Transaction Isolation: Serializable isolation level for data consistency
- Deadlock Prevention: Database deadlock detection and resolution mechanisms
- Consistency Monitoring: Continuous monitoring of data consistency metrics

**Data Export and Portability:**
- User Data Export: Complete user data export in JSON format within 7 days
- Data Format Standards: Export format follows industry-standard data portability practices
- Data Completeness: All user data included in export including todos and preferences
- Export Security: Data exports encrypted and delivered through secure channels
- Retention of Export Rights: User data export capability maintained for 2 years after account deletion

# TodoApp Project Requirements Analysis

## Project Overview

### Purpose and Scope
TodoApp is a personal productivity application designed to help users manage their daily tasks and improve their organizational efficiency. The application provides a simple yet effective way for users to create, track, and organize their Todo items with complete CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) functionality.

### Business Value Proposition
The application addresses the fundamental need for personal task management in an increasingly complex digital world. By providing a clean, intuitive interface for task management, TodoApp enables users to increase productivity through clear task visibility, reduce mental load through external storage of tasks, improve organization through structured task management, and enable progress tracking through visual feedback on completion.

### Target Users
TodoApp serves two primary user categories: Individual Users (Members) who seek personal task management solutions requiring secure, personal account management with full control over their Todo items, and System Administrators (Admins) who manage the application infrastructure, user accounts, and system operations.

### Development Approach
The project follows a structured documentation approach that separates business requirements from technical implementation decisions, enabling developers to maintain full autonomy over architecture, technology choices, and implementation strategies while ensuring business objectives are clearly defined and achievable.

## Document Navigation Structure

This requirements analysis consists of ten interconnected documents that provide comprehensive coverage of the TodoApp system. Each document serves a specific purpose and builds upon the others to create a complete understanding of the application requirements.

### Core Requirements Documents

**Service Overview** - Executive summary, problem definition, solution overview, business value proposition, target users, and success metrics

**User Actors & Authentication** - User actor hierarchy, authentication requirements, permission matrix, user roles and capabilities, security model

**Functional Requirements** - Core Todo operations, user interface requirements, data validation rules, error handling scenarios, user workflows

**User Stories** - Primary user scenarios, secondary user scenarios, edge cases and error scenarios, user journey maps, success paths

### Business Logic and Constraints

**Business Rules** - Data validation rules, business logic constraints, workflow rules, security constraints, operational rules

**Non-Functional Requirements** - Performance requirements, scalability requirements, reliability requirements, maintainability requirements, quality standards

**Data Management** - Data flow overview, data lifecycle, data storage requirements, data backup and recovery, data archival

### Security and Implementation

**Security Requirements** - Authentication security, authorization model, data protection, API security, compliance requirements

**Integration Guidelines** - API integration patterns, third-party service requirements, deployment considerations, monitoring and logging, integration testing

**Implementation Guidelines** - Development methodology, code quality standards, testing requirements, deployment process, maintenance guidelines

## User Actors and Authentication Requirements

### User Actor Hierarchy

#### Member
**Actor Description**: Authenticated users who create, manage, and organize their personal Todo lists with full control over their own data.

**Actor Capabilities**:
- Create new Todo items with titles, descriptions, due dates, and priority levels
- Read and view all Todo items assigned to their account
- Update existing Todo items including status, details, and categorization
- Delete Todo items they have created
- Organize Todos through categorization and priority management
- View their own activity history and completion statistics
- Manage their personal account settings and preferences

**Data Scope**: Members can only access, modify, and manage Todo items where they are the designated owner. They cannot view, modify, or access Todo items belonging to other users.

#### Administrator  
**Actor Description**: System administrators with elevated permissions to manage all Todo items across the system, oversee user accounts, and perform system administration functions.

**Actor Capabilities**:
- Create, read, update, and delete any Todo item across the entire system
- View comprehensive system statistics and usage analytics
- Manage user accounts including account creation, modification, and deactivation
- Perform system-wide data maintenance and cleanup operations
- Access system logs and audit trails
- Manage system configuration and operational settings
- Moderate content and enforce system policies
- Generate system reports and usage analytics

### Authentication Requirements

**WHEN a user registers for a new account, THE system SHALL validate email format and password strength requirements, create user record with verified status, and send email verification link within 30 seconds.**

**WHEN a user logs in with valid credentials, THE system SHALL authenticate user identity, generate JWT access token with 15-minute expiration, generate refresh token with 30-day expiration, establish authenticated session, and redirect to user dashboard.**

**WHEN a user logs out, THE system SHALL invalidate current session tokens, clear stored authentication data, and display login confirmation message.**

**WHEN an authenticated session expires, THE system SHALL require user to re-authenticate, preserve unsaved data if applicable, and display session expired message with login option.**

**WHEN a user requests password reset, THE system SHALL validate email address, generate temporary reset token, send reset email with secure link, and invalidate reset token after 24 hours.**

### Permission Matrix

| Action | Member | Administrator |
|--------|--------|---------------|
| Create personal Todo items | ✅ Allowed | ✅ Allowed (all users) |
| Read own Todo items | ✅ Allowed | ✅ Allowed (all users) |
| Update own Todo items | ✅ Allowed | ✅ Allowed (all users) |
| Delete own Todo items | ✅ Allowed | ✅ Allowed (all users) |
| Read other users' Todo items | ❌ Denied | ✅ Allowed |
| Update other users' Todo items | ❌ Denied | ✅ Allowed |
| Delete other users' Todo items | ❌ Denied | ✅ Allowed |
| Create user accounts | ❌ Denied | ✅ Allowed |
| Modify user account settings | ✅ Allowed (own) | ✅ Allowed (all users) |
| Delete user accounts | ❌ Denied | ✅ Allowed |
| View system analytics | ❌ Denied | ✅ Allowed |
| Access system logs | ❌ Denied | ✅ Allowed |
| Manage system configuration | ❌ Denied | ✅ Allowed |

## Functional Requirements

### Core Todo Operations

**WHEN a user creates a new Todo item, THE system SHALL validate the input data and store the item with appropriate metadata including creation timestamp, status, and user association.**

**WHEN a user accesses their Todo list, THE system SHALL display all Todo items associated with that user, sorted by creation date in descending order, with completed items visually distinguished from active items.**

**WHEN a user updates an existing Todo item, THE system SHALL verify ownership and update the specified fields while preserving audit trail information including modification timestamp.**

**WHEN a user deletes a Todo item, THE system SHALL permanently remove the item from the user's list and update related statistics.**

### Task Creation Requirements

**THE system SHALL allow users to create Todo items with the following mandatory fields:**
- **Task Title**: Text field between 1-200 characters, required
- **Task Description**: Optional text field up to 1000 characters
- **Due Date**: Optional date field, must be current date or future date
- **Priority Level**: One of "Low", "Medium", "High", or "Critical" (default: "Medium")
- **Category/Tag**: Optional classification label up to 50 characters

**WHEN a user submits a new Todo item, THE system SHALL validate that:**
- Task title is not empty and does not exceed character limits
- Due date (if provided) is not in the past
- All character limits are respected for text fields
- Priority level is one of the allowed values

**THE system SHALL automatically assign the following metadata to every new Todo item:**
- Unique identifier (auto-generated UUID)
- Creation timestamp (current system time)
- Status: "active" (default)
- User ID: ID of the creator
- Last modified timestamp (initially same as creation)

### Task Completion and Status Management

**WHEN a user marks a Todo item as completed, THE system SHALL:**
- Update status from "active" to "completed"
- Set completion timestamp to current system time
- Preserve original creation date and all other metadata
- Visual indication of completion status in subsequent displays

**WHEN a user reopens a completed Todo item, THE system SHALL:**
- Restore status to "active"
- Clear completion timestamp
- Update modification timestamp
- Remove visual completion indicators

### Data Validation Rules

**THE system SHALL validate all user input according to the following rules:**

**Task Title Validation:**
- Minimum length: 1 character
- Maximum length: 200 characters
- Required for task creation

**Task Description Validation:**
- Maximum length: 1000 characters
- Optional field (can be empty)
- Plain text only (no HTML or special formatting)

**Due Date Validation:**
- Format: YYYY-MM-DD
- Must be current date or future date (no past dates allowed)
- Optional field (can be empty)
- Must be a valid calendar date

**Priority Level Validation:**
- Allowed values: "Low", "Medium", "High", "Critical"
- Case-insensitive input (automatically normalize to proper case)
- Default value: "Medium" if not specified

### Error Handling Scenarios

**WHEN user authentication fails, THE system SHALL:**
- Return HTTP 401 Unauthorized status code
- Display clear error message: "Invalid email or password"
- Log failed authentication attempt for security monitoring
- Provide link to password reset functionality
- Lock account after 5 consecutive failed attempts for 15 minutes

**WHEN user input fails validation, THE system SHALL:**
- Return HTTP 400 Bad Request status code
- Provide specific field-level error messages
- Highlight invalid fields in the user interface
- Maintain all other valid user input (don't clear entire form)
- Provide clear guidance on correcting the errors

**WHEN database operations fail, THE system SHALL:**
- Return appropriate HTTP status code (500 for server errors)
- Display generic error message: "We're experiencing technical difficulties. Please try again later."
- Log detailed error information for technical support
- Attempt automatic retry for transient errors (max 3 attempts)
- Provide user with option to retry the operation

## Business Rules

### Todo Ownership and Access Rules

**WHEN a user interacts with a Todo item, THE system SHALL verify that:**
- The Todo item belongs to the authenticated user (for member users)
- Admin users can access all Todo items across the system
- No user can modify Todo items belonging to other users

**IF an unauthorized access attempt is made, THEN THE system SHALL:**
- Return HTTP 403 (Forbidden) status with appropriate error message
- Log the unauthorized access attempt for security monitoring
- Not reveal information about the existence of the target Todo item

### Todo Lifecycle Management

**THE Todo item lifecycle SHALL follow these rules:**
- Todo items start in "pending" status upon creation
- Todo items can transition to: "in_progress", "completed", or "cancelled"
- Completed Todo items can be reopened by changing status back to "pending" or "in_progress"
- Cancelled Todo items cannot be reopened

### Security Constraints

**THE system SHALL enforce strong authentication by:**
- Requiring all API requests to include valid authentication tokens
- Implementing session timeouts to limit token validity
- Supporting secure password reset workflows
- Tracking and limiting failed login attempts

**THE system SHALL protect user data by:**
- Encrypting sensitive data in storage
- Validating all input to prevent injection attacks
- Sanitizing user-provided content to prevent XSS
- Implementing rate limiting to prevent abuse

## User Workflows

### Complete Todo Management Workflow

**Primary User Journey: Creating and Managing a Todo Item**

1. **User Access**
   - User logs in with valid credentials
   - System redirects to user's Todo dashboard
   - Dashboard displays current Todo summary and quick actions

2. **Creating a New Todo**
   - User clicks "Add Todo" or "+" button
   - System displays new Todo creation form
   - User enters task title (required)
   - User optionally adds description, due date, priority, and category
   - User clicks "Create" or "Save" button
   - System validates input and creates Todo item
   - System redirects to Todo list view with new item highlighted

3. **Managing Existing Todos**
   - User views Todo list with all active items
   - User can filter, sort, or search for specific items
   - User clicks on any Todo item to edit details
   - System allows inline editing or detailed edit modal
   - User modifies any allowed fields
   - User saves changes or cancels editing

4. **Completing Todos**
   - User marks Todo as complete (checkbox, button, or status toggle)
   - System updates status and records completion timestamp
   - Todo moves to completed section or gets visual completion indicator
   - User can reopen completed items if needed

5. **Deleting Todos**
   - User clicks delete option on desired Todo item
   - System displays confirmation dialog: "Are you sure you want to delete this Todo?"
   - User confirms deletion
   - System permanently removes Todo item
   - System updates user's Todo statistics

## Success Criteria and Validation

### Authentication Success Criteria
- User registration completes within 30 seconds and sends verification email
- Successful login redirects to dashboard within 5 seconds
- JWT token generation and validation functions correctly for all user roles
- Session management maintains user state across browser sessions
- Password reset process completes within 60 seconds

### Todo Management Success Criteria
- Todo creation succeeds within 2 seconds for valid inputs
- Todo updates maintain data integrity and audit trails
- Todo deletion removes items permanently with user confirmation
- Todo retrieval supports filtering, sorting, and pagination
- All validation rules enforce business requirements correctly

### Security Success Criteria
- Password policies enforce required complexity standards
- Rate limiting prevents authentication abuse
- JWT tokens expire as specified and refresh correctly
- Sensitive data encryption functions properly
- Security monitoring detects and reports suspicious activities

## Developer Autonomy Statement

> *Developer Note: This documentation defines business requirements and system objectives only. All technical implementation decisions, including but not limited to database design, application architecture, API specifications, technology stack selection, and development methodologies, are at the complete discretion of the development team. The documents describe WHAT the system should accomplish and WHY it should exist, while HOW to build it remains the responsibility of technical experts who will make informed decisions based on project constraints, team expertise, and organizational standards.*
