operations.name: registerMember
operations.description:
Creates a new member account in the TodoApp system and establishes the initial authentication session.

This endpoint allows new users to register for TodoApp access by providing their email address and basic profile information. Upon successful registration, the system creates a new todo_app_members record with the provided email, first name, last name, and sets the account status to 'active'. A corresponding todo_app_member_sessions record is also created to track the registration session with connection metadata including IP address, connection URL, and referrer information.

The registration process generates initial JWT tokens for the new member, enabling immediate access to Todo management functionality. The session is tracked with detailed connection metadata for security monitoring and audit purposes. Members can register with optional first and last names, but must provide a unique email address that serves as their account identifier.

This operation is essential for onboarding new users to the TodoApp system and establishing their initial authenticated session. After registration, members can immediately start creating and managing their personal Todo items using other authenticated endpoints.

requestBody.description: Member registration information including email and optional profile details

responseBody.description: Authentication response with member profile and initial JWT tokens

operations.name: authenticateMember
operations.description:
Authenticates an existing member user and establishes a new authenticated session with comprehensive security tracking.

This endpoint validates member credentials and creates a new todo_app_member_sessions record for ongoing Todo management access. The system verifies the member exists in the todo_app_members table and has an 'active' status before creating the session. Upon successful authentication, the member gains access to their personal Todo items and can perform all CRUD operations on their own data.

The login process creates a new session record with detailed connection metadata including the member's IP address, connection URL, and referrer URL for comprehensive security monitoring and audit trails. This enables the system to track login patterns, detect suspicious activity, and provide detailed session management capabilities for individual members.

After successful authentication, JWT tokens are issued that enable the member to access authenticated Todo management endpoints. The session tracking ensures all Todo operations can be properly attributed to the authenticated member and provides the foundation for comprehensive security monitoring and user activity analysis.

requestBody.description: Member login credentials for authentication

responseBody.description: Authentication response with member profile and JWT access tokens

operations.name: refreshMemberToken
operations.description:
Refreshes the authentication tokens for an existing member session, extending access to Todo management functionality.

This endpoint allows members to renew their JWT access tokens using a valid refresh token without requiring re-authentication with their credentials. The system validates the refresh token against existing todo_app_member_sessions records to ensure the session is still active and hasn't expired. Members can refresh their tokens as long as they have a valid session record in the database.

Token refresh is essential for maintaining seamless access to Todo management features without interrupting the user's workflow. When a refresh is successful, new JWT tokens are issued while maintaining the existing session context and security tracking. The refresh operation updates the session expiration time to extend the member's authenticated access period.

This operation is crucial for user experience optimization, allowing members to continue managing their Todo items without needing to repeatedly log in. It supports the TodoApp's goal of providing efficient task management by maintaining persistent, secure authentication sessions for active members.

requestBody.description: Member refresh token for extending authentication session

responseBody.description: Updated authentication response with new JWT access tokens

operations.description:
Administrative account registration endpoint that creates new system administrator accounts with elevated privileges and issues initial JWT tokens for system-wide management access.

This endpoint allows the creation of new administrative users who can access all TodoApp system features, manage other users, and perform system administration tasks. The operation creates a new record in the todo_app_administrators table with secure password hashing, role level assignment, and active status by default.

The join process includes comprehensive validation of email uniqueness across administrators, password strength requirements, role level assignment (super_admin, admin, moderator), and proper audit trail creation. New administrators receive initial JWT access tokens with appropriate privileges for their role level.

Security considerations include mandatory email uniqueness validation to prevent duplicate administrator accounts, encrypted password storage using industry-standard hashing algorithms, and comprehensive audit logging of all administrative account creation events. The operation supports the administrative account lifecycle with proper status tracking and soft deletion capabilities for account recovery.

Administrative account creation establishes the foundation for secure system management with role-based access control, ensuring administrators can perform their duties while maintaining strict security protocols and compliance requirements.

requestBody.description: New administrator account creation data including email, password, name information, and role level specification for initial account setup

responseBody.description: Created administrator account information with initial authentication tokens and access credentials for immediate system access

operations.name: join

operations.description:
Administrative authentication endpoint that validates administrator credentials and issues JWT access tokens for system-wide management operations and privileged access.

This endpoint provides secure authentication for system administrators who need access to all TodoApp features, user management capabilities, and system administration functions. The login process validates the administrator's email and password against the todo_app_administrators table, verifies account status is active, and generates appropriate JWT tokens based on the administrator's role level.

The authentication system includes comprehensive security measures such as account status validation, password verification using stored hash comparisons, and audit logging of all administrative login attempts. Successful authentication generates both access and refresh tokens with appropriate expiration times and role-based privileges.

Security considerations include mandatory email and password validation, account status verification to ensure only active administrators can access the system, and comprehensive audit trail creation for all administrative access attempts. The operation supports secure session management with proper token generation and validation mechanisms.

Administrative login establishes authenticated session context for privileged operations, ensuring system administrators can securely access management functions while maintaining strict security protocols and compliance requirements.

requestBody.description: Administrator login credentials including email address and password for secure authentication and access token generation

responseBody.description: Authenticated administrator information with JWT access tokens, refresh tokens, and session credentials for secure system management access

operations.name: login

operations.description:
Administrative token refresh endpoint that renews JWT access tokens for authenticated administrators to maintain secure system management sessions without re-authentication.

This endpoint allows system administrators to refresh their access tokens using valid refresh tokens, ensuring uninterrupted access to privileged TodoApp management features. The refresh process validates the provided refresh token against active administrative sessions in the todo_app_administrator_sessions table, verifies the administrator account status, and generates new JWT access tokens with appropriate role-based privileges.

The token refresh system includes comprehensive security measures such as refresh token validation, session existence verification, account status checks, and proper token expiration management. New access tokens are generated with appropriate expiration times while maintaining security best practices for administrative sessions.

Security considerations include mandatory refresh token validation to prevent unauthorized token usage, session existence verification to ensure active administrative sessions, and audit logging of all token refresh events. The operation supports seamless session management while maintaining strict security protocols for privileged access.

Administrative token refresh maintains secure authenticated context for ongoing system management operations, ensuring administrators can perform their duties efficiently while maintaining strict security protocols and compliance requirements.

requestBody.description: Valid refresh token for renewing administrative access tokens and maintaining authenticated session for system management operations

responseBody.description: Renewed administrative authentication tokens with updated access tokens and continued session credentials for seamless system management

This operation provides detailed security monitoring and compliance data by fetching all audit trail entries involving the specified member, including actions where they were the actor performing operations, actions where they were the target of operations performed by others, and actions affecting their associated entities such as todos.

The operation accesses the todo_app_audit_logs table and returns audit log entries that comprehensively track all member-related activity including login/logout activities, todo management operations, profile updates, and administrative actions. Each audit log entry contains complete metadata including the actor performing the action (whether member or administrator), detailed action descriptions, affected entities, IP addresses, user agent information, and timestamps for complete forensic analysis.

The audit log system supports multiple tracking scenarios:
1. Actions performed BY the member (actor_member_id references)
2. Actions performed BY administrators ON the member (target_member_id references)  
3. Actions affecting member's todos (target_todo_id references)
4. Administrative login/logout activities by administrators (actor_administrator_id references)

Security and access control are strictly enforced - only administrators with appropriate security clearance can access member audit logs due to the sensitive nature of security monitoring data. The operation requires authentication and authorization verification to ensure only authorized personnel can view user activity trails for compliance and security investigation purposes.

The audit log data supports security incident investigation, compliance reporting, user behavior analysis, and operational oversight. All audit entries are immutable and preserve complete historical context for regulatory compliance and security analysis requirements.

operations.description:
Permanently remove a specific Todo item from the system with comprehensive authorization validation and audit trail tracking.

This operation performs a hard delete of a Todo item, permanently removing it from the user's personal task list. The endpoint supports comprehensive user isolation by ensuring that users can only delete Todo items they own, with administrators having elevated permissions to delete any Todo item across the system.

When a user or administrator attempts to delete a Todo item, the system performs multiple validation layers:

1. **User Ownership Verification**: The system verifies that the requesting user owns the target Todo item by checking the relationship to `todo_app_members.id` or `todo_app_administrators.id` depending on the user type. For regular members, only Todos with matching `todo_app_member_id` can be deleted. For administrators, Todos with any ownership can be deleted.

2. **Soft Delete Implementation**: Rather than permanent database deletion, the system implements soft deletion by setting the `deleted_at` timestamp. This maintains audit trails and data integrity while removing the item from active views. The Todo item will be excluded from normal queries but preserved in the database for potential recovery.

3. **Business Logic Validation**: The system validates that the Todo item is in an appropriate state for deletion. Active, completed, or cancelled Todos can be deleted, but the operation logs the deletion reason and current status.

4. **Audit Trail Recording**: Every deletion is recorded in the `todo_app_audit_logs` table with detailed information including the actor, target Todo ID, action type 'delete_todo', old values for potential rollback, and contextual information like IP address and user agent.

The operation returns the deleted Todo item data to confirm successful removal, including the `deleted_at` timestamp set during the deletion process. This allows clients to confirm the operation and update their local state.

Security considerations include proper session validation, rate limiting to prevent abuse, and comprehensive logging for security monitoring. The soft delete approach ensures compliance with data retention policies while providing flexibility for administrative recovery if needed.

Related operations include Todo creation (POST /todos), Todo updates (PUT /todos/{todoId}), and Todo status management operations. This deletion operation is part of the complete Todo lifecycle management system.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target Todo item to be permanently removed from the system

responseBody.description: The deleted Todo item data including all fields and the deletion timestamp

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive system audit logs for security monitoring, compliance reporting, and operational oversight across the entire TodoApp ecosystem.

This operation provides administrators with complete visibility into all user actions, system events, and operational activities within the TodoApp platform. The audit logging system serves as the primary mechanism for security monitoring, compliance reporting, regulatory audit trail requirements, and operational analysis.

The audit logs encompass a wide range of activities including:

1. **User Action Tracking**: Complete logging of all member and administrator actions on Todo items (create, update, delete, complete operations), user account management activities (registration, profile updates, session management), and administrative operations across the system.

2. **Security Event Monitoring**: All authentication events (login, logout, failed login attempts), authorization attempts, privilege escalation activities, and potential security violations are logged with detailed context including IP addresses, user agent information, and session identifiers.

3. **System Operational Events**: System configuration changes, maintenance activities, database operations, performance monitoring events, and infrastructure-related activities are captured to provide complete operational visibility.

4. **Compliance and Forensic Support**: The system maintains detailed audit trails that support regulatory compliance requirements, legal discovery processes, security incident investigation, and forensic analysis capabilities. Each log entry includes comprehensive metadata for complete context.

The operation supports advanced filtering and pagination capabilities:

- **Actor Filtering**: Filter logs by specific users (both members and administrators)
- **Action Type Filtering**: Filter by specific action types like 'create_todo', 'login', 'admin_update_user', etc.
- **Entity-Based Filtering**: Filter logs related to specific Todo items or user accounts
- **Time Range Filtering**: Support for time-based queries to analyze specific periods
- **Severity Level Filtering**: Filter by severity levels (info, warning, error, critical, security)
- **IP Address Analysis**: Support for geographic or security analysis based on source IP addresses

The response includes comprehensive audit log entries with all fields from the `todo_app_audit_logs` table including actor information, target entities, action details, old and new values for state changes, security metadata (IP, user agent), and temporal information. The operation provides both summary information for dashboard views and detailed entries for investigation purposes.

Administrative access is strictly controlled with role-based authorization ensuring only properly authenticated administrators can access this sensitive system information. All audit log access is itself logged to maintain complete audit trail integrity.

This operation is essential for security operations center (SOC) activities, compliance reporting, user behavior analysis, system health monitoring, and regulatory audit requirements. The comprehensive audit trail enables organizations to meet various compliance frameworks while maintaining operational security and transparency.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of comprehensive audit log entries with detailed user actions, system events, and security monitoring data

The system metadata framework stores configuration in various data types including boolean feature flags for enabling/disabling functionality, numeric thresholds and limits, string configuration values for system parameters, JSON configuration objects for complex structured data, and version tracking for configuration schema evolution.

Configuration categories include feature flags (todo sharing, user permissions), system limits (max todos per user), UI settings (theme defaults), security settings (authentication policies), performance settings (caching, timeouts), integration settings (external service configurations), and operational settings (maintenance modes, deployment parameters).

The metadata system supports environment-specific configurations, allowing different settings for development, staging, and production environments. All configuration entries include detailed descriptions, validation schemas, default values, and range restrictions to ensure configuration integrity and prevent system instability.

This operation is critical for system administration, configuration management, feature rollout control, and operational monitoring of the TodoApp platform.

This operation performs a logical deletion on the todo_app_system_metadata table in the Prisma schema, marking the configuration record as deleted while preserving it in the database for audit and rollback purposes.

The configuration entry is excluded from normal system queries and operations, but remains accessible through administrative interfaces and audit logs. This enables safe deletion with restore capabilities and maintains complete configuration history for compliance requirements.

Before deletion, the system validates that the configuration can be safely removed without affecting critical system functionality. System-level configurations that affect core system behavior require proper authorization and confirmation. The operation includes comprehensive audit logging to record who performed the deletion and when it occurred.

ITodoAppMember.description:
Member user profile in the TodoApp system with complete identity and account information.

Represents a registered member user with separated profile data that focuses on user identity, contact information, and account lifecycle management. This entity handles all user-facing profile aspects while maintaining security separation from authentication credentials for enhanced protection.

The member profile includes personal identification details (email, names), account status for lifecycle management, and comprehensive audit trail information (creation, updates, soft deletion). Status tracking enables proper user access control to Todo management functionality and system features.

Profile data remains independent of authentication mechanisms, allowing updates to personal information without affecting login credentials or security settings. The separation supports better security practices and enables flexible authentication implementations.

Soft deletion capability ensures account recovery possibilities while maintaining data integrity. Status values ('active', 'suspended', 'deactivated') control member access levels and determine available system functionality, with proper validation and audit trail maintenance throughout the member lifecycle.

created_at.description: Member profile creation timestamp recording when the member account was initially created and registered in the system. This timestamp establishes the member's registration date for audit trail purposes and enables proper chronological sorting and filtering of member records.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp for account recovery management. Null when account is active, contains deletion timestamp when account is soft deleted for recoverable account management. This field enables account restoration and maintains historical data integrity while preventing active system access for deleted accounts.

email.description: Member email address used for account identification and communication. Must be unique across all members for account differentiation and contact purposes. Serves as primary identifier for member lookup, authentication correlation, and all system communications including notifications and account-related messages.

first_name.description: Member's first name for personalization and user interface display. Used for addressing the user in communications, displaying personalized content throughout the application, and personal identification purposes. This optional field enables human-friendly member interactions while maintaining privacy controls.

id.description: Unique identifier for the member profile using UUID v4 format. This primary key ensures global uniqueness across all member records and serves as the primary reference for all member-related database operations, relationships, and API endpoints.

last_name.description: Member's last name for complete user identification and family name tracking. Works in conjunction with first name to provide full name display for formal communications, address formatting, and comprehensive user identification throughout the TodoApp system.

status.description: Current account status for lifecycle management and access control. Valid values include 'active' for fully functional accounts, 'suspended' for temporarily disabled access, and 'deactivated' for permanently disabled accounts. This status controls member access to Todo management functionality, system features, and determines available operational capabilities.

updated_at.description: Last profile modification timestamp that updates whenever member profile information is changed. This timestamp maintains accurate audit trail and change history for compliance, security monitoring, and data synchronization purposes. Automatically updated on all profile modifications to ensure chronological accuracy.

ITodoAppMember.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating new member profiles in the TodoApp system with full profile data submission.

Enables comprehensive member registration and profile creation with complete user identification information while maintaining security separation from authentication data. This DTO handles all profile creation aspects of member onboarding including account status initialization.

The creation process supports both individual member registration and administrative member creation, with validation of unique email addresses and proper status management. Profile data is created independently of authentication credentials to maintain proper security boundaries and enable flexible authentication implementations.

Members can register with optional first and last names, must provide a unique email address, and require explicit status designation. Status controls access to Todo management functionality and system features from the moment of account creation.

Soft deletion is supported for account recovery scenarios, and proper status initialization determines the member's initial access level to Todo management functionality and system features.

email.description: Member email address for account identification and communication. Must be unique across all members for account differentiation and contact purposes. Used as primary identifier for member lookup, authentication verification, and contact operations throughout the system.

first_name.description: Member's first name for personalization and user interface display throughout the application. Optional field used for addressing the user in communications, displaying personalized content, and creating a more engaging user experience in Todo management interfaces.

last_name.description: Member's last name for complete user identification and family name tracking. Optional field that works with first name for full name display, formal communications, and proper member identification in system administration and reporting features.

status.description: Current account status for lifecycle management and access control. Valid values: 'active' (full access to Todo management features), 'suspended' (limited access), 'deactivated' (no access). Controls immediate member access to Todo management functionality and system features upon account creation.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp for account recovery and compliance management. Null when account is active, contains deletion timestamp when account is soft deleted for recoverable account management and data retention compliance.

ITodoAppMember.ILogin.description:
Member login credentials for secure authentication and access token generation with mandatory session context for comprehensive security tracking.

This schema represents the complete authentication request structure that enables members to establish secure sessions in the TodoApp system. The essential authentication fields (email and password) are combined with mandatory session metadata to create comprehensive security monitoring capabilities.

The session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are essential for audit trails, security monitoring, and compliance requirements. Each login attempt creates a detailed session record in the todo_app_member_sessions table with connection metadata, enabling comprehensive tracking of user activity patterns and security incident investigation.

This authentication mechanism ensures that all Todo management operations can be properly attributed to authenticated members while maintaining detailed security oversight. The mandatory session metadata supports geographic security analysis, suspicious login pattern detection, and compliance with security monitoring requirements.

refreshToken.description: Valid refresh token for extending member authentication session. Token that allows members to renew their access tokens without re-authentication. Must be a valid, non-expired token associated with an active member session.

ITodoAppMember.IRefresh.description:
Member refresh token for extending authentication session through secure token renewal process.

This schema facilitates seamless authentication continuity by allowing members to extend their access period without requiring repeated credential authentication. The refresh token mechanism maintains the security integrity of the authentication system while optimizing user experience by preventing frequent login interruptions.

Token refresh operations validate the refresh token against existing todo_app_member_sessions records to ensure session validity and security. Successful refresh operations generate new JWT access tokens while maintaining the existing session context and security tracking, extending the member's authenticated access period for continued Todo management functionality.

This authentication maintenance process is crucial for user experience optimization in the TodoApp system, enabling members to focus on task management activities without authentication workflow disruptions. The refresh mechanism supports persistent, secure sessions that align with the system's goal of efficient task management through streamlined user workflows.

The summary includes only the core identification and display information: unique identifier, email, names, and current status. Audit timestamps are excluded to minimize data transfer and simplify rendering in user interfaces.

Represents administrative users who can access all user data, manage member accounts, monitor system performance, and perform administrative functions. Administrators have system-wide privileges while maintaining secure authentication and session management.

Administrative accounts include enhanced security measures and comprehensive audit logging for all administrative actions. These accounts can manage user lifecycle, system configuration, and provide user support through full system access.

IAuthSession.description:
Represents authentication session information from either member or administrator contexts. This unified session type supports cross-role session management and administrative oversight, enabling security monitoring and audit capabilities across different user types.

The session captures essential connection metadata including IP address, referrer information, and session lifecycle timing. Each session is associated with a specific user type (member or administrator) and includes comprehensive tracking for security investigations, user support activities, and compliance auditing.

Sessions maintain independent lifecycle management with creation timestamps and optional expiration handling. The type supports unified session retrieval across both todo_app_member_sessions and todo_app_administrator_sessions tables while preserving role-specific context and security boundaries.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authentication session for tracking and administrative reference

user.description: Complete user account information for this session including profile details and status. Provides full context for session ownership and user association without requiring additional API calls.

referrer.description: Referrer URL that led to the session creation. Provides context for how the user accessed the system for security analysis, marketing attribution, and user journey tracking

created_at.description: Session creation timestamp. Records when the user successfully authenticated and established this session for audit trail and session lifecycle management

ITodoAppMember.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating existing member profiles in the TodoApp system.

Allows modification of member profile information including personal details and account status while maintaining security boundaries and data integrity. This DTO supports profile updates during user lifecycle management, account modifications, and status changes.

The update operation maintains separation from authentication data and supports partial updates of profile information. Status changes affect member access to Todo functionality and system features, with proper validation and audit trail maintenance.

Soft deletion is supported for account recovery scenarios, and status modifications provide administrative control over member access levels and account lifecycle management.

first_name.description: Updated member's first name for personalization and user interface display. Used for addressing the user in communications and displaying personalized content throughout the application.

last_name.description: Updated member's last name for complete user identification and family name tracking. Works with first name for full name display and formal communications.

status.description: Updated account status for lifecycle management. Valid values: active, suspended, deactivated. Changes to status control member access to Todo management functionality and system features.

ITodoAppMember.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for member search, filtering, and pagination operations in the TodoApp system.

Provides comprehensive filtering and search capabilities specifically designed for Todo application member management. This schema supports efficient member discovery and management workflows within the context of Todo list functionality.

Members in the TodoApp system have access to personal Todo management features including creating, updating, completing, and deleting their Todo items. Search functionality covers member identification fields including email addresses, names, and account status for targeted member interactions.

Status filtering enables administrators to manage member access levels: active members can fully utilize Todo features, suspended members have limited access, and deactivated members cannot access Todo functionality. Pagination parameters ensure optimal performance when managing large member bases.

Used primarily for administrative member management interfaces and Todo system administration workflows where member filtering and discovery are essential for system oversight and user support.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Defaults to 1 for first page of results. Used for browsing through large member lists efficiently.

limit.description: Number of members to return per page. Maximum 100 members per page for optimal API performance. Larger limits may impact response times for systems with many members.

search.description: Text search across member email, first name, and last name fields. Case-insensitive search with partial match support. Useful for finding specific members when managing Todo users or providing customer support.

oneOf.description: Filter members by account status. Active members have full Todo app access, suspended members have limited functionality, deactivated members cannot access the system. Essential for member lifecycle management and access control.

ITodoAppMember.IInvert.description:
Complete member profile with personal information and Todo app account details.

Provides comprehensive member profile information including personal details, account status, and Todo application access capabilities. This schema represents the complete member context needed for profile displays, member management interfaces, and Todo system administration.

Members in the TodoApp system have access to personal Todo management functionality including creating and organizing personal task lists, marking items as complete, setting priorities and categories, and managing their Todo workflow. The profile maintains essential identity information while providing access to account lifecycle management.

This variant includes the full member profile with complete personal information, account status for access control, and audit timestamps for compliance and system monitoring. The structure supports efficient member profile display for administrative oversight, customer support interactions, and Todo system management workflows.

Key member capabilities include Todo creation and management, personal productivity tracking, and integration with the broader TodoApp ecosystem. Account status directly controls access to Todo functionality: active members have full access, suspended members have limited capabilities, and deactivated members cannot access any Todo features.

Used in member management interfaces, profile administration screens, customer support tools, and any context requiring complete member context with Todo application integration details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the member account. Generated automatically upon registration using UUID v4 for global uniqueness across the TodoApp system.

email.description: Member email address for account identification and communication. Used for login, notifications, and Todo-related communications. Must be unique across all members.

first_name.description: Member's first name for personalization and user interface display. Used for addressing the member in Todo notifications, progress updates, and personalized application content.

last_name.description: Member's last name for complete user identification and family name tracking. Works with first name for formal communications and Todo sharing features when implemented.

status.description: Current account status for Todo app lifecycle management and access control. Active members can create and manage Todos, suspended members have restricted access, deactivated members cannot access Todo functionality.

created_at.description: Member profile creation timestamp in the TodoApp system. Records when the member initially registered and gained access to Todo management features for audit trail and compliance purposes.

updated_at.description: Last profile modification timestamp. Updates whenever member information changes to maintain accurate change history for Todo app administration and compliance monitoring.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp for account recovery. Null when account is active, contains deletion timestamp when account is soft deleted for recoverable account management.

actor_member_id.description: Member user who performed the audited action, if applicable. References todo_app_members when the action was performed by a regular member user.

actor_administrator_id.description: Administrator user who performed the audited action, if applicable. References todo_app_administrators when the action was performed by an administrative user.

target_member_id.description: Member user who is the subject of the audited action, if applicable. References todo_app_members when the action targets a specific member user.

target_todo_id.description: Todo item that is the subject of the audited action, if applicable. References todo_app_todos when the action involves a specific todo item.

action_type.description: Type of action that was performed. Valid values include: create_todo, update_todo, delete_todo, complete_todo, incomplete_todo, login, logout, register, update_profile, admin_create_user, admin_update_user, admin_delete_user, admin_view_user, system_config_update, system_maintenance, and other action types.

action_description.description: Detailed description of the action performed, providing context and specific information about what was done. This field contains human-readable explanation of the audit event for operational review and compliance purposes.

entity_type.description: Type of entity that was affected by the action. Valid values include: user, todo, session, system_config, and other entity types that can be audited.

entity_id.description: Unique identifier of the specific entity that was affected by the action. This references the primary key of the affected entity (todo, user, etc.) and is null for system-level actions that don't target specific entities.

old_values.description: Previous state of the entity before the action was performed, stored as JSON string. This captures the 'before' state for update actions to enable complete change tracking and rollback capabilities. Null for actions that don't modify state (create, delete, read operations).

new_values.description: New state of the entity after the action was performed, stored as JSON string. This captures the 'after' state for update actions and the complete state for create actions. Null for delete operations and read-only actions.

ip_address.description: IP address of the user who performed the action, used for security monitoring, location-based security analysis, and forensic investigations. This field supports both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

user_agent.description: User agent string from the client's browser or application, providing information about the client software, operating system, and device used for the action. This aids in security analysis and client compatibility monitoring.

session_id.description: Session identifier that was active when the action was performed, linking the audit log to the specific user session for comprehensive activity tracking and session-based analysis.

request_id.description: Unique request identifier for correlating related actions and requests across distributed system components, enabling request tracing and distributed transaction analysis.

severity_level.description: Severity level of the audit event for filtering and prioritization. Valid values include: info, warning, error, critical, and security. Used for operational monitoring and alert filtering.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the audit log entry was created, automatically set to current system time when the action occurs. This serves as the primary temporal reference for audit timeline analysis and compliance reporting.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the audit log entry was last modified, automatically updated when any field of the log entry is changed. This supports audit log integrity and change tracking requirements.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp for audit log entries that are marked for removal but preserved for compliance requirements. When populated, indicates that this audit log entry has been logically deleted but retained for legal and regulatory requirements.

ITodoAppAuditLog.description:
Comprehensive activity tracking system that records all user actions and system events for security, compliance, and operational monitoring purposes.

This table provides a complete audit trail of user interactions with the TodoApp system, including member and administrator actions on todos, user account activities, session management, and system-level events. Each audit log entry captures the actor, action performed, affected entities, and detailed context information to support forensic analysis and regulatory compliance requirements.

The audit logging system ensures transparency and accountability by tracking who performed what actions, when they occurred, and what data was affected. This enables security monitoring, user behavior analysis, compliance reporting, and incident investigation capabilities across the entire TodoApp ecosystem.

actor_member_id.description: Member user who performed the audited action, if applicable.

new_values.description: New state of the entity after the action was performed, stored as JSON string. Captures the 'after' state for change tracking and audit completeness.

severity_level.description: Severity level of the audit event for filtering and prioritization.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the audit log entry was created.

ITodoAppAuditLog.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and filtering parameters for audit log retrieval with advanced filtering options.

Provides comprehensive search capabilities for security monitoring, compliance reporting, and operational oversight. Supports filtering by multiple criteria including actor types, action types, severity levels, temporal ranges, entity relationships, and full-text search across descriptions.

Enables targeted security investigations, regulatory compliance analysis, and operational monitoring through flexible query parameters while maintaining audit trail integrity and proper access controls.

config_key.description: Unique configuration key that identifies the specific metadata entry. Keys follow a hierarchical naming convention using dots for organization (e.g., 'features.todo_sharing', 'limits.max_todos_per_user', 'ui.theme_default') and must be unique across the entire system.

config_value.description: Configuration value stored as string, which can represent various data types based on the configuration schema. Numeric values are stored as strings and parsed by applications, boolean values use 'true'/'false', and complex objects are stored as JSON strings.

config_type.description: Data type of the configuration value for validation and parsing. Valid values include: string, number, boolean, json, and url. This enables proper validation and type conversion by consuming applications.

category.description: Configuration category for organizational purposes and administrative grouping. Valid categories include: feature_flags, system_limits, ui_settings, security_settings, performance_settings, integration_settings, and operational_settings.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this configuration controls, its purpose, valid values, and impact on system behavior. This provides context for administrators and supports configuration management best practices.

is_active.description: Whether this configuration entry is currently active and being used by the system. Inactive configurations are preserved for reference but not applied to system behavior, enabling safe deprecation and rollback scenarios.

is_system_config.description: Whether this configuration is a system-level setting that affects all users and cannot be overridden by user-specific settings. System configurations take precedence over user-level settings and are typically managed by administrators only.

environment_scope.description: Deployment environment scope for this configuration. Valid values include: all, development, staging, production. Configurations with 'all' scope apply to all environments, while specific environment scopes apply only to those environments.

oneOf.description: Member user who created this configuration entry, if applicable. References the todo_app_members.id when the configuration was created by a member user (typically for user-level preferences).

created_by_member_id.description: Member user who created this configuration entry, if applicable. References the todo_app_members.id when the configuration was created by a member user (typically for user-level preferences).

created_by_administrator_id.description: Administrator user who created this configuration entry, if applicable. References the todo_app_administrators.id when the configuration was created by an administrative user.

oneOf.description: Default value for this configuration if not explicitly set, providing fallback behavior and ensuring system stability when specific configurations are not defined.

default_value.description: Default value for this configuration if not explicitly set, providing fallback behavior and ensuring system stability when specific configurations are not defined.

oneOf.description: Minimum allowed value for numeric configurations, providing lower bounds validation for system limits and thresholds. Null for non-numeric configurations.

min_value.description: Minimum allowed value for numeric configurations, providing lower bounds validation for system limits and thresholds. Null for non-numeric configurations.

oneOf.description: Maximum allowed value for numeric configurations, providing upper bounds validation for system limits and thresholds. Null for non-numeric configurations.

max_value.description: Maximum allowed value for numeric configurations, providing upper bounds validation for system limits and thresholds. Null for non-numeric configurations.

oneOf.description: JSON array string of allowed values for this configuration, providing enumeration validation for configurations with limited valid value sets. Null for configurations without value restrictions.

allowed_values.description: JSON array string of allowed values for this configuration, providing enumeration validation for configurations with limited valid value sets. Null for configurations without value restrictions.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was created, automatically set to current system time during initial configuration setup.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was last modified, automatically updated when any field of the configuration is changed.

ITodoAppSystemMetadata.description:
Application-wide configuration and operational metadata storage that provides centralized management of system settings, feature flags, operational parameters, and application-wide configuration values.

This table serves as the single source of truth for all TodoApp system configuration, enabling dynamic configuration management, feature toggles, operational settings, and application metadata without requiring code deployments. System administrators can modify configuration values through administrative interfaces while maintaining complete audit trails of all configuration changes.

The system metadata framework supports various configuration types including boolean feature flags for enabling/disabling functionality, numeric thresholds and limits, string configuration values for system parameters, JSON configuration objects for complex structured data, and version tracking for configuration schema evolution.

All configuration changes are fully audited through the audit logging system, ensuring complete traceability of who made configuration changes, when they occurred, and what the previous values were. This enables rollback capabilities, compliance reporting, and operational governance of the TodoApp system configuration.

ITodoAppSystemMetadata.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering, searching, and paginating system metadata configuration entries.

Provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for system administrators to locate specific configuration entries based on category, environment, activation status, data types, and configuration key patterns. Supports both exact matching and partial search capabilities for configuration keys.

The request parameters support pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting by various metadata fields including configuration key, category, creation date, last update, and priority. This enables efficient browsing of large configuration sets and targeted searching for specific settings.

Filtering options include configuration category (feature_flags, system_limits, ui_settings, etc.), environment scope (development, staging, production), active status, system-level designation, and data type filtering (string, number, boolean, json, url). The search functionality supports partial matching of configuration keys for discoverability.

Used for administrative dashboards, configuration management interfaces, system monitoring, and bulk configuration operations where administrators need to locate and analyze system settings efficiently.

page.description: Page number for pagination, starting from 1. Used in combination with limit to navigate through large result sets. Each page contains up to 'limit' configuration entries. Default value is 1 for first page.

limit.description: Number of configuration entries to return per page. Controls the page size for pagination and performance optimization. Maximum limit is 100 entries per page to prevent excessive data transfer. Default value is 20 entries per page.

search.description: Partial search string for configuration key matching. Performs case-insensitive substring matching on configuration keys to help discover related settings. Supports searching by key segments (e.g., searching 'todo' finds 'features.todo_sharing' and 'limits.max_todos'). Useful for finding configurations when exact key names are not known.

category.description: Filter by configuration category. Supported values include 'feature_flags', 'system_limits', 'ui_settings', 'security_settings', 'performance_settings', 'integration_settings', and 'operational_settings'. Returns only configurations belonging to the specified category.

environment.description: Filter by environment scope. Supported values include 'development', 'staging', 'production', and 'all'. Returns configurations that match the specified environment scope, helping administrators focus on environment-specific settings.

is_active.description: Filter by activation status. When true, returns only active configuration entries; when false, returns only inactive entries. Allows administrators to focus on currently used configurations or review disabled settings for potential reactivation.

data_type.description: Filter by configuration data type. Supported values include 'string', 'number', 'boolean', 'json', and 'url'. Returns configurations that match the specified data type, helping administrators locate specific types of settings.

is_system_level.description: Filter by system-level designation. When true, returns only system-level configurations that affect all users; when false, returns only user-level configurations. Helps administrators distinguish between global and user-specific settings.

order_by.description: Sort order for results. Supported values include 'config_key', 'category', 'created_at', 'updated_at', and 'priority'. Determines the field used for sorting the returned configuration entries. Default sorting is by configuration key in ascending order.

oneOf.description: Sort direction for ordering results. Supported values are 'asc' for ascending order and 'desc' for descending order. Controls whether sorting is performed in forward or reverse order. Default direction is ascending order.

Sort direction for ordering results. Supported values are 'asc' for ascending order and 'desc' for descending order. Controls whether sorting is performed in forward or reverse order. Default direction is ascending order.

order_direction.description: Sort direction for ordering results. Supported values are 'asc' for ascending order and 'desc' for descending order. Controls whether sorting is performed in forward or reverse order. Default direction is ascending order.

ITodoAppSystemMetadata.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating existing system metadata configuration entries.

Allows modification of configuration values, types, categories, and operational properties while maintaining system integrity and audit trails. This DTO enables administrators to update system settings, feature flags, operational parameters, and application-wide configuration without requiring code deployments.

The update operation supports various configuration types including boolean feature flags for enabling/disabling functionality, numeric thresholds and limits, string configuration values for system parameters, JSON configuration objects for complex structured data, and version tracking for configuration schema evolution.

All configuration changes are validated against stored validation schemas when present, ensuring configuration integrity before applying modifications. System-level configurations that affect all users and environment-specific settings can be managed through this update interface while maintaining proper security controls and administrative oversight.

config_value.description: Updated configuration value stored as string. Can represent various data types based on the configuration schema. Numeric values stored as strings, boolean values use 'true'/'false', and complex objects stored as JSON strings. Supports both single and multiple value configurations.

config_type.description: Updated data type of the configuration value for validation and parsing. Valid values include: string, number, boolean, json, and url. Changing this type requires updating associated validation schemas and default values accordingly.

category.description: Updated configuration category for organizational purposes and administrative grouping. Valid categories include: feature_flags, system_limits, ui_settings, security_settings, performance_settings, integration_settings, and operational_settings. Category changes affect administrative interfaces and configuration management workflows.

description.description: Updated human-readable description of what this configuration controls, its purpose, valid values, and impact on system behavior. Provides context for administrators and supports configuration management best practices with enhanced documentation.

is_active.description: Updated activation status for this configuration entry. When set to false, the configuration is preserved for reference but not applied to system behavior, enabling safe deprecation and rollback scenarios without data loss.

is_system_config.description: Updated system-level configuration flag indicating whether this setting affects all users and cannot be overridden by user-specific settings. System configurations take precedence over user-level settings and are typically managed by administrators only.

environment_scope.description: Updated deployment environment scope for this configuration. Valid values include: all, development, staging, production. Changes to environment scope affect which deployments the configuration applies to and require careful coordination across environments.

validation_schema.description: Updated JSON schema string that defines validation rules for this configuration value. Enables runtime validation of configuration changes and ensures configuration integrity before application. Null removes validation constraints.

default_value.description: Updated default value for this configuration if not explicitly set. Provides fallback behavior and ensures system stability when specific configurations are not defined. Must align with config_type and validation_schema if specified.

min_value.description: Updated minimum allowed value for numeric configurations. Provides lower bounds validation for system limits and thresholds. Null for non-numeric configurations or when no minimum constraint is needed.

max_value.description: Updated maximum allowed value for numeric configurations. Provides upper bounds validation for system limits and thresholds. Null for non-numeric configurations or when no maximum constraint is needed.

allowed_values.description: Updated JSON array string of allowed values for this configuration. Provides enumeration validation for configurations with limited valid value sets. Null for configurations without value restrictions, enabling full range of values for the specified type.

config_key.description: Unique configuration key that identifies the specific metadata entry. Keys follow a hierarchical naming convention using dots for organization (e.g., 'features.todo_sharing', 'limits.max_todos_per_user', 'ui.theme_default') and must be unique across the entire system.

environment_scope.description: Deployment environment scope for this configuration. Valid values include: all, development, staging, production. Configurations with 'all' scope apply to all environments, while specific environment scopes apply only to those environments.

created_by_member_id.description: Member user who created this configuration entry, if applicable. References todo_app_members.id when the configuration was created by a member user (typically for user-level preferences).

created_by_administrator_id.description: Administrator user who created this configuration entry, if applicable. References todo_app_administrators.id when the configuration was created by an administrative user.

ITodoAppSystemMetadata.ISummary.description:
Summary view of system metadata for list display and administrative management.

Provides essential configuration information optimized for display in metadata management interfaces, configuration overviews, and administrative dashboards. This summary variant includes key identification fields, current status indicators, operational metadata, and full traceability information while maintaining the core field structure for efficient list rendering.

ITodoAppAdministrator.IAuthorized.description:
Authenticated administrator information with JWT access tokens and session credentials for secure system management access.

Contains the administrator's unique identifier and authentication tokens for privileged system operations in the TodoApp administrative interface. This response type provides both the administrator ID for subsequent API operations and JWT tokens for maintaining authenticated session state throughout administrative actions.

The response includes comprehensive authorization token information with access and refresh token details, expiration timestamps, and role-based permissions. This enables secure privileged system access while maintaining proper session management and audit protocols for all administrative operations.
